yRmdNlDhJS.one_liner: Symbolic Lean 4 pipeline recording verified proof edits, used to study what models learn from search-generated supervision.
yRmdNlDhJS.problem: Verification shows a proof edit is correct but not that its training signal is free of search artifacts such as ordering shortcuts and rewards for trivial deletions.
yRmdNlDhJS.method: LeanPolish releases 33,402 accepted local edits and 65,596 same-state failed attempts, then trains rankers and editors on them, evaluating complete candidate menus beyond the first success to remove the ordering shortcut and iterating the symbolic pass for compression.
yRmdNlDhJS.key_idea: Record every verified edit with same-state failures and score complete candidate menus beyond first success, exposing selection effects like ordering shortcuts in search-generated supervision.
yRmdNlDhJS.evidence: Lean 4 proof-compression experiments on miniF2F, PutnamBench, and AxiomProver, with frozen-baseline and frozen-editor controls and fine-tuning of DeepSeek-Prover on LeanPolish pairs.
yRmdNlDhJS.claimed_gains: A trained ranker selects the best candidate on 70.1% of held-out states versus 36.9% for the strongest frozen baseline, iterating the symbolic pass raises miniF2F savings from 19.7% to 27.5%, and fine-tuned DeepSeek-Prover shortens 58% of 351 miniF2F proofs instead of 12% and saves 8.6% of tokens.
yRmdNlDhJS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controls (first-success ranking reaching 100% from menu order alone, a deletion rule reproducing reference edits) expose shortcuts in search-generated supervision and that the released dataset supports controlled study.
yRmdNlDhJS.main_concern: Learned editing adds little practical value: frozen editors match or exceed trained ones under matched hybrid loops, and the extra PutnamBench and AxiomProver savings lack a matched frozen-editor control.

kNE7WNxuZK.one_liner: Transformer variant splitting the residual stream into orthogonal Data and Type subspaces, with Type-based attention and gating controlling Data transformations.
kNE7WNxuZK.problem: It is unclear whether transformers on symbolic tasks learn generalizable rules or statistical shortcuts, and standard transformers struggle to learn logic rules from limited data.
kNE7WNxuZK.method: STRAT (Stratified Registers And Types) partitions the residual stream into orthogonal Data and Type subspaces and uses Type-based attention and gating to govern Data transformations. The paper pairs it with controlled arithmetic ablations, a factorial ablation, and mechanistic analysis.
kNE7WNxuZK.key_idea: Make the separation of values from the types that control their manipulation an architectural primitive via orthogonal Data/Type subspaces and Type-driven attention and gating.
kNE7WNxuZK.evidence: Controlled arithmetic ablations, a factorial ablation, mechanistic analysis, and 11 datasets spanning 10 tasks, with both models trained from 10 base examples per dataset using identical task-specific augmentation.
kNE7WNxuZK.claimed_gains: Reduces median out-of-distribution arithmetic error 35-fold relative to a Transformer baseline, outperforms it by 26 percentage points on average across 11 datasets spanning 10 tasks, and under distribution shift STRAT's mean accuracy drops by only 2.39 percentage points.
kNE7WNxuZK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the out-of-distribution improvements are large and that the controlled analysis of why small transformers fail, followed by architecture changes motivated by it, is clear and well written.
kNE7WNxuZK.main_concern: The experiments use predefined hand-crafted value and type encodings rather than learned ones, and the proposed failure mechanisms (Linear Trap, Gradient Wall, Open Gate Trap) are suggestive interpretations without causal validation.

dyRAZ3n57Z.one_liner: Vertical sliced Wasserstein compares distributions of distributions by projecting inner measures with test functions and using 1D Wasserstein.
dyRAZ3n57Z.problem: Optimal transport distances on the space of meta-measures (distributions over distributions) are prohibitively expensive to evaluate.
dyRAZ3n57Z.method: VSW projects each inner measure using continuous test functions and compares the resulting one-dimensional distributions with the 1D Wasserstein distance, and the authors derive a particle gradient for the empirical VSW_2^2 objective to transport meta-measures.
dyRAZ3n57Z.key_idea: Replace transport-geometry slicing of the inner measure space with expected projections onto continuous test functions, which reduces comparison to 1D Wasserstein distances.
dyRAZ3n57Z.evidence: Proofs that VSW is a metric, metrizes weak convergence and has dimension-independent statistical convergence guarantees, plus experiments comparing accuracy and efficiency with existing meta-measure distances and a gradient-based transport demonstration.
dyRAZ3n57Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation is new, simple and theoretically well grounded, with runtime advantages over other meta-measure distances and a well-behaved sample complexity.
dyRAZ3n57Z.main_concern: There are no theoretical bounds relating VSW to the Wasserstein-over-Wasserstein distance it approximates, and performance and assumptions depend on the test-function kernel, which is under-illustrated.

EBhtPdtKOL.one_liner: Primal-dual algorithm with adaptive FTRL and an exponential Lyapunov function achieving sqrt(K) regret and constraint violation in adversarial linear CMDPs.
EBhtPdtKOL.problem: The best prior algorithm for adversarial linear CMDPs has K^{3/4} regret and constraint violation, leaving a gap to the optimal sqrt(K) dependence on the number of episodes K.
EBhtPdtKOL.method: A primal-dual algorithm combining adaptive FTRL, contracted value estimation and an exponential Lyapunov function, extended to the same guarantees for hard constraint violation, without Slater's condition.
EBhtPdtKOL.key_idea: An adaptive dual regularizer offsets dual-weight dependence in the primal regret bound, removing policy mixing that would enlarge the value-function class covering number.
EBhtPdtKOL.evidence: Theoretical regret and constraint-violation bounds for episodic adversarial linear CMDPs with unknown transitions; no experiments are mentioned in the visible text.
EBhtPdtKOL.claimed_gains: Achieves O~(sqrt(K)) regret and cumulative constraint violation without Slater's condition, improving the previous O~(K^{3/4}), and the same O~(sqrt(K)) for regret and hard constraint violation.
EBhtPdtKOL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the result closes a real gap in CMDP theory and that the paper is clearly presented.
EBhtPdtKOL.main_concern: Technical novelty is unclear (standard FTRL techniques and proof steps), and the full-information feedback assumed is stronger than the bandit feedback in prior work.

JYMIxuG7ph.one_liner: CGIB-RCL clusters multi-modal data using sample-adaptive cross-modal information bottleneck guidance and reliability-weighted contrastive negatives.
JYMIxuG7ph.problem: Existing information-bottleneck multi-modal clustering ignores per-sample modality contributions, and contrastive methods treat negative pairs alike despite ambiguous relations and unreliable samples.
JYMIxuG7ph.method: Cross-Guided Information Bottleneck (CGIB) builds per-sample guidance for each target modality by adaptively combining the remaining modalities, and Reliable Contrastive Learning (RCL) separately models relation ambiguity and sample reliability to weight each negative pair.
JYMIxuG7ph.key_idea: Guide each modality's bottleneck with an adaptive per-sample combination of the other modalities, and down-weight negative pairs that are ambiguous or involve unreliable samples.
JYMIxuG7ph.evidence: Experiments on five datasets reporting ACC and NMI, with parameter sensitivity, training convergence, learned-representation and mechanism analyses (the abstract is truncated).
JYMIxuG7ph.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is well motivated, CGIB and RCL address complementary issues, and the method reports the best ACC and NMI on all five evaluated datasets.
JYMIxuG7ph.main_concern: Closely related methods (PTIB, STCMC-UR) are not directly compared, and it is unclear that the bottleneck regularizer preserves cross-modal information without discarding discriminative modality-specific content.

ijKTLDpoKI.one_liner: RAP compresses hyperbolic embeddings by keeping the radial coordinate and randomly projecting only the angular direction.
ijKTLDpoKI.problem: Hyperbolic representations lack an oblivious random-projection primitive like Johnson-Lindenstrauss, since tangent-space schemes are chart-bound with curvature penalties and hyperboloid projections mix radial and angular error.
ijKTLDpoKI.method: Preserves the radial coordinate exactly, applies a Euclidean random projection to the angular direction, and lifts the result back to the target hyperboloid at the cost of one Gaussian matrix-vector product. It proves a finite-set guarantee with sinh-based conditioning plus a local tangent-space JL theorem.
ijKTLDpoKI.key_idea: Splitting a hyperboloid point into radius and angle lets a Euclidean Johnson-Lindenstrauss projection act only on the angle, avoiding arcosh conditioning from mixed radial-angular error.
ijKTLDpoKI.evidence: A finite-set theoretical guarantee and a local tangent-space JL theorem, with experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks against non-data-driven baselines.
ijKTLDpoKI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the radial-angular decoupling is elegant, the theory is sound and clearly linked to the method, and experiments on synthetic and real benchmarks show improvements over non-data-driven baselines.
ijKTLDpoKI.main_concern: Prior hyperbolic dimension-reduction work (Benjamini and Makarychev, 2009), whose bounds may be at least as strong, is not cited or compared, and the guarantees carry assumptions that weaken the JL analogy.

nrpbe5hr2x.one_liner: Frames ultrasound examination as a POMDP and benchmarks LLM agents on acquiring evidence, stopping, and reporting conclusions.
nrpbe5hr2x.problem: Ultrasound AI work has largely overlooked the sequential decision loop in which a sonographer decides where to scan next and stops once the evidence is sufficient.
nrpbe5hr2x.method: Ultrasound examination is formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process in which diagnostic evidence is revealed only when the matching acquisition action is taken. SonoArena is an interactive benchmark where agents sequentially acquire evidence and decide what to report, with a theoretical characterization of operating regimes for different policy types.
nrpbe5hr2x.key_idea: Reveal diagnostic evidence only when an acquisition action is taken, so agents are scored on acquisition decisions and conclusions rather than on interpreting given observations.
nrpbe5hr2x.evidence: 24 LLM-based policy configurations spanning general-purpose and task-trained policies, plus programmatic baselines, in a simulator with textual observations.
nrpbe5hr2x.claimed_gains: The strongest task-trained policy outperforms the evaluated baselines overall but remains below the reference; no numbers stated.
nrpbe5hr2x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the move beyond static medical imaging evaluation valuable, with theoretical analysis and diverse policy types yielding useful negative findings.
nrpbe5hr2x.main_concern: The benchmark uses simulated textual observations rather than real ultrasound images, with fully synthetic emergency cases and a manually specified utility matrix, so real-world applicability is unclear.

YHqiLhTols.one_liner: Applies drifting to sequences of continuous token representations to learn a one-pass map from Gaussian noise to text.
YHqiLhTols.problem: Diffusion language models generate tokens in parallel but still need multiple sampling steps to reach high-quality text.
YHqiLhTols.method: Seq-Drifting builds a drift field over continuous token representations whose position-wise targets adapt to the current generated context: attraction pulls each output toward contextually plausible token representations, while repulsion discourages collapse across samples and repetition within sequences. The generator learns from this field and produces all tokens jointly in one pass.
YHqiLhTols.key_idea: Replace per-position ground-truth token supervision with a context-dependent drift field of attraction toward plausible token representations and repulsion against collapse and repetition.
YHqiLhTols.evidence: LM1B and OpenWebText generation, unconditional and conditional, plus translation, summarization and reasoning, with GPT-2 as the support model according to reviewers.
YHqiLhTols.claimed_gains: Achieves a generative perplexity of 36.01 on LM1B in one step and performs competitively in unconditional and conditional generation.
YHqiLhTols.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find adapting drifting models to language a promising direction for one-step generation, with well-motivated design choices such as sphere geometry and context-dependent support tokens, and competitive quality at much lower inference cost.
YHqiLhTols.main_concern: Performance may depend heavily on the frozen autoregressive support model (LM1B Gen-PPL moves from 93.81 to 36.01 with pretrained GPT-2), with no simple one-step distillation baseline and weaker conditional and OpenWebText results.

x6pWVkCBF8.one_liner: Heterogeneous collaborative perception through grounded text messages with Fourier numerical embeddings and position-aware text-to-feature fusion.
x6pWVkCBF8.problem: Heterogeneous agents limit the scalability of collaborative perception, and existing approaches need encoder retraining, feature interpretation, or protocol adaptation to align representations.
x6pWVkCBF8.method: Agents exchange grounded text of positional, geometric, and semantic key-value pairs with numerical attributes, encoded by a lightweight text encoder with Fourier numerical embeddings and sub-sentence attention. A position-aware text-to-feature enhancer injects the text into spatially relevant local features, and each agent is pre-trained independently on perceived and synthetic grounded text plus annotation-derived pseudo-labels.
x6pWVkCBF8.key_idea: Use structured grounded text as a shared interface so independently pre-trained agents can collaborate without feature alignment or joint post-training.
x6pWVkCBF8.evidence: Simulated and real-world experiments, with ablations on numerical encoding, synthetic cross-task text, and dropped or permuted key-value pairs (per reviews).
x6pWVkCBF8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically relevant and that letting heterogeneous detection and segmentation agents collaborate without dense feature exchange or joint training is attractive.
x6pWVkCBF8.main_concern: It is unclear why text is needed over simpler structured object encodings, since baselines such as a per-box MLP or set encoder and adapted feature- or codebook-based interfaces are missing and latency overhead is unaddressed.

bITW1JwxpG.one_liner: XOR-Trellis pairs a hardware-light XOR-based trellis dequantizer with a curvature-aware Viterbi objective for Hadamard-free ultra-low-bit LLM quantization.
bITW1JwxpG.problem: Trellis-coded LLM weight quantization needs high-throughput dequantization to avoid an inference bottleneck and usually relies on costly incoherence transformations to keep accuracy.
bITW1JwxpG.method: A structured, hardware-efficient state-to-value mapping (palettes with XOR masks) gives an ultra-low-complexity trellis dequantizer while keeping diverse reconstruction choices, and trellis path optimization is reformulated with a curvature-aware objective in the original coordinate space.
bITW1JwxpG.key_idea: Map trellis states to values via a structured XOR palette decoder, and weight the path search by curvature (D-weighting) so Hadamard incoherence processing is unnecessary.
bITW1JwxpG.evidence: Experiments on Llama-3.1 models against QTIP and YAQA at ultra-low bit widths, a gate-level hardware analysis, and cross-family results in the appendix (details from reviews).
bITW1JwxpG.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract describes high-quality ultra-low-bit quantization with cheap parallel reconstruction and no Hadamard processing, but gives no numbers.
bITW1JwxpG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the XOR trellis simple, hardware-friendly and well justified, with D-weighting nearly free and good results without a Hadamard transform.
bITW1JwxpG.main_concern: Baseline comparisons are questioned: XOR-Trellis uses a finer scaling scheme (one E5M3 scale per 32 elements versus channel-wise scales, roughly a 0.25-bit advantage), its baseline numbers differ from published QTIP results, and no measured throughput speedup is shown.

DaxTQCSuCf.one_liner: PrivacyAlign supplies human-annotated privacy judgments and annotation-conditioned reward modeling to align LLM agents with contextual privacy norms via RL.
DaxTQCSuCf.problem: Existing agent privacy training and evaluation rely on unreliable proxies rather than human judgments of what is appropriate to share in context.
DaxTQCSuCf.method: The authors collect 1,350 samples with 3,516 annotations from 599 annotators, condition LLM judges on human annotations and explanations for reference responses, and introduce annotation-conditioned reward modeling that scores new responses during RL of small open-weight agents.
DaxTQCSuCf.key_idea: Score new responses during RL with a reward model conditioned on human annotations and explanations for reference responses to the same prompt.
DaxTQCSuCf.evidence: The PrivacyAlign dataset, judge-reliability tests, and RL training of small open-weight agents evaluated on PrivacyAlign and existing benchmarks (details truncated).
DaxTQCSuCf.claimed_gains: Reports strong gains on PrivacyAlign and existing benchmarks for small open-weight agents trained with the reward; no gain numbers are visible in the truncated abstract.
DaxTQCSuCf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the human-annotated dataset with pairwise preferences, leak/omit labels and rationales, and see annotation-conditioned reward modeling as a promising way to use human judgments in RL.
DaxTQCSuCf.main_concern: Novelty relative to existing human-annotated privacy datasets (for example CIDER) may be overstated, and annotator agreement is moderate (preference kappa 0.61, leak 0.56, omission 0.12) with no analysis of the disagreements.

7oXfx7L8Zw.one_liner: Rotation-equivariant spin-2 polarimetric encoder feeds orientation-independent features into a frozen geometry backbone for metric depth.
7oXfx7L8Zw.problem: Monocular metric depth is scale-ambiguous, and the angle of polarization is measured relative to an arbitrary sensor reference axis, so encoders that ignore this depend on the manufacturer's axis choice (spin-2 angle ambiguity).
7oXfx7L8Zw.method: POLARIS builds a rotation-equivariant polarimetric encoder and injects its orientation-independent features into a largely frozen geometry backbone through a prior-preserving interface. Reviews describe a circular-harmonic convolution with magnitude readout and about 1.07M extra parameters.
7oXfx7L8Zw.key_idea: Treat the angle of linear polarization as a spin-2 field and encode it with equivariant circular-harmonic convolutions so features are invariant to analyser-axis rotation.
7oXfx7L8Zw.evidence: Tested on HAMMER against MoGe-2 fine-tuned on the same data and the same weights without polarization, on unseen HouseCat6D, and under arbitrary analyser-axis rotation of the input.
7oXfx7L8Zw.claimed_gains: Lowers metric AbsRel by 16% over MoGe-2 fine-tuned on the same data and by 11% over the same weights without polarization on HAMMER, with the lowest metric error on HouseCat6D.
7oXfx7L8Zw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the spin-2 treatment of polarization angle physically grounded and principled, with a cheap add-on branch that falls back exactly to RGB-only input.
7oXfx7L8Zw.main_concern: The gain appears to come largely from correcting global scale without analysis of how polarization reaches the scale estimate, and gains outside HAMMER and against other baselines such as PPFT are limited or unclear.

7CCTaMlmaj.one_liner: Privately learns a low-dimensional linear model to choose public-dataset pretraining mixtures before DP finetuning.
7CCTaMlmaj.problem: DP finetuning after public pretraining depends on how relevant the public data is to the sensitive task, and no pipeline privately chooses the mixture of several public datasets.
7CCTaMlmaj.method: The method privately fits a low-dimensional linear model (a k-dimensional convex problem over frozen public proxies) to find mixture weights, then pretrains on that mixture before DP finetuning. Reviews note a disjoint private split is used for mixture selection so parallel composition avoids extra privacy budget.
7CCTaMlmaj.key_idea: Learn mixture weights over public datasets by privately fitting a low-dimensional linear model on frozen public proxies, using a disjoint private split to avoid epsilon composition.
7CCTaMlmaj.evidence: NIH ChestX-ray14 X-ray classification and ENRON email language modeling with The Common Pile, under sample-level and user-level DP, against uniform and random-search baselines.
7CCTaMlmaj.claimed_gains: Improves macro AUC by up to 0.037 across privacy budgets, with +22.8% relative AUC on Cardiomegaly at epsilon=1, and lowers ENRON test perplexity by 16% relative to baseline mixtures.
7CCTaMlmaj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is simple, the DP accounting is sound, and the utility gains on real medical data are large against well-chosen uniform and random-search baselines.
7CCTaMlmaj.main_concern: Limited novelty and weak vision baselines (a regressed label-average pretraining target, no standard multi-label or matched-label source) may inflate gains, and the method needs extra private data and a non-private hyperparameter search.

nH30NJqLzs.one_liner: Two-stage structural-functional graph fusion with homogeneity and boundary losses for deep multi-modal clustering of infant cortical parcellation.
nH30NJqLzs.problem: Infant data are noisy and high-dimensional, and existing unsupervised objectives do not meet group-level parcellation needs such as cross-subject adaptability, anatomical consistency, and spatial continuity.
nH30NJqLzs.method: SABER fuses structural and functional data in two stages, multi-layer graph mutual learning and vertex-level modality weighting. It adds a Dynamic Spatial-Weighted Generalized Homogeneity Loss and a boundary-aware loss that makes parcellation sensitive to local biological boundaries.
nH30NJqLzs.key_idea: Optimize group parcellation homogeneity over individual-level features with dynamic spatial weighting and align predicted boundaries with probabilistic boundary priors, after graph-mutual-learning fusion of modalities.
nH30NJqLzs.evidence: Reviews cite a subject-disjoint split of 148 training and 33 test infants, ablations, spatial null controls, multiple resolutions, downstream prediction, and transfer of the losses to other networks.
nH30NJqLzs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two tailored losses are well motivated by practical parcellation needs, the evaluation with ablations is fairly comprehensive, and the losses transfer to other clustering networks.
nH30NJqLzs.main_concern: Generalization evidence is thin (33 test infants, longitudinal identification includes atlas-training subjects), the source of boundary supervision is unclear, and the reported Hausdorff metric is actually a one-sided average distance.

ZXvQ3FOvhr.one_liner: Perturbation-sensitivity-guided edge pruning plus proxy-model self-distillation for test-time graph anomaly detection under normality shift.
ZXvQ3FOvhr.problem: Previously unseen but normal patterns that appear at deployment degrade graph anomaly detectors, and existing test-time adaptation suffers from heterogeneous semantic pattern conflicts and biased predictions.
ZXvQ3FOvhr.method: Given a pretrained detector, PUPPY estimates each node's sensitivity to graph perturbations to guide selective edge pruning of the test graph, and uses a self-distillation framework with a proxy model to correct prediction bias. Reviews add that the teacher is initialized with anchor normals chosen by smallest source anomaly margin.
ZXvQ3FOvhr.key_idea: Prune edges guided by node sensitivity to perturbations to suppress structural contamination, while proxy-rectified teacher-student self-distillation corrects biased predictions under normality shift.
ZXvQ3FOvhr.evidence: The visible abstract does not describe experiments; reviewers cite an ablation (Table 2) confirming each component and a complete code repository.
ZXvQ3FOvhr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing normality shift into structural contamination and prediction bias is a clear, well-motivated framing with a dedicated mechanism for each and supporting ablations.
ZXvQ3FOvhr.main_concern: There is no analysis of proxy-label quality or stability (a possible positive feedback loop), and the perturbation-consistency and source-anchor assumptions are unvalidated under severe shift.

m3CQsWsbtX.one_liner: Full-stack agentic recipe: multimodal evidence harness, synthesized trajectories, benchmark, and SFT plus RL for agent policy and image backend.
m3CQsWsbtX.problem: Image generation and editing models are unreliable when prompts need external world knowledge, and existing agentic methods have insufficient visual verification, overloaded policy models, and weak integration of retrieved text and images.
m3CQsWsbtX.method: WeAgent-Harness is a multimodal runtime with persistent evidence management and verification and integration tools that organize retrieved evidence into a dense carrier. On top of it the authors build a prompt-synthesis and trajectory pipeline (23K supervised trajectories, 14.7K RL tasks with three-layer checklists), the bilingual WeBench-MMGenEdit benchmark, and a two-sided SFT and RL recipe for the agent policy and image backend.
m3CQsWsbtX.key_idea: Organize retrieved multimodal evidence into a dense carrier with dedicated verification tools, then post-train both the agent policy and the image backend with SFT and checklist-verified RL.
m3CQsWsbtX.evidence: WeBench-MMGenEdit for knowledge-intensive generation and multi-image editing, plus KnowGen and Mind-Bench, with component ablations and a three-level evaluation of process, generation input, and final image per reviews.
m3CQsWsbtX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a practical, well-motivated engineering contribution with evidence carriers, a useful three-level diagnostic evaluation, and ablations plus results on other benchmarks.
m3CQsWsbtX.main_concern: Gains may be confounded by backend fine-tuning (33.54 vs 32.63 W Avg under the same Qwen-Image backend), the advance over existing harnesses and inference cost are unclear, and automatic evaluation is not validated.

2lFqeLZcwb.one_liner: Language-model-free cross-domain graph vectorization using global relational graphs, spectral embeddings, and aligned orthogonal transformations.
2lFqeLZcwb.problem: Graph datasets differ in topology, attribute semantics, feature dimensions, and attribute availability, which makes transferable graph-level representations across domains hard to learn.
2lFqeLZcwb.method: GraphVec builds multi-scale global relational graphs and spectral embeddings to replace raw attributes with comparable relational features, aligns dataset-level means through orthogonal transformations optimized by a density-maximization algorithm, and uses a GIN-Graph Transformer backbone with hierarchical reference distribution encoding. A generalization bound links cross-domain contrastive pretraining to few-shot classification.
2lFqeLZcwb.key_idea: Replace incomparable raw node attributes with spectral features of multi-scale global relational graphs aligned across datasets by orthogonal transformations, then encode node distributions hierarchically.
2lFqeLZcwb.evidence: 13 datasets against more than 15 baselines on cross-domain few-shot graph classification, graph clustering, and few-shot node classification; a reviewer cites an average of 66.14 vs 58.63 for GCN.
2lFqeLZcwb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the handling of heterogeneous attributes is well motivated and the paper reports large transfer gains supported by ablations, sensitivity studies, and resource measurements.
2lFqeLZcwb.main_concern: Pretraining is not isolated from input-feature effects (Letter-med moves from 55.33 to 85.60 from features alone), gains are uneven across datasets, and the benchmark is cross-dataset rather than cross-domain.

qw8TdVXsvc.one_liner: Estimates time-varying generalized linear bandit parameters with discounted online mirror descent at constant per-round computation and memory.
qw8TdVXsvc.problem: Existing nonstationary GLB methods based on maximum-likelihood estimation with sliding windows, restarts, or discounting revisit past observations every round, so computation and memory grow with time, and several need a non-convex projection.
qw8TdVXsvc.method: DOMD-GLB estimates the parameter with discounted online mirror descent, using O(1) computation and memory per round, and is analyzed for dynamic regret in drifting and piecewise-stationary environments.
qw8TdVXsvc.key_idea: Replace repeated discounted MLE with one-pass discounted online mirror descent updates, so the estimator needs no stored history and no non-convex projection.
qw8TdVXsvc.evidence: Dynamic regret bounds for drifting and piecewise-stationary environments, plus experiments on synthetic logistic bandits (d=5 per a review) with smooth drift and abrupt parameter changes.
qw8TdVXsvc.claimed_gains: Dynamic regret with leading terms O-tilde(d^{3/4} P_T^{1/4} T^{3/4}) in drifting environments and O-tilde(d^{2/3} Gamma_T^{1/3} T^{2/3}) in piecewise-stationary environments, at O(1) computation and memory per round.
qw8TdVXsvc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the constant-cost, one-pass estimator without a non-convex projection is a practical advantage for long-running online use, with a clear analysis and competitive regret guarantees.
qw8TdVXsvc.main_concern: The best regret guarantees require oracle tuning of the discount factor from the unknown path length or number of changes, and experiments are limited to low-dimensional synthetic logistic problems.

TmpqenYxDb.one_liner: Trains LLMs to produce deductive proofs by supervised fine-tuning on A* execution traces and RL with A*-informed rewards.
TmpqenYxDb.problem: LLMs doing deductive reasoning often produce incorrect or redundant inference steps, and a correct solution needs a valid proof rather than just a correct final answer.
TmpqenYxDb.method: They frame natural language inference as search in a hypergraph and train with guidance from A* forward chaining, using supervised fine-tuning on A* execution traces and reinforcement learning with A*-informed reward models.
TmpqenYxDb.key_idea: Teach proof search by imitating A* traces and rewarding proofs with A*-derived signals that trade off correctness against search efficiency.
TmpqenYxDb.evidence: Llama-3.2 models in the 1B-3B range trained with SFT and RL and compared with DeepSeek-V3.2, with analyses of the accuracy-efficiency trade-off and of larger search spaces.
TmpqenYxDb.claimed_gains: Llama-3.2 models in the 1B-3B range go from near-zero accuracy to outperforming DeepSeek-V3.2; exact accuracy figures are not stated.
TmpqenYxDb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the background is clearly presented, the method rewards valid proofs rather than only final answers, and the reported performance gains are substantial.
TmpqenYxDb.main_concern: Efficiency is computed only on solved problems, which confounds comparisons, and novelty is limited because the approach combines existing A*, SFT, and RL on synthetic logic-programming data.

QFIRgU2Gex.one_liner: Forward-only coreset selection scoring candidates by token-level residual flows matched one-to-one to target-task prototypes.
QFIRgU2Gex.problem: Last-layer-state coreset selection misses information because samples with similar last-layer states can have different intermediate token updates (last-layer similarity collapse).
QFIRgU2Gex.method: BiTFlow summarizes target-task residual flows (per-token residual updates between selected layers) into token-level prototypes, aligns candidate tokens to them via one-to-one bipartite matching, and scores each sample by match quality and by how many distinct target token IDs it covers.
QFIRgU2Gex.key_idea: Compare residual updates between layers rather than last-layer states, and score samples by one-to-one token matching balanced with target token coverage.
QFIRgU2Gex.evidence: Instruction-tuning selection at a 5% budget on the LESS (0.27M samples) and SmolTalk (1.04M samples) pools, with transfer across model scales and families.
QFIRgU2Gex.claimed_gains: At a 5% selection budget on the LESS and SmolTalk pools it reaches the highest average performance and exceeds full-data fine-tuning on multiple benchmarks; exact scores are not stated.
QFIRgU2Gex.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is coherent and computationally efficient, with detailed ablations, broad benchmark coverage, and selections that transfer to other models at a strict 5% budget.
QFIRgU2Gex.main_concern: The benefit of residual-flow encoding over ordinary multi-layer states is not clearly established (Table 4a and probe results), and the average gains lack significance tests.

Z046iwD4c6.one_liner: Trains a Gaussian posterior over solver parameters for multi-sample coverage using one posterior draw per update via Fenchel-Bregman reweighting.
Z046iwD4c6.problem: Minimizing average single-attempt loss does not directly optimize candidate coverage, and direct Monte Carlo optimization of the finite-K objective needs K posterior draws per update.
Z046iwD4c6.method: An exact Fenchel reformulation separates problem-specific weights from the posterior update, a closed-form Bregman update tracks those weights with an exponential running average of observed failures, and the method is instantiated with the IVON variational optimizer as FBI.
Z046iwD4c6.key_idea: Track per-problem failure weights with an exponential running average from a Fenchel reformulation, so one posterior draw per update optimizes the finite-K coverage objective.
Z046iwD4c6.evidence: Recursive and autoregressive reasoning tasks (Maze-Hard, Sudoku, and MATH per the reviews) with a matched comparison against a direct Monte Carlo baseline.
Z046iwD4c6.claimed_gains: Comparable Pass@10 while using only 6.8% of the direct Monte Carlo baseline's measured training time per update.
Z046iwD4c6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that optimizing finite-K candidate coverage is a meaningful objective, the Fenchel-Bregman derivation is clear, and the matched comparison shows comparable coverage at much lower update cost.
Z046iwD4c6.main_concern: Gains are small and lack uncertainty estimates (a single seed for the language-model result), and it is unclear whether the weighting beats a simpler constant-weight baseline with the same optimizer.

y2VNlwDT4z.one_liner: Shows expected truncated-CoT correctness is a martingale, so rises in forced-readout accuracy curves come from the measurement.
y2VNlwDT4z.problem: Truncation-curve studies read a rise in accuracy against truncation point as the moment a chain of thought commits to an answer, but the quantity they target is constant in expectation.
y2VNlwDT4z.method: They prove the probability of a correct final answer given a prefix is a bounded martingale under exact continuation, so its expectation is flat and equals full-CoT accuracy, and decompose a published-style pipeline into three departures: interventional readout, survivorship, and an index that is not a stopping time. They also propose specification tests and a corrected protocol.
y2VNlwDT4z.key_idea: Under exact continuation the correct-answer probability given a prefix is a bounded martingale, so any rise in forced-readout curves reflects the intervening readout, not commitment.
y2VNlwDT4z.evidence: 8 models and 4 datasets (1,237,682 generations) comparing exact-continuation and forced-readout curves on the same traces, plus an audit of 18 chat endpoints.
y2VNlwDT4z.claimed_gains: The exact-continuation curve rises on no arm (equivalent to no change within 0.03-0.05) while the forced-readout curve climbs by +0.03 to +0.64, and 12 of 18 audited chat endpoints silently ignore assistant prefills (text cut off).
y2VNlwDT4z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the continuation-versus-intervention distinction is precise and useful, the experiments compare protocols cleanly on shared trajectories, and the corrected protocol has practical value.
y2VNlwDT4z.main_concern: The framing of prior work is too strong because forced readout is a legitimate quantity and the paper does not show what the curve measures instead, and conceptual novelty is modest since flatness follows from conditional-expectation properties.

Y4jlW4Mws6.one_liner: Multi-arm causal deep learner with renormalized pairwise-propensity weighting and transitive pairwise contrasts for e-commerce packaging selection.
Y4jlW4Mws6.problem: Packaging selection at e-commerce scale is largely heuristic and cannot jointly weigh damage protection, material waste, labor, and transportation, while multi-treatment effect estimation suffers from confounded assignment and sparse overlap on rarely used pack types.
Y4jlW4Mws6.method: Frames packaging selection as a multi-armed causal optimization problem. MATEL combines a multi-armed prediction engine with self-calibrating loss and hybrid representation layers, interchangeable tabular backbones, renormalized pairwise-propensity weighting that keeps counterfactual contrasts bounded, and transitive pairwise contrasts with bounded extrapolation for rare pack types.
Y4jlW4Mws6.key_idea: Renormalize pairwise propensity weights to keep counterfactual contrasts bounded and doubly robust under overlap, and build effects for rare arms through transitive pairwise contrasts.
Y4jlW4Mws6.evidence: Large-scale fulfillment data estimating per-shipment damage rates for each pack type, compared with a double machine learning benchmark; reviews also cite synthetic-data validation.
Y4jlW4Mws6.claimed_gains: Recovers the directional agreement of the observed pairwise treatment effect on 91% of focal pairs versus 62% for a DML benchmark, improves per-unit CATE directional agreement by >= 12 pp, and keeps every per-unit effect bounded on sparse arms.
Y4jlW4Mws6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the application is practically important and that the architecture and theory (doubly robust, bounded pairwise reconciliation) are well designed, with validation on synthetic and real data.
Y4jlW4Mws6.main_concern: Real-data evaluation relies on an observational reference without ground-truth effects and without real competitors, so directional agreement and coverage do not establish accuracy against true causal effects.

OVMrRLGiPf.one_liner: One-step generation in Representation Autoencoder latent spaces by distilling with a drifting field instead of teacher trajectories.
OVMrRLGiPf.problem: Distilling models in RAE latent spaces is hard because conventional trajectory-based distillation depends on plain teacher-trajectory priors, while RAE latents are highly anisotropic and give more complex trajectories.
OVMrRLGiPf.method: Drift-RAE uses the drifting field as the distillation method, exploiting semantically rich RAE latents and supervising without teacher trajectories. It adds modifications including an extrapolation-based guided sampling method for one-step generation.
OVMrRLGiPf.key_idea: Supervise a one-step student with a drifting field computed in RAE latent space, so distillation needs no teacher trajectories.
OVMrRLGiPf.evidence: ImageNet 256 with 16-epoch distillation and a geometric study of latent spaces; reviews cite ablations on softmax axes, perturbations, sample allocation, CLS tokens, and guidance-head objectives.
OVMrRLGiPf.claimed_gains: Reaches 1.48 FID with only 16-epoch distillation on ImageNet 256, which the abstract says surpasses various existing methods.
OVMrRLGiPf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the generation quality is competitive, the motivation and VAE-versus-RAE latent analysis are sound, and the extensive ablations support the recipe.
OVMrRLGiPf.main_concern: The efficiency claim lacks direct cost comparison (GPU-hours and peak memory; the 16 epochs exclude detached generated samples), and no standard deviations are reported.

J1RUFSFUsk.one_liner: Score Bridge Distillation periodically rebuilds the distillation target from the student's own score, adapted toward the teacher.
J1RUFSFUsk.problem: Score differences at different noise levels give conflicting student updates in distribution matching distillation, and fixed intermediate distributions become misaligned as the student evolves.
J1RUFSFUsk.method: SBD alternates Bridge Score Adaptation, which adapts the current student score toward the teacher to form a bridge, and Bridge Distribution Matching, which trains the student to match that bridge, repeating as the student changes.
J1RUFSFUsk.key_idea: Reconstruct the intermediate matching target periodically from the current student score estimate adapted toward the teacher, instead of using a distribution path fixed before distillation.
J1RUFSFUsk.evidence: Text-to-image (SDXL), unconditional, and class-conditional generation, with controlled ablations, GPU-time-matched DMD controls, and gradient conflict and retention diagnostics per reviews.
J1RUFSFUsk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the target construction has a clear purpose, is supported by meaningful controls, and shows gains across several generation settings.
J1RUFSFUsk.main_concern: It adds an auxiliary bridge denoiser and alternating stages, raising training complexity and tuning burden, with inconsistent DMD versus DMD2 baselines and unquantified overhead.

CRRQwa2mPa.one_liner: Trains a one-step discrete language model without distillation by minimizing a conservation-equation residual of a time-independent flow map.
CRRQwa2mPa.problem: Compressing many-step discrete diffusion or flow sampling into few steps normally requires distilling a pretrained teacher, which caps student quality and needs a two-stage pipeline.
CRRQwa2mPa.method: DBTM builds on a time-independent flow whose autonomous transport map sends any point to a fixed vertex of the simplex in one step, and trains the map by directly minimizing a conservation-equation residual from data with no teacher or time conditioning. Generation iterates the map to a fixed point, and a partial-context interpolant makes extra function evaluations act as refinement steps.
CRRQwa2mPa.key_idea: Learn a time-free transport map whose fixed points are simplex vertices by minimizing a conservation-equation residual, so one map application (or iteration) generates tokens without a teacher.
CRRQwa2mPa.evidence: Language modeling (LM1B and OpenWebText per reviews) and reasoning tasks (Sudoku and GSM8K per reviews) against discrete diffusion and continuous flow baselines such as FMLM, plus flow-level theory.
CRRQwa2mPa.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims improved quality and accuracy over discrete diffusion and continuous flow baselines at one and few steps.
CRRQwa2mPa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distillation-free, time-independent one-step formulation and its flow-level theory are principled and appealing.
CRRQwa2mPa.main_concern: The experiments do not back the theory: DBTM trails FMLM at low NFE without refinement-in-the-loop, GSM8K stays far below autoregressive baselines, and the learned map is not shown to match the idealized flow.

aDOccokoIO.one_liner: Taxonomizes error sources in trajectory-based data attribution and proposes AdamW-influence, which propagates perturbations through AdamW optimizer states.
aDOccokoIO.problem: Trajectory-based attribution methods lack systematic error analysis and mostly assume SGD even when models are trained with AdamW, which undermines faithfulness.
aDOccokoIO.method: Errors are organized into config-level, algorithm-level, and system-level categories. AdamW-influence accounts for AdamW's optimization dynamics (per reviews, by propagating perturbations through parameters and optimizer moment states with linear complexity in training steps), and the paper analyzes the first-order Taylor error and gives practical guidelines.
aDOccokoIO.key_idea: Propagate a training-sample perturbation through both model parameters and AdamW moment states, instead of assuming SGD dynamics, to estimate influence along the trajectory.
aDOccokoIO.evidence: Spearman correlation against ground-truth influence on MLP, CNN, GPT-2 and Llama 3.2-1B settings plus downstream data selection; the error proxy is validated only on MLP and CNN trained on MNIST (per reviews).
aDOccokoIO.claimed_gains: Improves the Spearman correlation between estimated and ground-truth influence by 10% to over 300% across settings spanning MLP, CNN, GPT-2, and Llama 3.2-1B.
aDOccokoIO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the error-source taxonomy and the principled AdamW-aware extension address an important, underexplored reliability problem.
aDOccokoIO.main_concern: Baselines are weak (mainly SGD-influence), and AdamW-influence costs roughly three times the compute and memory, with masking and first-order approximations raising scalability and error-accumulation concerns.

NMYyv3UJhy.one_liner: Trains an LLM to decompile MIDI into Strudel music programs using synthetic supervised data, then RL on unpaired MIDI.
NMYyv3UJhy.problem: Recovering editable, high-level music instructions from symbolic performance is a hard inverse problem, Strudel has little paired MIDI-code data, and optimizing reconstruction alone collapses to unreadable note-by-note transliteration.
NMYyv3UJhy.method: Decomposer first fine-tunes on Strudel-Synth, a synthetic corpus of paired Strudel programs and rendered MIDI (21,174 pairs per reviews). It then refines the model with reinforcement learning on unpaired MIDI, with rewards for both reconstruction faithfulness and code readability.
NMYyv3UJhy.key_idea: Combine synthetic paired SFT with RL on unpaired MIDI using joint faithfulness and readability rewards to avoid note-by-note transliteration.
NMYyv3UJhy.evidence: Synthetic and real-world MIDI benchmarks against closed-source LLMs and a heuristic converter, plus human evaluation (per reviews).
NMYyv3UJhy.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers in the abstract, which claims substantially higher MIDI reconstruction faithfulness than closed-source LLMs and more readable, diverse code than the heuristic converter; reviews cite LMD Onset F1 rising from 0.10 to 0.60 for the 8B model.
NMYyv3UJhy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the symbolic music decompilation task, the synthetic dataset, and the SFT-plus-RL pipeline are useful and deliver substantial faithfulness gains.
NMYyv3UJhy.main_concern: Faithfulness is only partial (note durations and velocities are not in the input), and the LLM-generated synthetic corpus and a readability rubric used as both reward and metric risk circular evaluation and reward hacking.

iXC0nmOa1H.one_liner: Training-free anomaly detection combining patch-to-reference matching with regional pattern-proportion statistics, fused after score calibration.
iXC0nmOa1H.problem: Conventional anomaly detectors handle structural anomalies but struggle with logical anomalies, and recent fixes need category-specific training or auxiliary modules.
iXC0nmOa1H.method: PARC matches patch features against shared normal references for appearance. For composition it clusters normal features into recurring patterns and scores each image's per-region pattern proportions against normal images, then calibrates both scores with normal score distributions and fuses them.
iXC0nmOa1H.key_idea: Cluster normal patch features into recurring patterns, score per-region pattern proportions against normal images, and fuse with calibrated patch-matching scores.
iXC0nmOa1H.evidence: Image-level AUROC on MVTec-LOCO-AD with frozen features and different feature extractors; reviews cite ablations (Tables 4, 5, 9) and a comparison with LogSAD.
iXC0nmOa1H.claimed_gains: Combined image-level AUROC of 91.12% on MVTec-LOCO-AD using frozen features.
iXC0nmOa1H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, training-free, usable with different feature extractors, and promising on logical anomalies at lower compute than LogSAD.
iXC0nmOa1H.main_concern: The method adds little new methodology, since K-means, regional histograms, Mahalanobis distance and score calibration are established, and max-based fusion sometimes lowers logical AUROC.

riTPDTMY4Z.one_liner: Replaces prototype representations with multi-anchor encodings against anomaly and normal anchors for cross-domain text-attributed graph anomaly detection.
riTPDTMY4Z.problem: LLM-based cross-domain TAG anomaly detectors reach high AUROC but low AUPRC because prototype representations lose instance-specific detail, which the authors call the Over-Generalization problem.
riTPDTMY4Z.method: Each node is encoded against a set of high-confidence anomaly and normal anchors instead of prototypes, using textual and topological anchors, to keep cross-domain generalization while preserving instance-specific anomaly characteristics.
riTPDTMY4Z.key_idea: Encode each node by its relation to high-confidence anomaly and normal anchors rather than a shared prototype, retaining instance-specific anomaly signals.
riTPDTMY4Z.evidence: Eight real-world cross-domain datasets, a theoretical characterization of sufficient conditions for over-generalization, and matched-coverage and frozen-encoder controls (per reviews).
riTPDTMY4Z.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms all competitive baselines on eight datasets (abstract truncated); a reviewer cites AUPRC gains of 22.14 points on Pubmed and 15.86 on Texas over the strongest baseline.
riTPDTMY4Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Over-Generalization problem is concrete and practically important and that AUPRC improvements on several target graphs, supported by matched-coverage analysis, are substantial.
riTPDTMY4Z.main_concern: Reviewers question validity: constructed anomalies may align with the signals the method detects, and the contributions of LLM-derived confidence scores and the anchor design are not isolated.

wfDNKydk14.one_liner: Performs dense bundle adjustment by optimizing intermediate tokens of a frozen feed-forward reconstruction model to minimize reprojection error.
wfDNKydk14.problem: Feed-forward reconstruction models are robust but hard to combine with classical bundle adjustment accuracy, which is typically limited to poses and sparse points or patches.
wfDNKydk14.method: The method solves for latent updates to a set of tokens in a feed-forward reconstruction model such as VGGT-Omega or pi^3, minimizing reprojection error given sparse correspondences between frames. The latents jointly encode dense structure and camera poses, and the change in representation provides implicit regularisation.
wfDNKydk14.key_idea: Use intermediate tokens of a pretrained reconstruction network as the bundle-adjustment variable, so sparse matches refine dense geometry and poses through the frozen decoder.
wfDNKydk14.evidence: 3D reconstruction and camera pose estimation across datasets and four feed-forward backbones, with qualitative and quantitative analysis of parametrisations.
wfDNKydk14.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims leading performance on reconstruction and pose estimation without numbers).
wfDNKydk14.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and intuitive, improves pretrained feed-forward models across backbones without changing weights, and beats classical bundle adjustment from the same initialization and matches.
wfDNKydk14.main_concern: Novelty is limited because optimizing latents through a frozen network under multi-view constraints is already explored (NICE-SLAM, Test3R), and the paper does not explain why this parameterization works.

eVSsYh5zKy.one_liner: Distills LLMs by learning a rectified-flow student-to-teacher feature correction and guiding the student along it with a curriculum.
eVSsYh5zKy.problem: Current LLM distillation methods match discrete layer outputs and fail to capture the continuous dynamics of feature evolution inside the model.
eVSsYh5zKy.method: CONTRA-KD first learns a student-to-teacher correction flow in feature space with Rectified Flow. A curriculum-based distillation strategy then guides the student to progressively follow this flow through dynamic intermediate targets, complementing output-level distillation objectives.
eVSsYh5zKy.key_idea: Generate intermediate feature targets from a learned rectified-flow correction between student and teacher states, with progressively larger step sizes as a curriculum.
eVSsYh5zKy.evidence: Multiple teacher-student pairs on instruction-following benchmarks; reviews cite ROUGE-L, four baselines, three model pairs, a cross-tokenizer case, a 13B-to-7B setting and a small human evaluation.
eVSsYh5zKy.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative only: consistent improvements in distillation performance and training stability over strong baselines).
eVSsYh5zKy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is an easy-to-adopt add-on that brings a flow-matching perspective to feature distillation and consistently raises ROUGE-L across baselines and model pairs.
eVSsYh5zKy.main_concern: The learned flow matches paired same-layer states rather than layer-to-layer dynamics, so the dynamics-alignment claim is not supported by the theory, and ablations do not isolate the benefit of continuous-time flow matching.

tzrdDUdU29.one_liner: Benchmark of 19,200 synthetic diagrams plus a two-step VLM pipeline that extracts nodes, then predicts edges per source node.
tzrdDUdU29.problem: Complete diagram topology extraction, covering all entities and all relations among them, is underexplored for vision-language models that are mostly evaluated on recognizing elements and answering localized questions.
tzrdDUdU29.method: Knossos has 19,200 diagrams across six domains with 245,179 nodes and 439,740 edges, generated symbolically so images align exactly with topology, relation types and connector geometry. Ariadne decomposes extraction into node inventory extraction and source-conditioned edge prediction.
tzrdDUdU29.key_idea: Split diagram-to-graph extraction into a node inventory pass and edge prediction conditioned on each source node, trained on symbolically generated exact annotations.
tzrdDUdU29.evidence: Training smaller open-source VLMs on Knossos, comparing Ariadne with one-step extraction under matched supervision, and an external evaluation on TopoBench subsets per the reviews.
tzrdDUdU29.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before final numbers; it reports only that Knossos training substantially improves small open-source VLMs and that Ariadne improves over one-step extraction).
tzrdDUdU29.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree Knossos is a valuable, precisely annotated resource for complete topology extraction and that training on it and staged extraction clearly improve edge extraction.
tzrdDUdU29.main_concern: Gains from source-group decomposition are confounded with node-edge separation and unequal training budgets, and the fully synthetic benchmark shows limited generalization to external real diagrams.

B4kFuN1Azr.one_liner: Partitions long game interaction into visually recognized places and shares skill experience across places via optimal-transport outcome compatibility.
B4kFuN1Azr.problem: Visual agents in unfamiliar 3D environments accumulate long interaction streams that are brittle to retrieve or replay as monolithic trajectories.
B4kFuN1Azr.method: Visually re-identifiable places split long-horizon interaction into retrievable, verifiable segments. SCOCS compares skill-conditioned outcome distributions with optimal transport and evaluates successor compatibility recursively; screened successful segments adapt a visual-action controller for low-level actions while the VLM uses retrieved evidence to set persistent goals and replan.
B4kFuN1Azr.key_idea: Decide whether experience transfers between places by comparing skill-conditioned outcome distributions with optimal transport, rather than by visual similarity of the places.
B4kFuN1Azr.evidence: A common protocol in ViZDoom and held-out Xonotic and Sauerbraten, with online acquisition and reuse of experience and no target-engine policy training.
B4kFuN1Azr.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims the best system-level results in ViZDoom and the best task performance on Xonotic and Sauerbraten without numbers).
B4kFuN1Azr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating place recognition from skill-specific experience applicability is well motivated, with ablations showing that selective sharing matters.
B4kFuN1Azr.main_concern: It is a complex multi-component system whose core contribution is hard to isolate, with unclear novelty over topological place maps and no isolation of optimal transport against simpler sharing rules.

zE3sfnvmoP.one_liner: Real-scale Hong Kong 3D city sandbox with continuous control for testing whether MLLM agents turn local perception into long-horizon navigation.
zE3sfnvmoP.problem: It is unclear how far current MLLM agents can turn local urban perception into reliable action once they start to move in a real-scale city.
zE3sfnvmoP.method: UrbanGround is built from Hong Kong's territory-wide 3D geospatial data, with continuous collision-constrained control, first-person observations and an interactive map. Tasks run from local question answering to long-horizon navigation, organized around three research questions on local evidence, navigation at distance, and robustness to route changes and pedestrian motion.
zE3sfnvmoP.key_idea: Evaluate agents on a ladder of tasks in a real-scale 3D city so failures can be traced as tasks grow from local perception to long-horizon exploration.
zE3sfnvmoP.evidence: An evaluation of MLLM agents across the task ladder (reviews mention 12 models) with trajectory diagnostics.
zE3sfnvmoP.claimed_gains: not stated (benchmark paper; the abstract reports qualitative findings that atomic recognition and short-range reasoning are useful while orientation, pedestrian-aware movement and extended exploration are unreliable).
zE3sfnvmoP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the realistic 3D urban environment with continuous control and the progressive task ladder are valuable for evaluating MLLM agents.
zE3sfnvmoP.main_concern: Findings largely restate known perception-action and error-accumulation gaps, and near-zero success on many navigation tasks creates floor effects without ablations of the agent harness or memory.

bL0K0Fcsdb.one_liner: Distills plan-perceive-compose reasoning from separate teachers into one mixture-of-experts vision-language model for egocentric spatial reasoning.
bL0K0Fcsdb.problem: Vision-language models struggle with complex egocentric spatial questions, and agentic systems that call external vision and geometry tools leave those tools unchanged during reasoning training.
bL0K0Fcsdb.method: Planner and Perception teachers are trained with separate Dual-LoRA adapters, then a mixture-of-experts student is fine-tuned under their supervision. The student is further trained on its own trajectories with a segment-level extension of multi-teacher on-policy distillation, with different segments supervised by different teachers.
bL0K0Fcsdb.key_idea: Assign trajectory segments to Planner or Perception teachers during multi-teacher on-policy distillation so one MoE student runs the full workflow without external tools.
bL0K0Fcsdb.evidence: Evaluated on three spatial reasoning benchmarks (the rest of the abstract is cut off), with comparison to a direct-RL baseline in the supplement.
bL0K0Fcsdb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the plan-perceive-compose decomposition well motivated, the method coherent, and the improvements over baselines clear and practically significant.
bL0K0Fcsdb.main_concern: The most relevant baseline, direct RL on the target benchmarks, is placed in the supplement, and benchmark and backbone diversity is limited.

Soo1kJI9oA.one_liner: Adds an on-policy ELBO regularizer to diffusion policy-gradient updates to keep the ELBO tight and training stable.
Soo1kJI9oA.problem: Diffusion policy gradient methods are unstable because optimizing a variational surrogate lets the ELBO drift from the true log-likelihood, making the proxy gradient misaligned with the true policy gradient (double drift).
Soo1kJI9oA.method: DiPOD interleaves self-distillation with policy-improving gradient updates, which in practice means adding an on-policy ELBO regularizer to each diffusion policy-gradient update.
Soo1kJI9oA.key_idea: Keep the ELBO tight to the true likelihood during RL post-training by regularizing each policy-gradient step with an on-policy ELBO term.
Soo1kJI9oA.evidence: Diffusion language model post-training and continuous-control diffusion policies, plus theory linking variational discrepancy to policy-gradient error and improvement.
Soo1kJI9oA.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that training is substantially stabilized and higher rewards are reached than with previous methods).
Soo1kJI9oA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the double-drift view insightful, the fix simple, and the reported improvements on reasoning tasks substantial, for example Countdown accuracy from 51.95 to 80.08 with SPG+DiPOD per one review.
Soo1kJI9oA.main_concern: The policy-improvement theorem covers an idealized alternating procedure and does not cover the practical joint-update algorithm actually used.

JV9P4TpgC3.one_liner: Regularizes intermediate slider trajectories in instruction-based image editing with velocity- and semantic-space losses, spectral control and disentanglement.
JV9P4TpgC3.problem: Existing edit-strength sliders show abrupt jumps, non-monotonic changes and interference between jointly controlled sliders.
JV9P4TpgC3.method: SliderEdit++ adds velocity- and semantic-space trajectory regularization with spectral control, plus a disentanglement objective, on a few-step editing backbone. The authors also introduce SlideBench with metrics for monotonic progression, perceptual continuity and inter-slider disentanglement.
JV9P4TpgC3.key_idea: Supervise the interior of the slider trajectory, not just its endpoints, using trajectory regularizers and a disentanglement loss.
JV9P4TpgC3.evidence: Evaluated on the new SlideBench benchmark against slider-based baselines, with a same-backbone ablation of the regularizers.
JV9P4TpgC3.claimed_gains: Improves the SlideBench overall score by 18.5% relative to the strongest baseline and is approximately 3x to 20x faster than existing slider-based approaches.
JV9P4TpgC3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear, explicit interior regularization is a sensible extension of endpoint-only training, and the benchmark is useful.
JV9P4TpgC3.main_concern: The advance is narrow relative to SliderEdit and Kontinuous Kontext, and the evaluation does not separate smoother trajectories from lost low-strength editing range.

eUlR2auf5L.one_liner: Frames LLM distillation attacks and defenses as a minimax game, yielding adaptive students and a Product-of-Experts defense.
eUlR2auf5L.problem: Antidistillation defenses are evaluated against passive students, which understates what adaptive students can recover from released outputs.
eUlR2auf5L.method: A minimax game between a utility-constrained teacher and an adaptive student yields one-sided response rules: a student that reweights high-value examples and a teacher-side defense template. From a cheap proxy for example value they derive Product-of-Experts (PoE), a forward-pass-only defense that combines the teacher with a proxy student during generation.
eUlR2auf5L.key_idea: Combine teacher and proxy-student distributions at generation time (PoE) to suppress outputs most useful for distillation, evaluated against adaptive reweighting students.
eUlR2auf5L.evidence: Experiments on GSM8K and MATH comparing PoE with existing defenses under passive and adaptive students, including compute cost and reasoning-trace quality.
eUlR2auf5L.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports qualitatively that adaptive students recover substantially more capability and that PoE is substantially cheaper with higher-quality reasoning traces).
eUlR2auf5L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the finding that passive evaluation understates adaptive students, the clean minimax framing, and the compute-efficient PoE defense with ablations on cost and reasoning quality.
eUlR2auf5L.main_concern: The implemented adaptive attack and PoE differ from the theoretical population-level game (minibatch normalization, one-sided best response), and evaluation covers only two math datasets.

gejhRo8Pdz.one_liner: Pairs application-level agent telemetry with kernel syscall traces to test whether kernel evidence improves attack detection.
gejhRo8Pdz.problem: Agent-security benchmarks and defenses operate at the application layer and miss threats that smuggle instructions or actions past it.
gejhRo8Pdz.method: The authors introduce Agent Cross-Layer Evidence (ACE), a paired-session corpus of 4,047 sessions and 17 threat models across six delivery-vector families and 14 of 25 OWASP categories, organized into 12 attack mechanics. They compare app-only, kernel-only and combined views across four detector families.
gejhRo8Pdz.key_idea: Pair application-layer agent telemetry with kernel-level syscall traces from the same sessions to measure the complementary signal of each layer.
gejhRo8Pdz.evidence: Four detector families on ACE, with per-mechanic analysis, generalization to unseen attack families and transfer to an alternate agent runtime.
gejhRo8Pdz.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says kernel evidence is discriminative alone and combining it with application-layer evidence generally outperforms either view.
gejhRo8Pdz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the paired benchmark covering many attack entry points and the systematic comparison of app, kernel and cross-view evidence across detectors.
gejhRo8Pdz.main_concern: Contribution is mainly a dataset and empirical characterization with hand-crafted attacks in controlled environments, with unclear new findings beyond prior execution-level work and open transfer questions.

IoYBVmgSfD.one_liner: Measures a composition penalty when LLMs answer from histories with updated facts, and tests rewriting history as one current state.
IoYBVmgSfD.problem: Language models answer less accurately from a history containing original facts and updates than they do on identifying current facts or answering from them separately.
IoYBVmgSfD.method: Controlled tasks separately test current-fact identification and answering, then combined history-based answering, with duplication, attention blocking and activation patching to probe causes. Rewriting the history into one current state is tested as a mitigation.
IoYBVmgSfD.key_idea: Stale or duplicated state descriptions interfere with in-context computation, and compiling a faithful single current-state description removes most of the penalty.
IoYBVmgSfD.evidence: Controlled tasks across three model families, attention blocking of obsolete values, deletion experiments on novels, and longer-history tests with rewriting.
IoYBVmgSfD.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract describes the penalty and says rewriting nearly eliminates it in controlled tasks without giving numbers).
IoYBVmgSfD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the controlled experiments convincing, with alternative explanations ruled out, the penalty shown on items where both separate tasks succeed, and honest reporting of failed cases.
IoYBVmgSfD.main_concern: The link between the controlled mechanism and long-history failures is incomplete, and some headline numbers mix stale-state interference with other long-context demands.

jjKYVDeVNx.one_liner: Selects instruction-tuning data with a submodular graph cut over a gradient similarity graph, then synthesizes examples for uncovered target directions.
jjKYVDeVNx.problem: Point-wise targeted data selection scores each candidate independently, so at tight budgets the chosen subset is dominated by near-redundant examples.
jjKYVDeVNx.method: QSGS formulates selection as a submodular graph cut over a gradient similarity graph, with a modular relevance term toward the target set and a pairwise dispersion penalty against redundancy. A gradient-guided synthesis step then identifies under-covered target directions and generates examples for them (the abstract is cut off).
jjKYVDeVNx.key_idea: Replace independent top-k gradient scoring with a graph-cut objective that trades target relevance against intra-subset redundancy, plus synthesis for gaps in coverage.
jjKYVDeVNx.evidence: Reviews describe selecting about 1,350 examples from a 270K pool, tested on three models and three benchmarks (MMLU, TyDiQA, BBH) against LESS with three-seed standard deviations.
jjKYVDeVNx.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that the benefit of diversity-aware selection grows as the data budget decreases).
jjKYVDeVNx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the redundancy-at-tight-budgets motivation clear and the graph-cut selector simple and cheap, with results across several models close to full-data training in the reported regime.
jjKYVDeVNx.main_concern: Novelty over LESS and other gradient-based or submodular selection methods is limited, and the gradient-guided synthesis step is neither isolated by a control nor specified well enough to reproduce.

0KYXYHJ0My.one_liner: Makes token generation order the only variable in a shared causal model to compare autoregressive and random orders.
0KYXYHJ0My.problem: It is unclear what determines the best generation order, because prior AR versus masked-diffusion comparisons change attention, objective and decoding schedule at the same time.
0KYXYHJ0My.method: A shared causal-attention model takes token order as an explicit input and decouples training order from inference order. Linear dynamical systems and their shuffled versions serve as controlled proxies, supported by an information-theoretic analysis.
0KYXYHJ0My.key_idea: Make order the only variable and test all training-order and inference-order combinations to separate order diversity as data augmentation from scattered orders limiting error accumulation.
0KYXYHJ0My.evidence: Language, image and linear-dynamical-system experiments with controlled order comparisons, fixed-random controls and an information-theoretic analysis; reviews note the images are CIFAR-10 and FFHQ at 32x32.
0KYXYHJ0My.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports that AR order wins on language and ordinary LDS and random order wins on images and shuffled LDS, without numbers).
0KYXYHJ0My.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled design that separates training order from inference order under a fixed architecture, and the fixed-random control that distinguishes order diversity from a particular order.
0KYXYHJ0My.main_concern: Theorem 2 assumes single-token conditioning and does not explain full-prefix transformers, and the image experiments are limited to small 32x32 datasets.

4StuYSDTaq.one_liner: Trains a vision-language model to predict and render an object-centered coordinate frame on the image before reasoning from another viewpoint.
4StuYSDTaq.problem: Vision-language models struggle with perspective taking and often default to the camera viewpoint when a query requires another entity's or an imagined observer's perspective.
4StuYSDTaq.method: LeRF decides whether a coordinate frame is needed, grounds the reference entity, predicts the frame's origin and entity-centered axes, and a lightweight renderer overlays the frame on the image. Training uses supervised fine-tuning for selective tool invocation and frame prediction, then reinforcement learning on spatial VQA pairs.
4StuYSDTaq.key_idea: Make the requested viewpoint explicit as a rendered 2D-projected reference frame that the model predicts itself, avoiding external perception models or 3D reconstruction.
4StuYSDTaq.evidence: Several perspective-taking benchmarks compared with the backbone and open-source methods, with diagnostics on frame use and SFT versus direct RL.
4StuYSDTaq.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that LeRF consistently improves over its backbone and performs strongly against open-source methods).
4StuYSDTaq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the explicit reference-frame idea intuitive and well motivated, with consistent same-backbone gains and a practical data-curation pipeline from existing pose annotations.
4StuYSDTaq.main_concern: Ablations show the rendered frame adds little (57.18 vs 57.97 overall without rendering), so gains may come from frame-prediction SFT and RL, and performance drops on the OmniSpatial-PT Ego subset.

CXSB8FgWxu.one_liner: Restores KV caches by a staircase partition of token-layer space and batch-aware dynamic-programming planning across GPUs.
CXSB8FgWxu.problem: KV cache restoration is a bottleneck in long-context serving, yet existing methods treat it as a coarse per-request choice between recomputing and loading and ignore parallelism within the model and contention across requests.
CXSB8FgWxu.method: CacheFlow unifies token- and layer-wise restoration as a staircase partition of the token-layer space, uses lightweight boundary activations to restore across model shards concurrently, and runs a batch-aware dynamic-programming planner that decides what to recompute and what to load across requests and layer blocks.
CXSB8FgWxu.key_idea: Treat restoration as joint parallel execution over tokens, layers and GPUs, with a dynamic-programming planner balancing GPU compute against shared I/O.
CXSB8FgWxu.evidence: Dense and hybrid models from single-digit to hundred-billion parameters, diverse workloads and hardware conditions; reviews mention a 122B hybrid MoE on eight H100 GPUs.
CXSB8FgWxu.claimed_gains: not stated (the supplied abstract is cut off at 'CacheFlow reduces restoration latency by'; the TL;DR says it significantly reduces time-to-first-token).
CXSB8FgWxu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the staircase formulation clean, the joint token-layer-device optimization and hybrid-architecture handling interesting, and the planning overhead low.
CXSB8FgWxu.main_concern: Practical motivation and novelty are questioned: it is unclear how often restoration is the bottleneck, token- and layer-wise pieces resemble Cake and HCache, and boundary-activation overhead is not reported.

BBazok7QP3.one_liner: Co-trains the teacher in on-policy distillation with reinforcement learning on student-generated prefixes.
BBazok7QP3.problem: In on-policy distillation the student's trajectories are off-policy for the teacher, whose continuation quality degrades as student prefixes grow longer.
BBazok7QP3.method: SCOUT periodically optimizes the teacher's conditional ability alongside standard OPD updates: the teacher generates continuations from student prefixes and learns from outcome rewards with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.
BBazok7QP3.key_idea: Adapt the teacher to student-generated prefixes by RLVR during distillation instead of keeping the teacher fixed.
BBazok7QP3.evidence: Controlled experiments on the teacher's continuation ability from student prefixes, and runs across multiple teacher-student configurations, model scales and reasoning domains (math and code per reviews).
BBazok7QP3.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that SCOUT consistently improves the effectiveness of on-policy distillation).
BBazok7QP3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem identification and diagnostics clear, the method simple, and the improvements consistent, with controls such as fixed student prefixes and teacher-only GRPO supporting the mechanism.
BBazok7QP3.main_concern: Comparison against alternatives with the same feedback and compute, such as fixed-teacher OPD plus student-side reward optimization, is missing, and the method needs a tunable teacher and verifiable rewards.

yVo9mX6Bo8.one_liner: Measures how a failed attempt in context biases later LLM reasoning toward similar errors, and tests filtering drafts.
yVo9mX6Bo8.problem: Self-improvement pipelines reuse prior attempts as context, but flawed attempts may bias later generations even when the model recognizes them as wrong.
yVo9mX6Bo8.method: The authors study contextual drag, mainly self-drag where a model conditions on its own incorrect draft, across many reasoning models and tasks, with tree edit distance on Game of 24 to show structural bias. They test a FILTER step that cleans the draft before reuse, without training or external labels.
yVo9mX6Bo8.key_idea: Incorrect drafts in context pull later generations toward structurally similar errors, and filtering the draft before reuse reduces this pull.
yVo9mX6Bo8.evidence: 10 open-weight reasoning models and 8 reasoning tasks, with explicit error signals, iterative refinement, a Game of 24 tree-edit-distance case study and filtering tests.
yVo9mX6Bo8.claimed_gains: A single incorrect draft drops average pass@1 accuracy by around 25 points on problems where direct reasoning produces both successes and failures; filtering reduces drag on every model tested, by a model-dependent amount.
yVo9mX6Bo8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the phenomenon practically relevant to self-refinement pipelines and the evidence broad across models and tasks, with confounds checked and a useful structural analysis.
yVo9mX6Bo8.main_concern: Structural evidence is limited to Game of 24, FILTER stays below simply discarding the draft in the single-step setting, and novelty over prior self-correction limitation work is questioned.

WlMyCip81U.one_liner: Retrains models on residue-order-shuffled sequences to show a sparse-autoencoder interpretability metric rises even when native structure is destroyed.
WlMyCip81U.problem: Interpretability metrics are justified by robustness checks such as seeds and analytic choices, which do not show the metric is valid for the interpretation attached to it.
WlMyCip81U.method: They test the metric L_struct, which measures whether SAE feature activations cluster across spatially contacting residues, in masked versus causal protein language models. Models are retrained on sequences with native residue order destroyed, and compared with random-initialisation, no-model and amino-acid-stratified permutation baselines.
WlMyCip81U.key_idea: Use a training-distribution control, retraining on order-destroyed data, to falsify whether a metric depends on the structure it claims to measure.
WlMyCip81U.evidence: Controlled masked versus causal comparison across depths and seeds, six diagnostic analyses, shuffled-data retraining, random-initialisation baselines and permutation nulls.
WlMyCip81U.claimed_gains: After order-destroying retraining, L_struct increases in 52 of 54 objective-by-depth-by-seed cells, and a cysteine indicator exceeds every learned feature in 32 of the same 54 cells.
WlMyCip81U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paired design rigorous, controlling architecture, initialization, corpus and batch order, and the result a striking warning that robustness does not imply validity.
