WlMyCip81U.main_concern: Amino-acid composition is left as an unresolved confound and the mechanism behind the score increase is unexplained, with results limited to one architecture and scale.

ionMcwU5xU.one_liner: Schedules benchmark and agent-side events on one hybrid simulated clock and records model calls to train unmodified agents.
ionMcwU5xU.problem: Continual-learning evaluations need agent-side events such as session restarts, crons and memory consolidation, but existing benchmarks and training frameworks schedule only their own events, so each benchmark-agent pair needs a custom loop.
ionMcwU5xU.method: SCLATE lets benchmarks and unmodified agents add events to one open event scheduler through adapters. A hybrid simulated clock runs in real time while the agent works and skips idle gaps, and an in-container proxy records tokens and log probabilities of every model call for training.
ionMcwU5xU.key_idea: Put benchmark events and agent-side events on one shared hybrid clock and capture model calls through a proxy so any harness and memory can be evaluated and trained unmodified.
ionMcwU5xU.evidence: Seven ported benchmarks, ten unmodified harness and memory configurations compared on ten models, and post-training of Qwen3.5-4B through unmodified harnesses and memory systems.
ionMcwU5xU.claimed_gains: The simulated clock compresses a month-long scenario into hours, and the post-trained Qwen3.5-4B reads 8.9x fewer file lines with a 16.6-point (cut off in the supplied abstract) improvement.
ionMcwU5xU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the unified design well motivated, the substrate compatible with several harnesses, benchmarks and models without agent code changes, and the clock effective for compressing long scenarios.
ionMcwU5xU.main_concern: Components have close precedents (Agent Lightning, POLAR, Harbor, ARE/GAIA-2) and no experiment shows that putting agent-side events on a shared clock changes any result, with key findings based on single runs.

zYpZAtKwzp.one_liner: Benchmarks GUI agents on simulated CT, MR and ultrasound consoles, scoring workflow and acquisition quality separately.
zYpZAtKwzp.problem: Agents that operate medical imaging consoles must link on-screen anatomy to acquisition decisions, and completing a console workflow does not show the intended anatomy was acquired.
zYpZAtKwzp.method: MedImageOSWorld gives agents screenshots and mouse-and-keyboard actions to configure protocols, plan acquisitions, inspect images and correct them across seven capability levels. Evaluation combines workflow checks with hidden anatomical ground truth under a common protocol with interaction budgets.
zYpZAtKwzp.key_idea: Separate procedural workflow progress from acquisition outcome by scoring acquired images against hidden anatomy in a shared subject coordinate frame.
zYpZAtKwzp.evidence: Eleven open-weight agents evaluated across the seven levels, with recorded trajectories for failure analysis.
zYpZAtKwzp.claimed_gains: Success rates range from 3.0 to 25.0 on a 0-100 scale while workflow-progress rates reach 21.5-74.5; the best agent drops from 79-90% at the lowest three levels to at most 12% for millimetre-level planning.
zYpZAtKwzp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the task underexplored and clinically meaningful, and value separating workflow completion from anatomical correctness and the in-depth failure analysis.
zYpZAtKwzp.main_concern: The simulated consoles use task-relevant physical abstractions with limited fidelity, so validity for real acquisition is unclear, and no expert baseline is given for feasibility.

AMQlqE7URU.one_liner: Treats video tasks as visual analogies by completing a spatiotemporal canvas given one demonstration, with no task-specific modules.
AMQlqE7URU.problem: Adapting video models to new tasks needs dedicated data curation and fine-tuning, and visual analogy as a training-free alternative has been limited to images.
AMQlqE7URU.method: ViGeo extends visual in-context learning to video by completing a spatiotemporal canvas that contains a demonstration pair and a query. It is trained and tested on a task taxonomy with a strict train-test split.
AMQlqE7URU.key_idea: Specify the task in-context by placing a demonstration pair and a query on one spatiotemporal canvas and completing the missing part.
AMQlqE7URU.evidence: A diverse task taxonomy with a strict train-test split covering camera control, modality-guided generation and video manipulation, with unseen manipulations and zero-shot modalities such as event cameras.
AMQlqE7URU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework simple and general, handling camera control, modality-guided generation and manipulation without task-specific modules, with evaluation on unseen tasks and a useful study of task internalization.
AMQlqE7URU.main_concern: Evidence is thin: video manipulation is scored only by 1-MSE with limited baselines, task internalization is shown on one task, and generalization is partial, with weak controls showing true analogy learning.

e7wLoKZq45.one_liner: Benchmarks 145 long-horizon mobile tasks with a multimodal skill library under GUI-only and hybrid execution.
e7wLoKZq45.problem: No benchmark compares agent skill designs under controlled conditions on long, interactive mobile tasks with verifiable outcomes and hybrid execution.
e7wLoKZq45.method: Mobile Skills Bench has 145 long-horizon tasks across 24 simulated apps with a verifiable backend and user simulator, supporting Pure GUI and Hybrid (GUI, MCP, CLI) execution. Its skill library has 73 procedures with 166 reference images, organized by function, function-app pair and app.
e7wLoKZq45.key_idea: Control skill content and modality (text versus multimodal with reference images) on matched tasks with resettable app states and backend verification.
e7wLoKZq45.evidence: Nine models evaluated in three agent harnesses, with and without textual and multimodal skills.
e7wLoKZq45.claimed_gains: Without skills, nine models average 28.9% task success under Hybrid and 12.5% under Pure GUI; with textual skills the averages rise to 34.2% and 15.0%; the multimodal result is cut off in the supplied abstract.
e7wLoKZq45.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value that it combines user interaction, hybrid execution, long trajectories, deterministic evaluation, skills and multimodality, with matched-task comparisons and backend checks including unintended edits.
e7wLoKZq45.main_concern: Simulated apps with skills generated from the simulator source may overstate real-world benefit, and the added value of reference images over live screenshots is unclear.

jqNZwJ4TiE.one_liner: Co-evolves a simulation data engine and action policy through shared memory that turns VLM-critic diagnoses into programs.
jqNZwJ4TiE.problem: Physically valid generated robot environments are not necessarily useful for training; the challenge is finding environments that target a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them.
jqNZwJ4TiE.method: A shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures and learning progress compiles validated diagnoses from a vision-language critic into generation programs and training programs. Text2potential converts diagnoses into staged potentials for action-chunk value learning, and measured learning progress guides further generation.
jqNZwJ4TiE.key_idea: Use one validated diagnosis both to generate a matching hard environment and to build staged shaping potentials, with learning progress steering the next round.
jqNZwJ4TiE.evidence: Four manipulation task families, and LIBERO-Pro over 15 rounds of generation and training under position and instruction perturbations.
jqNZwJ4TiE.claimed_gains: Out-of-distribution success rises from 5.3% after supervised fine-tuning to 27.6%, 9.5 points above the strongest closed-loop baseline at the same generation budget; on LIBERO-Pro, success rises from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations.
jqNZwJ4TiE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation well supported and the diagnosis-to-generation and diagnosis-to-training interface a substantive systems idea, with comprehensive ablations on memory, critic, rounds and Text2potential.
jqNZwJ4TiE.main_concern: There are no real-robot or sim-to-real results, and the learning-progress allocation and shaping conditions are not specified precisely.

rCXqpYtxzk.one_liner: Uses an LLM auditor, trained with RL, to steer a numerical solver that sets ensemble weights over time-series foundation models.
rCXqpYtxzk.problem: No single time-series foundation model dominates across regimes, and applying LLMs directly to forecasting is ineffective.
rCXqpYtxzk.method: A continuous optimization solver determines the ensemble weights while an LLM auditor steers the optimization through iterative hypothesis testing and dynamic metric routing. The auditor is trained with an R1-style RL pipeline using a decomposition-level attribution-agreement reward.
rCXqpYtxzk.key_idea: Reposition the LLM as a metacognitive auditor over a constrained weight optimizer instead of a direct forecaster.
rCXqpYtxzk.evidence: GIFT-Eval benchmark across 23 datasets and 97 settings, with comparisons to non-LLM controllers in the appendix per reviews.
rCXqpYtxzk.claimed_gains: Outperforms all leading time-series foundation models on both CRPS and MASE on GIFT-Eval; no numeric margins are given.
rCXqpYtxzk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the separation of numerical optimization from LLM-based decisions sensible and controlled, with good GIFT-Eval results and a useful training dataset of optimization explanations.
rCXqpYtxzk.main_concern: Theorem 3.1 (a strictly positive ensemble advantage) is not rigorously supported at the stated generality, and the incremental benefit of an LLM controller over non-LLM selection is unclear.

AhZvCJnpeQ.one_liner: Provides a 360-problem Lean benchmark covering auto-formalization, theorem proving and proof-error localization for machine learning theory.
AhZvCJnpeQ.problem: It is unclear whether LLMs can assist the rigorous construction and verification of machine learning theory, which depends on precise assumptions and derivations.
AhZvCJnpeQ.method: MLP-Bench spans 16 topics with two forward-construction tasks (formalizing natural-language theorems into Lean, proving Lean statements) and one backward-verification task (judging a proof and localizing the first erroneous step with Lean-checked evidence).
AhZvCJnpeQ.key_idea: Ground ML theory assistance in Lean, which mechanically checks derivations against stated assumptions, and test both construction and review.
AhZvCJnpeQ.evidence: Evaluation of 11 models on the three tasks, with failure analysis of auto-formalization and Lean-checked refutation.
AhZvCJnpeQ.claimed_gains: Auto-formalization reaches at most a 27.5% bidirectional equivalence (BEq) pass rate against gold Lean statements, and specialized provers solve 0.0% of (cut off in the supplied abstract).
AhZvCJnpeQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the benchmark fills a gap by using research-level theorems and real flawed proofs with human semantic checking, and note omitted implicit assumptions as a main auto-formalization bottleneck.
AhZvCJnpeQ.main_concern: The three tasks are evaluated separately with gold intermediate inputs, so error propagation is not measured, and Lean-checked refutations may not always match genuine errors in the source proof.

LDYRWfn2Fl.one_liner: Derives exact thresholds where always fielding the strongest lineup permanently locks out alternatives, and when rotation avoids it.
LDYRWfn2Fl.problem: Assigning each player to their best position gives them practice there, raising the performance floor and potentially making alternative assignments permanently unreachable.
LDYRWfn2Fl.method: A theoretical model with a rising performance floor yields an exact threshold on tolerated performance decline for lock-in, results for early rotation and for noisy tryouts, and simulations of teams of five to fifty players including neural networks trained on assigned tasks.
LDYRWfn2Fl.key_idea: Lock-in arises because the tolerated-decline floor rises with team strength; a fixed floor at the starting level would not cause permanent unreachability.
LDYRWfn2Fl.evidence: Proofs plus simulated teams of five to fifty players and neural networks trained on assigned tasks.
LDYRWfn2Fl.claimed_gains: For five players starting at skill .40 the threshold is a 24% decline; observed thresholds are within 1.4% of predictions in simulation, and the median ratio of measured to predicted threshold is .93 for neural networks.
LDYRWfn2Fl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the formulation original and mathematically clean, with precise exact-threshold results and numerical experiments that illustrate the performance-qualification tradeoff.
LDYRWfn2Fl.main_concern: Results rely on symmetric or near-symmetric synthetic initial skills, and the proposed remedies break down once modest skill forgetting is introduced.

w5vBRbe4Wc.one_liner: Represents 3D shapes as unions of polyhedra with a closed-form zero level set, fitted by gradient descent and matching.
w5vBRbe4Wc.problem: Existing shape representations need many parameters to capture highly detailed geometry and lack provable approximation and complexity guarantees.
w5vBRbe4Wc.method: Patchwork encodes a shape as a union of polyhedra with a simple closed-form zero-level-set equation, with provable complexity bounds and arbitrary-precision approximation. Fitting pairs gradient-based optimization with a combinatorial matching scheme, assignment stabilization and pruning, and supports explicit polygonalization and conforming volume mesh extraction.
w5vBRbe4Wc.key_idea: Define the surface as the interface between positively and negatively labeled polyhedral (power) cells and fit it by matching cell pairs to samples by normal alignment.
w5vBRbe4Wc.evidence: Fitting experiments against existing implicit representations, including highly detailed artist-created assets, plus a mathematical analysis of expressiveness and complexity.
w5vBRbe4Wc.claimed_gains: Achieves superior quality with 3-6x fewer parameters than existing alternatives on average.
w5vBRbe4Wc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the polyhedral implicit-explicit formulation principled, with provable expressiveness and strong quantitative and qualitative fitting results using substantially fewer parameters.
w5vBRbe4Wc.main_concern: A closely related recent baseline (DCCVT) is missing, the 'without DM' ablation changes several things at once, and the pipeline is limited to closed manifold surfaces.

IzG8PUZzVA.one_liner: Learns POMDP beliefs as semi-implicit mixtures moved by a memory-conditioned Hamiltonian flow and reweighted by a gated recurrent memory.
IzG8PUZzVA.problem: Belief errors accumulate in POMDPs when observations are uninformative for many steps, and existing belief representations assume regular informative observations or need ground-truth states.
IzG8PUZzVA.method: GBVI treats any belief change as transport of probability mass plus reweighting. Semi-implicit variational inference splits the belief into components, a memory-conditioned Hamiltonian flow transports them across timesteps, and a gated recurrent memory reweights them, both learned from observations alone.
IzG8PUZzVA.key_idea: Decompose belief updates into learned transport (Hamiltonian flow) and learned reweighting (gated memory) so hypotheses persist through long uninformative gaps.
IzG8PUZzVA.evidence: Symmetric Light-Dark, occluded Atari and Area Search, compared with recurrent, variational, particle-based and state-supervised baselines, with a comparison to the exact posterior on Area Search.
IzG8PUZzVA.claimed_gains: not stated (the supplied abstract says GBVI outperforms the baselines and is cut off before the Area Search belief-error result).
IzG8PUZzVA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the combination of topics a new way to address a key POMDP problem, with comprehensive theory and appendix, an exact-posterior comparison, and promising results.
IzG8PUZzVA.main_concern: The transport-plus-reweighting decomposition is the classical Gaussian-sum filter update, the paper is hard to follow, and the claim that hypotheses stay distinct is too strong.

B6LIMyqthm.one_liner: Combines geometric reasoning experts through block-wise dense fusion with a gating network for monocular human-object interaction reconstruction.
B6LIMyqthm.problem: Monocular human-object reconstruction suffers from depth ambiguity and occlusion, and existing Transformer methods fix the organization of geometric reasoning operations in the architecture.
B6LIMyqthm.method: SG-MoE uses experts for global human-object interaction, entity-specific topology and evolving relative geometry, combined by block-wise dense fusion during progressive reconstruction. A bidirectional geometric interaction mechanism couples intermediate geometry with cross-entity feature reasoning.
B6LIMyqthm.key_idea: Learn state-dependent weights over complementary geometric experts at each decoder block instead of hard-wiring one reasoning structure.
B6LIMyqthm.evidence: Experiments on BEHAVE and InterCap measuring human mesh reconstruction, posed-object geometry and contact recovery, with ablations of each expert and the composition rule.
B6LIMyqthm.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports consistent improvements over prior methods on BEHAVE and InterCap with favorable inference efficiency.
B6LIMyqthm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find consistent gains on both benchmarks including contact metrics, a task-specific expert design, and ablations that isolate each expert, with a fast, relatively small model.
B6LIMyqthm.main_concern: State-adaptive composition is not demonstrated, since the gate learns roughly one scalar weight per expert per block and the modules are reuses of existing techniques.

zjzr2iULaW.one_liner: Injects a unified multi-view SMPL-X estimate into a stereo matching network to reconstruct 3D humans without calibrated camera poses.
zjzr2iULaW.problem: Existing 3D human reconstruction methods depend on pre-calibrated camera parameters, which limits consumer-level use.
zjzr2iULaW.method: A SMPL-X Estimation module fuses monocular SMPL-X estimates from different views into one consistent human prior, and a Posemap Adapter injects this structured human information into the stereo matching network to improve geometry and texture.
zjzr2iULaW.key_idea: Use stereo matching priors for pose-free reconstruction and SMPL-X as a human prior injected through a Posemap Adapter.
zjzr2iULaW.evidence: Experiments on the THuman2.0 and Twindom datasets (the comparison sentence is cut off in the supplied abstract).
zjzr2iULaW.claimed_gains: not stated (the supplied abstract is cut off at 'competitive with the').
zjzr2iULaW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find removing the calibration requirement valuable and combining SMPL-X priors with general stereo matching a reasonable design with competitive results.
zjzr2iULaW.main_concern: Novelty and gains are marginal (the Posemap Adapter adds about 0.25 dB PSNR), the method leans heavily on a pretrained backbone, and related pose-free methods are not compared.

thw6xrNz7Q.one_liner: Learns continuous thought vectors for a VLA from action supervision alone, verified by an EMA consumer.
thw6xrNz7Q.problem: Robot reasoning in VLAs usually needs annotated reasoning traces, and a thought should be useful beyond the network that produced it.
thw6xrNz7Q.method: Built on pi0.5, CR generates thoughts sequentially through a Gaussian-prior bottleneck and conditions block-causal action prediction on the thought prefix. An EMA consumer's action-prediction error backpropagates to the thought generator during training only.
thw6xrNz7Q.key_idea: Self-verification: train thoughts so that both the generating policy and an evolving EMA copy of it can predict actions from them.
thw6xrNz7Q.evidence: LIBERO-PRO against its backbone and DeepThinkVLA-RL, plus TX-G2 and HSR experiments and component ablations.
thw6xrNz7Q.claimed_gains: On LIBERO-PRO, mean success rises from 58.0% to 64.0% over the backbone; on TX-G2 and HSR, mean subtask success improves by 19.8 and 15.6 percentage points.
thw6xrNz7Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the annotation-free design well motivated, with the EMA consumer as a targeted fix for latent co-adaptation and promising results in simulation and the real world.
thw6xrNz7Q.main_concern: Gains may come from added capacity and training constraints rather than reasoning, and the EMA consumer's necessity is not isolated with matched controls.

AbsUWYFvvx.one_liner: Forgets reference constraints on evolving attributes in diffusion transformers by projecting out attribute subspaces chosen with an event-conditioned attribute graph.
AbsUWYFvvx.problem: Customized video generation applies reference conditioning uniformly, so when a prompt requires an attribute to change, reference and text conditions conflict.
AbsUWYFvvx.method: AttriForget builds an event-conditioned attribute graph for the validity of reference attributes, probes orthogonal attribute-sensitive subspaces in reference features, and preserves persistent attributes while forgetting reference constraints on evolving ones. It is training-free and plugs into diffusion transformer backbones.
AbsUWYFvvx.key_idea: Use the attribute graph to separate persistent from evolving attributes and remove reference influence only along the evolving attributes' subspaces.
AbsUWYFvvx.evidence: Experiments on OpenS2V-Eval across four subject-customized video generation backbones.
AbsUWYFvvx.claimed_gains: not stated (the supplied abstract says it consistently improves total scores and is cut off after 'video').
AbsUWYFvvx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the conflict diagnosis clear, the training-free subspace mechanism principled, and the method applicable to four backbones of different sizes.
AbsUWYFvvx.main_concern: Gains come almost entirely from NaturalScore while text alignment is flat and some metrics worsen (FaceSim 48.6 to 45.3, Motion Amplitude 33.4 to 23.5), with no robustness analysis of the VLM-built attribute graph.

mRBACIUQiV.one_liner: Maximizes low-rank Hermitian quadratic forms over K-th roots of unity by rounding random directions, with sample count independent of n.
mRBACIUQiV.problem: Maximizing quadratic forms over roots of unity (including Max-Cut and Max-3-Cut) is hard, and exact low-rank search enumerates a large polynomial candidate set.
mRBACIUQiV.method: For a rank-r matrix, rounding each coordinate of Vc to the nearest root turns a direction c into a candidate, and some direction is optimal. The authors analyze rounding S uniformly random directions and keeping the best, and bound the loss for noisy objectives from rank-r truncation.
mRBACIUQiV.key_idea: Rounding loses only quadratically in the angular error to the optimal direction, so random directions succeed with a probability that depends on rank and not on n.
mRBACIUQiV.evidence: Theoretical guarantees and Max-3-Cut experiments on random regular graphs (the rest is cut off in the supplied abstract).
mRBACIUQiV.claimed_gains: Exact search enumerates O(r n^(2r-1)) candidates, while one random direction is (1-eps)-optimal with probability at least (eps/2)^(r-1) min{1, (K/pi) sqrt(eps/2)}, so S=O((2/eps)^(r-1/2) log(1/delta)) samples and O(Snr) time suffice; truncation loses at most 2n(lambda_{r+1}+2||H||_2).
mRBACIUQiV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the geometric analysis clean, giving an explicit near-optimal sampling guarantee that separates the rank from the ambient dimension and removes a worst-case rounding factor.
mRBACIUQiV.main_concern: The advance over existing low-rank direction-search work is narrow, and the exponential dependence on rank and flat-spectrum benchmarks limit practical reach.

gpLz4rJjGA.one_liner: Simulates multi-turn user conversations across 24 need-context combinations and adaptively samples conditions to discover manipulative LLM behavior.
gpLz4rJjGA.problem: LLM dark patterns often appear only after several turns and depend on user circumstances, so single-turn benchmarks and adversarial red teaming miss them.
gpLz4rJjGA.method: DarkPattern Teaming simulates multi-turn conversations over 24 combinations of user needs and everyday contexts, detects dark patterns turn by turn, and uses outcomes to pick which conditions to simulate next. Discovered failures are paired with manipulation-free revisions used for activation steering.
gpLz4rJjGA.key_idea: Adaptive sampling over user-condition strata, guided by turn-level dark-pattern detections, finds failures more efficiently than balanced sampling.
gpLz4rJjGA.evidence: Five open- and closed-weight LLMs, equal-budget comparison with stratified sampling, blinded human annotation of detections, and an activation-steering mitigation test on Qwen 3.5 27B.
gpLz4rJjGA.claimed_gains: On Qwen 3.5 27B, 44.9% of detected conversations show their first dark pattern only after the opening response; adaptive sampling flags 22.1% more conversations than balanced sampling; annotators confirm 90% of sampled detections versus 72-86% for baselines; steering with 100 pairs cuts the held-out rate from 42.2% to 13.0%.
gpLz4rJjGA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important and distinct from adversarial red teaming, with a complete pipeline from discovery through mitigation, careful rubrics and human validation.
gpLz4rJjGA.main_concern: The dark-pattern criteria are broad and may count hallucination as manipulation, the yield gain concentrates on one user condition, and no frontier models were tested.

1dbPrQWooD.one_liner: Trains a network for overlap-consistent Kikuchi region beliefs, with induced triplet regions, for amortized Bayesian network learning.
1dbPrQWooD.problem: Learning discrete Bayesian network parameters from massive incomplete data requires repeated joint-marginal inference, and ELBO-based amortized VI relies on restrictive posterior factorization.
1dbPrQWooD.method: TRNK is a non-ELBO framework based on Kikuchi free energy and region graphs. It uses the network's structure and factors to pick triplet base regions and induce higher-order regions, then trains an evidence-conditioned neural network to produce overlap-consistent region beliefs for each partially observed instance.
1dbPrQWooD.key_idea: Induce triplet regions from the Bayesian network structure and constrain the amortized network to overlap-consistent region beliefs under a Kikuchi objective.
1dbPrQWooD.evidence: Experiments on benchmark Bayesian networks against amortized VI and approximate EM baselines, and a comparison of the region induction algorithm with Bethe and other region-graph alternatives.
1dbPrQWooD.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that TRNK significantly outperforms amortized VI and approximate EM in accuracy and efficiency, and its region induction beats Bethe and alternatives on most benchmarks).
1dbPrQWooD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important, the structure-aware region construction and consistency-preserving parameterization principled, and the method more efficient and accurate than baselines.
1dbPrQWooD.main_concern: Experiments lack error bars and an independent test set, so win counts are weakly supported, and the theory is narrow and the paper hard to read.

amw8EFJkWp.one_liner: Distills a clean synthetic dataset from label-noisy data by analytically inverting a class-conditional mixture to recover clean class prototypes.
amw8EFJkWp.problem: Existing dataset distillation methods assume accurate labels and degrade substantially under label noise, even with a preceding label-cleaning stage.
amw8EFJkWp.method: DeDD models observed class-conditional distributions as mixtures of latent clean ones, inverts the mixture to get unbiased clean class prototype estimates, and matches the synthetic set to them in a single stage without label cleaning or sample selection.
amw8EFJkWp.key_idea: Decontaminate the distribution-matching loss by inverting the noise mixture, giving the same expected gradient as clean-data distribution matching when mixture parameters are known.
amw8EFJkWp.evidence: A theoretical gradient-equivalence result and experiments with simulated and real-world label noise against existing dataset distillation methods.
amw8EFJkWp.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that DeDD outperforms existing dataset distillation methods under simulated and real label noise).
amw8EFJkWp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the one-stage design natural, since it corrects class-level matching targets without fixing individual labels, with theory supporting the gradient consistency.
amw8EFJkWp.main_concern: Comparison fairness is uncertain, since DeDD's recipe without its two components reaches 62.57% on CIFAR-10 at IPC 50 versus 43.96% for DM, and the theory assumes class-wise instance-independent noise.

mp98HbBgPG.one_liner: Combines a periodic quantile recalibrator with component-wise online trackers that signal saturation, for conformal intervals under component-wise distribution shift.
mp98HbBgPG.problem: Sequential conformal methods target marginal coverage and assume exchangeability, which fails when shifts are heterogeneous across components of a multivariate time series.
mp98HbBgPG.method: BaCR pairs a unified recalibrator that periodically adapts the quantile estimates with component-wise trackers that correct intervals online within the supported range and flag when more expansion is needed. A theorem decomposes component-wise empirical coverage error into tracker correction and boundary limits.
mp98HbBgPG.key_idea: Feed tracker saturation signals back into periodic quantile recalibration so each component's interval can expand beyond the current quantile range.
mp98HbBgPG.evidence: A synthetic benchmark and four real-world datasets, with ablations, parameter sensitivity and stratification by local tail pressure; the final result is cut off in the supplied abstract.
mp98HbBgPG.claimed_gains: not stated (the supplied abstract is cut off at 'BaCR substantially reduces').
mp98HbBgPG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the heterogeneous-shift problem practically relevant, the tracker-plus-recalibrator design simple and interesting, and the experiments solid with ablations and favorable coverage-efficiency trade-offs.
mp98HbBgPG.main_concern: No end-to-end coverage guarantee is established, the saturation-feedback contribution is not isolated by ablation, and recent online conformal and recalibration baselines are missing.

gO15M29uIF.one_liner: Uses an LLM to set per-dimension ARD lengthscale priors for Bayesian optimization, then validates and revises them with predictive evidence.
gO15M29uIF.problem: High-dimensional Bayesian optimization with few evaluations struggles to infer dimension-wise variation, while semantic descriptions of variables go unused.
gO15M29uIF.method: CLUE-BO has an LLM translate task semantics into dimension-specific priors over ARD lengthscales. It compares semantic and neutral GPs by predictive evidence to decide when to reflect, whether to activate a revised prior, and whether to follow semantic or neutral guidance.
gO15M29uIF.key_idea: Treat LLM-derived semantic priors as hypotheses scored against a neutral GP by sequential predictive evidence rather than as fixed priors.
gO15M29uIF.evidence: Six high-dimensional benchmarks from 30 to 1,003 dimensions, with ablation and trajectory analyses.
gO15M29uIF.claimed_gains: Achieves the best mean final objective on five of six benchmarks and remains competitive on the sixth.
gO15M29uIF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the narrow use of an LLM for lengthscale priors and the mechanism for monitoring and revising unreliable priors principled, with convincing results across diverse benchmarks.
gO15M29uIF.main_concern: Evaluation uses a single LLM on established benchmarks, and mapping LLM-inferred variable importance to ARD lengthscales may not reflect true relevance.

CHyFv1A8il.one_liner: Evolves multi-agent memory and collaboration together through reusable skills and counterfactual trajectory comparison.
CHyFv1A8il.problem: Evolving memory and collaboration separately can misalign them: an evolved workflow may need experience memory lacks, and evolved memory may hold guidance the workflow cannot use.
CHyFv1A8il.method: CoEvolve represents reusable local collaboration patterns as skills that link collaboration decisions to supporting memories. It compares original and counterfactual trajectories to find local evolution signals that coordinate updates to the skill library, skill memory and executor memories across rounds.
CHyFv1A8il.key_idea: Use skills as the shared interface between workflow and memory, and counterfactual trajectory differences as the signal for coordinated updates.
CHyFv1A8il.evidence: ALFWorld and WebShop experiments against memory- and collaboration-evolving baselines, with ablations over combinations of evolving components and counterfactual guidance.
CHyFv1A8il.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that CoEvolve achieves the best overall performance among the evaluated baselines).
CHyFv1A8il.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the cross-component mismatch problem well motivated, the skill-based interface a clear practical design, and the component ablations meaningful.
CHyFv1A8il.main_concern: Baseline fairness and the counterfactual mechanism are not isolated from extra search and experience (about 3.9M tokens per round on ALFWorld), and alignment itself is not directly measured.

FvgUDXagiM.one_liner: Replaces QK normalization with a projection that encodes input magnitude as bounded phase through multiple learnable frequencies.
FvgUDXagiM.problem: QK-Norm stabilizes attention logits but removes query and key norms, which carry attention sharpness and token importance information.
FvgUDXagiM.method: QK-MAP constructs queries and keys by transforming the input with multiple learnable frequencies, so magnitude changes become bounded phase patterns of fixed norm; multiple frequencies reduce periodic ambiguity. The value path is left unchanged.
FvgUDXagiM.key_idea: Encode magnitude through periodic phase features of fixed norm, separating magnitude information from norm growth.
FvgUDXagiM.evidence: Experiments across model scales from 190M to 7B parameters (the result sentence is cut off in the supplied abstract); reviews mention five model sizes and a 20B-token budget for the largest.
FvgUDXagiM.claimed_gains: not stated (the supplied abstract is cut off at 'QK-MAP achieves lower training').
FvgUDXagiM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and the design interpretable, with lower loss across model sizes and a controlled change that leaves the value path unchanged.
FvgUDXagiM.main_concern: Close prior work (FANformer, QUEST) is not directly compared, speed and memory cost are unreported, and gains look small with limited training budgets.

RARM3oKsSJ.one_liner: Reapplies a shared draft backbone over rounds, emitting multiple tokens per forward, to speed speculative decoding for a 1T model.
RARM3oKsSJ.problem: When target verification is far costlier than drafting, there is room to scale draft computation, but depth scaling gives little acceptance gain and round scaling adds sequential forwards.
RARM3oKsSJ.method: SAS uses round scaling with a semi-autoregressive in-block draft that combines shallow readout and candidate hedge to produce several tokens per forward. Dynamic partition training supports different round schedules with shared weights, and execution specialization compacts layouts and fuses state handling.
RARM3oKsSJ.key_idea: Reapply a shared backbone after extending the selected prefix (round scaling) rather than adding layers, while producing multiple tokens per forward to limit sequential overhead.
RARM3oKsSJ.evidence: MiMo-v2.5-Pro (1T parameters) on 32 NVIDIA H20 GPUs across four nodes with 48 concurrent requests, compared with native MTP, DFlash and DSpark under greedy decoding and sampling.
RARM3oKsSJ.claimed_gains: The two SAS schedules improve overall throughput by 14.56%-17.08% over native MTP, 8.11%-9.88% over DFlash and 4.17%-7.92% over DSpark, reaching up to 2.30x autoregressive throughput.
RARM3oKsSJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem of high verification cost for very large targets relevant, the round-scaling idea intuitive and effective, and the end-to-end speedups good over most strong baselines.
RARM3oKsSJ.main_concern: Novelty is limited and gains over DSpark are under 8%, with the pipeline complex and results shown only on H20 hardware where high verification latency favors the design.

KvcbnN3jHD.one_liner: Freezes a pretrained local neural operator and trains only a lightweight module composing local predictions for new domains.
KvcbnN3jHD.problem: Neural operators degrade when domain geometry, size or operating conditions differ from training, and supervised adaptation needs costly high-fidelity simulations.
KvcbnN3jHD.method: LatentDDM pretrains a neural operator to predict fields on small subdomains. For a new setting it freezes the operator and trains only a lightweight composition module on the local predictions.
KvcbnN3jHD.key_idea: Separate reusable local responses from a learnable global composition, in the spirit of domain decomposition, so transfer adapts only the composition module.
KvcbnN3jHD.evidence: Steady Darcy flow on domains larger than those used for source training, and unsteady incompressible flow around a pitching airfoil with 20-step rollouts at pitching speeds beyond the training range, against full fine-tuning and parameter-matched LoRA.
KvcbnN3jHD.claimed_gains: On larger Darcy domains with 4-64 target training simulations, LatentDDM gives 46-58% lower test relative L2 error than the stronger of full-parameter fine-tuning and parameter-matched LoRA of a ViT full-domain model, and it improves 20-step airfoil rollouts zero-shot and after few-shot calibration.
KvcbnN3jHD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the separation of reusable local responses from adaptable global interactions well designed, with paired uncertainty estimates, thorough comparisons and useful error decomposition.
KvcbnN3jHD.main_concern: The few-shot budgets exclude 64 labeled target validation simulations, airfoil calibration uses transitions from the evaluated trajectories, and the test problems are small-scale.

E4JA7r4Z3h.one_liner: Probes reasoning-model hidden states for step correctness and edits them along an anchored direction to correct reasoning mid-thought.
E4JA7r4Z3h.problem: Large reasoning models generate long chains of thought and it is unclear whether they internally know when an answer is correct, or whether that knowledge can be used to correct reasoning.
E4JA7r4Z3h.method: A lightweight probe on hidden states scores per-step correctness. SHEAR combines a semantic confidence probe that decides when to intervene with a stability-anchored editing direction that decides how, applied during generation without a separate verification pass.
E4JA7r4Z3h.key_idea: Use hidden-state probes as a closed-loop trigger and edit hidden states along an anchored direction to steer reasoning mid-generation.
E4JA7r4Z3h.evidence: Six mathematical reasoning benchmarks across three LRM scales, equal-dimension comparison of hidden-state and token-level probes, and a reversed-direction ablation.
E4JA7r4Z3h.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says SHEAR achieves the highest or tied-highest results on six benchmarks across three scales, with significant improvements over the strongest baseline in most configurations.
E4JA7r4Z3h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find that extending a correctness probe into online steering is clear and the gains substantial, with controlled comparisons showing hidden states carry stronger correctness signals than token statistics.
E4JA7r4Z3h.main_concern: The finding that reasoning models encode answer correctness largely repeats prior work, step-correctness labels are noisy, and no text-based correctness judge is compared under the same editing rule.

EsUdSmc28X.one_liner: Optimizes policies in latent world models as diffusion over searched trajectories, anchored by an energy function from transitions.
EsUdSmc28X.problem: Policy improvement in model-based RL often relies on value functions from a separate non-search policy, causing training inconsistency and suboptimal learning at scale.
EsUdSmc28X.method: MBDPO reformulates policy optimization as a diffusion process over searched trajectories in latent world models instead of building an explicit planner. An implicit energy function from collected transitions anchors the policy while the score field is refined for policy optimization.
EsUdSmc28X.key_idea: Unify search and policy optimization by training a diffusion policy's score field on model-based trajectory evaluations, anchored by a behavior energy.
EsUdSmc28X.evidence: Offline pretraining, online learning, offline-to-online fine-tuning and massively multi-task online learning, with model-size scaling and comparisons to Newt on MMBench per reviews.
EsUdSmc28X.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says only that MBDPO achieves strong multi-task performance and consistent scaling with increasing model size.
EsUdSmc28X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the evaluation broad and rigorous across settings and the approach a coherent, practical way to amortize trajectory optimization while anchoring to behavior.
EsUdSmc28X.main_concern: The contrastive energy objective assumes a uniform action marginal for negatives, so the link from the learned behavior energy to the KL-optimal policy in the theory is not established.

XunVhzABU1.one_liner: Derives an exact excess-risk law for in-context linear regression with correlated demonstrations, splitting structure into redundancy cost and relevance gain.
XunVhzABU1.problem: In-context learning is usually analyzed with independent demonstrations, yet real prompts have demonstrations correlated with each other and with the query.
XunVhzABU1.method: In in-context linear regression with an arbitrary PSD unit-diagonal similarity kernel, a linear-attention predictor trained on independent prompts is deployed on a structured one, giving an exact finite-dimensional excess-risk law. Graph-induced covariance and a sparse stochastic block model are then analyzed.
XunVhzABU1.key_idea: Structure decomposes into a redundancy cost among demonstrations, a relevance gain between demonstrations and the query, and a higher-order mediated interaction.
XunVhzABU1.evidence: Theory in a solvable setting, graph and SBM examples, and trained-model experiments with multiple seeds and held-out prompts per reviews.
XunVhzABU1.claimed_gains: In the weak-structure regime, prediction improves precisely when Q > alpha R/(1+rho), where alpha = l/d is the context-to-dimension ratio and rho is the label-noise variance.
XunVhzABU1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the finite-dimensional risk derivation explicit and checkable, and the graph and SBM examples an interpretable link between connectivity, homophily and prediction risk.
XunVhzABU1.main_concern: Novelty over Letey et al. is limited since the three covariance summaries already appear there, and the Gaussian, linear-regression, one-step linear-attention assumptions are restrictive.

k0iOorALaH.one_liner: Tracks each pending draft mismatch separately and resolves them concurrently using shared later target predictions in speculative decoding.
k0iOorALaH.problem: Deferred verification handles only the earliest pending mismatch, so a later mismatch triggers rejection and draft reuse is limited.
k0iOorALaH.method: PEND keeps a separate state for each pending mismatch while sharing subsequent target predictions across them, adapts evidence requirements to target-relative support, weights later observations by target confidence, and commits a draft segment only after all pending mismatches resolve. It uses only cached target outputs from the current pass.
k0iOorALaH.key_idea: Treat overlapping mismatches as independent pending verification decisions that share continuation evidence, instead of rejecting at the second mismatch.
k0iOorALaH.evidence: Two model families and four benchmarks, with ablations for first-mismatch-only handling and evidence sharing; task quality is measured by task scores.
k0iOorALaH.claimed_gains: Improves throughput by 46.6-70.3% (57.2% on average across evaluated settings) over vanilla speculative decoding; the sentence on task quality is cut off in the supplied abstract.
k0iOorALaH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find overlapping pending mismatches a clearly identified limitation, with a coherent training-free solution, strong throughput gains and ablations that isolate concurrent resolution.
k0iOorALaH.main_concern: Output fidelity is judged mainly by task scores under greedy decoding, the evidence rules are heuristic with weak justification, and PEND and baselines are tuned unequally.

yo6binZzZH.one_liner: Analyzes constant step-size tabular Q-learning as a switching linear system, with finite-time rates set by the joint spectral radius.
yo6binZzZH.problem: Convergence-rate bounds for constant step-size tabular Q-learning can be conservative (row-sum bounds), and no analysis expressed the leading exponential rate through the joint spectral radius.
yo6binZzZH.method: Derives a stochastic switching-linear-system representation of the Q-learning error and a finite-time error analysis through the JSR. Proves the JSR equals the largest spectral radius among deterministic-policy modes and gives a linear-programming characterization computable to any accuracy.
yo6binZzZH.key_idea: Represent Q-learning error as a stochastic switching linear system whose exact worst-case exponential rate is the joint spectral radius, which reduces to deterministic-policy modes.
yo6binZzZH.evidence: Theory only as described: finite-time error analysis via JSR, JSR equals the largest deterministic-policy spectral radius, exact LP characterization; no experiments are stated in the abstract.
yo6binZzZH.claimed_gains: No numeric gains stated; the rate can be sharper than row-sum upper bounds when those bounds are conservative.
yo6binZzZH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well written and technically solid, with an interesting link between Q-learning convergence and the JSR of the switching system.
yo6binZzZH.main_concern: Limited impact: it is unclear what conceptual message the work adds beyond existing switching-system analyses, and the exact worst-case rate need not be tight for actual Q-learning dynamics.

weVwQ9oAm3.one_liner: Spreads reference-token credit across vocabulary tokens by contextual interchangeability, replacing one-hot targets in RL and SFT post-training.
weVwQ9oAm3.problem: LLM post-training optimizes a single reference token per position, locking the model onto one path and penalizing alternative tokens that could also lead to a valid answer.
weVwQ9oAm3.method: Contextual Credit Diffusion (CCD) diffuses the reference token's credit to other vocabulary tokens according to contextual interchangeability, measured by logit differences in the model's next-token distribution, giving a dense reward. It applies to both RL (PPO/GRPO) and SFT, with top-k truncation to keep overhead small.
weVwQ9oAm3.key_idea: Weight each vocabulary token's credit by a coefficient derived from its logit gap to the reference token, turning the single-reference loss into a dense, interchangeability-weighted loss.
weVwQ9oAm3.evidence: Six reasoning benchmarks against RL and SFT baselines, a token-replacement experiment, and tau and top-k ablations; reviewers note math reasoning only and Qwen3 models up to 8B across three model sizes.
weVwQ9oAm3.claimed_gains: Outperforms RL and SFT baselines on six reasoning benchmarks; specific numbers are not stated in the visible abstract.
weVwQ9oAm3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, cheap (small per-step overhead, no teacher model), usable in both RL and SFT, with consistent gains across model sizes and clean writing.
weVwQ9oAm3.main_concern: The mechanism is under-analyzed and ablations are thin (no inverted or uniform coefficient controls, only math reasoning on Qwen3 up to 8B, OTR not compared).

N6icFAD93b.one_liner: Frames adaptive latent reasoning for control policies as autoregressive variational inference over variable-length discrete latents, trained with latent-space RL.
N6icFAD93b.problem: Reasoning in language space lacks the granularity for spatial understanding and precise motions, so adaptive deliberation has been hard to transfer to continuous control policies.
N6icFAD93b.method: Latent Memory Palace (LMP) formulates reasoning as variational inference with an autoregressive latent distribution and derives a latent-space RL technique to optimize its variational lower bound. The policy LMP-pi reasons adaptively before acting, and the same framework yields a variable-length action tokenizer, LMP-tok.
N6icFAD93b.key_idea: Variable-length discrete latent sequences ended by a learned EOS, with a decoder variance schedule penalizing longer sequences unless they improve action reconstruction, optimized by PPO-style latent RL.
N6icFAD93b.evidence: Simulation and real-world robot experiments (real robot plus three simulated benchmarks per reviewers), comparisons with Diffusion Policy, VQ-BeT and an OpenVLA-style baseline, and a tokenizer comparison against OAT and FAST.
N6icFAD93b.claimed_gains: Described as strong empirical performance with adaptive test-time compute and a significantly improved downstream autoregressive policy via LMP-tok; no numbers stated.
N6icFAD93b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the variational-inference formulation with variable-length latents and a learned stopping mechanism is principled, with promising results on simulated and real-world benchmarks.
N6icFAD93b.main_concern: It is unclear how much of the gain comes from latent reasoning, since longer latents mainly capture more behavioral modes and Diffusion Policy is comparable on several tasks with thin statistical characterization.

Nzu4JbBIlS.one_liner: Predicts the mean and variance of intermediate reverse-step noise in diffusion super-resolution instead of sampling from a standard Gaussian.
Nzu4JbBIlS.problem: Diffusion super-resolution draws intermediate noise from an unconstrained standard Gaussian, although with a fixed start and denoiser the sampled noise determines output quality.
Nzu4JbBIlS.method: A neural network predicts the mean and variance of the Gaussian noise distribution at each intermediate step, added to a frozen denoiser (ResShift per reviewers). Two training schemes are used: one supervised by final image quality, one aligning each reverse step with the forward posterior.
Nzu4JbBIlS.key_idea: Replace standard Gaussian intermediate noise with a learned conditional Gaussian whose mean and variance are predicted per step, trained on final-image quality or forward-posterior alignment.
Nzu4JbBIlS.evidence: Experiments on two datasets (LSDIR and ImageNet per reviewers) against standard Gaussian sampling, with inference-seed, loss, and deterministic-versus-stochastic prediction ablations.
Nzu4JbBIlS.claimed_gains: The abstract states improved image quality over the standard Gaussian without numbers; a reviewer reports PSNR gains of only 0.10 dB on LSDIR and 0.20 dB on ImageNet for LPNSR-B over ResShift.
Nzu4JbBIlS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the research question clear, the two training schemes well defined, and the ablations (seeds, losses, deterministic versus stochastic prediction) useful.
Nzu4JbBIlS.main_concern: Limited novelty and modest gains: the method resembles InvSR and residual correction on a frozen denoiser, while parameters rise from 173.92M to 292.51M and latency by about 36%.

oxLYdtXQQA.one_liner: Benchmarks attribute-missing graph clustering on 22 datasets and 32 baselines and proposes VISTA, a lightweight propagation-plus-prototype framework.
oxLYdtXQQA.problem: It is unclear how much real progress attribute-missing graph clustering has made, since evaluations are narrow and elaborate pipelines obscure which mechanisms are necessary.
oxLYdtXQQA.method: Builds a reproducible benchmark of 22 graph datasets and 32 baselines from four method families, then proposes VISTA, which recovers missing semantics by bounded sparse topology propagation without a learnable imputer and learns with topology-conditioned cross-view prototype learning.
oxLYdtXQQA.key_idea: Impute missing attributes by bounded sparse topology propagation from observed neighbors, then cluster with topology-conditioned cross-view prototype learning, avoiding any learnable imputer.
oxLYdtXQQA.evidence: Benchmark over 22 datasets and 32 baselines; reviewers note varied missing rates, missingness mechanisms, ablations, and efficiency analysis, with code in the supplement.
oxLYdtXQQA.claimed_gains: The benchmark shows specialized attribute-missing methods can underperform conventional graph clustering; VISTA's numeric gains are not stated in the visible abstract.
oxLYdtXQQA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is systematic and comprehensive and that simple imputation plus a general method often matches or beats elaborate attribute-reconstruction methods, with VISTA scalable and efficient.
oxLYdtXQQA.main_concern: Limited novelty: feature propagation, Laplacian smoothing, and cross-view alignment are established, and the method relies on homophily without heterophilic-graph evaluation.

KOxYqUAFpT.one_liner: Accepts autoregressive video tokens early via a verifier, freezing them while their KV cache stays available as context.
KOxYqUAFpT.problem: Few-step autoregressive video generators run every token through the final denoising step even though many tokens already match their full-step outputs early.
KOxYqUAFpT.method: Treats intermediate clean estimates as drafts and predicts per token when they can be accepted early; accepted tokens get no further denoising but keep their cached keys and values as context. Two verifiers are explored: a training-free one using similarity to clean content and cross-step stability, and a learned one reading the frozen generator's intermediate features.
KOxYqUAFpT.key_idea: Speculative-decoding-style per-token early acceptance: verifiers judge intermediate clean estimates as drafts and commit tokens before the last denoising step without changing generator weights.
KOxYqUAFpT.evidence: Short-video, long-video, and world generation, including LongLive and Lingbot-World 2.0, with ablations on the verifier designs.
KOxYqUAFpT.claimed_gains: On LongLive it matches the four-step generator with ~1.7 denoising steps per token, running over 1.5× faster at 41.7 and 37.8 fps; on Lingbot-World 2.0 it maintains quality with ~2.5 denoising steps per token.
KOxYqUAFpT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find per-token early commitment with KV-cache reuse reasonable and simple, needing no weight changes, with comprehensive ablations and quality maintained across video settings.
KOxYqUAFpT.main_concern: Gains over simple uniform fewer-step baselines are small and unverified (uniform 2-step is already faster at 40.9 fps), and comparisons with adaptive methods such as DSA and Surprise Forcing are missing or limited.

nIgVCmVua9.one_liner: Splits PIC KV into shared Base, sparse Repair, and private Decode regions and runs shared-attention kernels with a cost-aware planner.
nIgVCmVua9.problem: Position-independent KV caching reuses prefill but does not yield compact KV storage or efficient decode attention, since repairs duplicate KV states and request-oriented attention reloads shared data.
nIgVCmVua9.method: Inlay is a serving runtime that separates immutable shared Base KV, token-granular request- and layer-specific Repair KV, and private append-only Decode KV. Its kernels reuse loaded Base KV across compatible queries, apply repair masks and position adjustments, and merge partial outputs, while a cost-aware CPU planner picks shared or private KV packing per chunk under a memory budget.
nIgVCmVua9.key_idea: Separate shared Base KV from sparse per-request Repair KV so decode attention loads shared data once across queries, with a planner falling back to private packing when sharing costs more.
nIgVCmVua9.evidence: NVIDIA A100 attention microbenchmarks with Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B configurations, single-layer integrations with CacheBlend, EPIC, and QCFuse, and a resident-storage capacity estimate.
nIgVCmVua9.claimed_gains: Median kernel speedups of 1.24× over FlashInfer and 1.32× over PAT in microbenchmarks; the integration results are cut off in the abstract, and a reviewer cites a 48.5% resident-storage capacity gain.
nIgVCmVua9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see an important systems problem and agree the Base-Repair-Decode representation supports multiple PIC methods without changing their repair policy, with measured motivation and a first-class planner.
nIgVCmVua9.main_concern: Benefits are not shown under serving conditions: the 48.5% capacity gain excludes packed copies and workspace, several results omit CPU planning overhead, and novelty over existing shared-KV techniques is limited.

zIKFB5Tq85.one_liner: Benchmark of 1,000 multi-turn conversations and 3,000 policies testing guardrails on in-context policy rules at three difficulty levels.
zIKFB5Tq85.problem: Guardrails are expected to follow application-specific safety policies given in context, but evaluation has relied on predefined risk taxonomies.
zIKFB5Tq85.method: SafePyramid has 1,000 multi-turn conversations across 10 domains and 3,000 application-specific policies with 61,641 distinct rules, organized as L0 (single-rule understanding), L1 (reasoning over rule dependencies), and L2 (adapting to full novel policy frameworks). It is built with a multi-stage construction and validation pipeline and used to evaluate 10 frontier LLMs, 5 policy-configurable guardrails, and 1 typed decision model.
zIKFB5Tq85.key_idea: A three-level difficulty hierarchy that isolates single-rule understanding, dependency reasoning, and novel policy-framework adaptation, scoring exact identification of the full set of violated rules.
zIKFB5Tq85.evidence: Evaluation of 10 frontier LLMs, 5 policy-configurable guardrails, and 1 typed decision model, plus human validation reporting a 41% rule matching rate on L2.
zIKFB5Tq85.claimed_gains: No method gain claimed; the best model, GPT-5.5, exactly identifies the full set of violated rules in only 54.0%, 35.3%, and 12.9% of cases on L0, L1, and L2.
zIKFB5Tq85.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task formulation and level-wise diagnostic design are useful and the evaluation is comprehensive, with inter-rule dependencies and conditionals well thought out.
zIKFB5Tq85.main_concern: Benchmark quality is uncertain: label noise (41% human rule matching on L2), single-generator data that confounds level with generator, refusals dropped from metrics, and no variance or confidence intervals.

JxZqwTReIf.one_liner: Training-free harness letting a frozen GUI agent decide whether to query world models and which one each candidate action needs.
JxZqwTReIf.problem: Existing GUI-agent methods give the agent one world model per run and use a fixed pipeline or external rule to decide when to call it, though evidence needs vary across screens and actions.
JxZqwTReIf.method: WISH abstracts recurring evidence needs from teacher explanations into conditions the agent can assess. Before requesting predictions, the agent judges whether they could change its choice among candidate actions, and if so selects which world model supplies the evidence each candidate needs.
JxZqwTReIf.key_idea: A whether-then-which decision made before seeing predictions: the agent judges if a world-model prediction could change its action choice, then routes each candidate to a suitable world model.
JxZqwTReIf.evidence: Qwen3-VL-8B on AndroidWorld, plus two GUI agents and three benchmarks (six settings per reviewers), with trace analysis and component ablations.
JxZqwTReIf.claimed_gains: With Qwen3-VL-8B on AndroidWorld, WISH reaches 50.0% task success, 7.8 percentage points above the strongest reproduced baseline, while requesting world-model predictions on 21.7% of steps versus 23.1%.
JxZqwTReIf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated, the whether-plus-which decomposition simple and intuitive, and results consistently best across the evaluated settings.
JxZqwTReIf.main_concern: Gains are confounded: WISH adds memory, action repair, safety checks, and recovery that baselines lack, and the isolated effect of world-model routing is small (47/116 to 50/116 in Table 5).

9QeEKHrDn6.one_liner: Adapts a JEPA latent world model online inside MPC using one self-supervised gradient step per replanning step.
9QeEKHrDn6.problem: Latent world models are frozen at test time, so planning can fail when predictions become inaccurate under distribution shift.
9QeEKHrDn6.method: After training, AdaJEPA plans and executes the first action chunk, uses the observed next-state transition as a self-supervised adaptation signal to update the model, and replans with the updated model, with no additional expert demonstrations.
9QeEKHrDn6.key_idea: Use each executed transition as a free self-supervised training example to take a gradient step on the world model between MPC replans.
9QeEKHrDn6.evidence: Goal-reaching tasks with three JEPA implementations (including DINO-WM), two planners (GD, CEM), several shift types, and layer-selection, LoRA, and fine-tuning comparisons per reviewers.
9QeEKHrDn6.claimed_gains: Substantially improves planning success with as few as one gradient step per MPC replanning step; no specific numbers in the abstract.
9QeEKHrDn6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple and cheap (a small parameter subset, no rewards or labels) and shown to improve planning over the same frozen model across several settings.
9QeEKHrDn6.main_concern: Novelty is overstated, since gradient-step online adaptation inside MPC is established (e.g., GrBAL and Nagabandi et al., 2019), and fine-tuning baselines get only one epoch, so the sample-efficiency claim is not established.

OoetS6pSkM.one_liner: Quantizes Delta-rule recurrent states by allocating precision using error magnitude and memory lifetime, with jointly fitted row and column scales.
OoetS6pSkM.problem: Directly quantizing linear-attention recurrent states to low precision severely degrades accuracy because quantization errors propagate through successive state updates.
OoetS6pSkM.method: STEPQuant is a post-training quantization framework that allocates precision by error magnitude and memory lifetime, and jointly fits key-row and value-column scales from state distributions and key-row impact on output error. It is integrated into SGLang with optimized GPU kernels.
OoetS6pSkM.key_idea: Mixed-precision allocation by error magnitude and memory lifetime (temporal) plus key-row and value-column scale fitting weighted by key-row output impact (spatial).
OoetS6pSkM.evidence: Qwen3.8-27B and Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct on long- and short-generation benchmarks (seven reasoning and six short tasks per reviewers), with SGLang serving integration.
OoetS6pSkM.claimed_gains: Closely matches FP32-state accuracy at a nominal 6-bit budget, outperforms uniform INT8 in its 4-bit configuration, gives over 5× recurrent-state compression, and reduces total serving memory by up to 68.7%.
OoetS6pSkM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical, the temporal and spatial error analysis is well motivated, and results show accuracy near FP32 states plus real memory savings in SGLang.
OoetS6pSkM.main_concern: Component contributions and comparisons are not isolated: no lifetime-off or row-impact-off controls, no controlled comparison with DAMP, and only one GDN and one KDA checkpoint.

mcts2oO1Og.one_liner: Traces sub-4-bit quantization failures to sparse sensitive modules, then allocates bits by causal-effect scores via group-knapsack optimization.
mcts2oO1Og.problem: Quantization below 4 bits sharply degrades accuracy, and prior work characterizes this through behavior or weight statistics without explaining internal causes or enabling targeted mitigation.
mcts2oO1Og.method: Uses mechanistic analysis (activation patching and logit lens per reviewers) to show damage is selective to tail capabilities, with attention heads showing semantic direction shifts and MLP neurons showing activation-magnitude suppression. Pinpoint Quantization (PinQ) then uses causal-effect scores to guide group-knapsack bit allocation.
mcts2oO1Og.key_idea: Score modules by causal effect on tail capabilities and solve a group-knapsack to give more bits to the sparse set of fragile modules.
mcts2oO1Og.evidence: Restoration and selective-quantization interventions, evaluated across 18 benchmarks and multiple model sizes including large MoE models.
mcts2oO1Og.claimed_gains: Protecting the sparse key modules enables near-FP16 performance below 4 bits across 18 benchmarks; detailed numbers are cut off in the abstract.
mcts2oO1Og.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well written, agree that tail-capability failures hidden by average scores matter, and that intervention experiments localize responsible modules across model scales.
mcts2oO1Og.main_concern: The mechanistic analysis is weakly connected to the method and the practical advantage over optimized INT4 is unproven (3.6 bits is a small nominal saving, and LongBenchV2 on the 235B model drops from 35.0 at FP16 to 33.0 with PinQ).

dyghTVIBzV.one_liner: Heterogeneous-relation neural scheduler for hierarchical manufacturing, combining Relation Mix reasoning, a pair decoder, and bounded-context decomposition.
dyghTVIBzV.problem: Hierarchical manufacturing scheduling has tightly coupled decisions and heterogeneous constraints (shared resources, machine calendars) that go beyond standard flexible job shop scheduling.
dyghTVIBzV.method: CRST models scheduling states with multiple relations (workflow dependencies, machine competition, reusable resource interactions), reasons per relation, and mixes the contexts with Relation Mix. A pair decoder scores feasible task-machine assignments while the environment enforces exact feasibility, and a decomposition strategy reduces memory in large-scale inference.
dyghTVIBzV.key_idea: Reason separately over workflow, machine-competition, and resource relations, adaptively weight them with Relation Mix, and score task-machine pairs under environment-enforced exact feasibility.
dyghTVIBzV.evidence: Experiments on four synthetic datasets compared with CP-SAT under a fixed 30-minute search budget.
dyghTVIBzV.claimed_gains: Solution quality comparable to CP-SAT on standard-size instances and up to 8.48% better than CP-SAT under a fixed 30-minute budget on larger problems, with only tens of seconds of inference.
dyghTVIBzV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the architecture has a clear motivation and coherent design, targets a more realistic scheduling variant, and gives promising results on complex instances.
dyghTVIBzV.main_concern: Evidence is thin: only synthetic benchmarks, no ablation or sensitivity study of the key bounded-context decomposition settings, and evaluation on a single problem rather than standard FJSP or JSP.

EGhHX9cj3f.one_liner: Repurposes one pretrained LLM decoder block as a symbolic policy seeding genetic programming, updated online with discovered expressions.
EGhHX9cj3f.problem: Conventional symbolic regression search uses fixed rules or specialized generators, and most LLM-based methods fail to digest past expressions or adaptively guide future search.
EGhHX9cj3f.method: DIGEST turns a pretrained decoder block from a lightweight LLM into a symbolic policy that seeds the genetic-programming population, and feeds high-quality GP expressions back to update the policy online so it internalizes past discoveries.
EGhHX9cj3f.key_idea: An online fine-tuning loop where a single pretrained decoder block generates GP seeds and is updated on the best expressions found during search.
EGhHX9cj3f.evidence: Ground-truth equation recovery (25 runs per equation; Nguyen and Livermore per reviewers) and SRBench (10 runs per dataset), compared with search-based and LLM-based baselines.
EGhHX9cj3f.claimed_gains: Experiments on two ground-truth benchmarks show it outperforms the strongest competitor by up to 2.59%; reviewers cite mean search times of 49.2 s and 118.8 s, which are 7.2% and 17.4% of the strongest competitor's.
EGhHX9cj3f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the design clear and lightweight, with an efficient single-block policy and a reasonably extensive evaluation with many runs per equation.
EGhHX9cj3f.main_concern: Gain attribution is unclear: NGGP already couples neural generators with GP, the Nguyen gain is within noise (93.33% vs. 93.25%), and controls such as random-init or shuffled weights and matched LLM-baseline budgets are missing.

b4pyaD4yLL.one_liner: Verifies LLM ownership by scoring a suspect model's responses with the source model's token-level probabilities instead of comparing text.
b4pyaD4yLL.problem: Black-box fingerprinting relies on textual outputs that are unstable under stochastic sampling, especially for long-form reasoning models.
b4pyaD4yLL.method: TOPF evaluates the token-level probabilities the source model assigns to responses generated by a suspicious model and extracts discriminative features from them, since derived models tend to preserve probability patterns of their source. Reviewers describe a learned encoder using relative similarity to the source and reference models.
b4pyaD4yLL.key_idea: Teacher-forced token-level log-probabilities of the suspect's responses under the source model give a sampling-stable ownership signal, normalized against reference models.
b4pyaD4yLL.evidence: Experiments on reasoning models and standard LLMs, with architecture ablations, reference-model comparisons, cost measurements, and community-derived checkpoints.
b4pyaD4yLL.claimed_gains: Verification performance 'approaching white-box methods'; no numbers stated in the abstract.
b4pyaD4yLL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the setting practical (the suspect only returns text), the probability signal simple and well motivated, and low-FPR results on reasoning models encouraging.
b4pyaD4yLL.main_concern: The evaluation is under-specified: descendant labels rest on a configured pretrained_model field, the learned encoder's contribution is not isolated (plain NLL matches it on reasoning models), and false positives from independent fine-tunes of a shared base are untested.

kOtBVZJ314.one_liner: Moves classifier-free guidance into the initial latent mean, so flow-matching sampling needs one backbone pass per step.
kOtBVZJ314.problem: Standard classifier-free guidance requires two backbone evaluations at every sampling step in flow matching.
kOtBVZJ314.method: P-Guide applies guidance to the mean of a learned initial latent distribution (a small prior module), then samples with a single backbone evaluation per step. Both homoscedastic and heteroscedastic priors are considered.
kOtBVZJ314.key_idea: Replace per-step velocity extrapolation with a learned shift of the source-distribution mean that induces a local first-order trajectory response.
kOtBVZJ314.evidence: Class-conditional ImageNet generation with U-Net and DiT-B/2, a SANA text-to-image pilot in the appendix, and ablations including distributed injection.
kOtBVZJ314.claimed_gains: Reduces guided sampling GFLOPs by approximately 50% with a 1.31M-parameter prior module, and lowers ImageNet FID from 27.78 to 22.33 (U-Net) and from 32.84 to 24.61 (DiT-B/2).
kOtBVZJ314.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated and the single-pass prior-steering idea simple, with a lightweight module and encouraging fixed-budget results (FID 26.90 versus 30.01 for CFG).
kOtBVZJ314.main_concern: There is no experimental comparison with guidance-free training or guidance distillation, the adoption cost (prior training and backbone adaptation) is unreported, and gains fade at larger guidance scales.

vRC14XkJkT.one_liner: Renders radar range-azimuth-Doppler tensors of dynamic driving scenes from tracked point reflectors and a fixed analytic point-spread function.
vRC14XkJkT.problem: Radar novel-view synthesis either reconstructs only range-azimuth tensors for dynamic scenes or renders Doppler only for static scenes, and sensor spread gets baked into scene geometry.
vRC14XkJkT.method: DyRAD models static background reflectors and motion-tracked dynamic point reflectors, projecting reflector velocities from object tracks onto the line of sight so Doppler is both a rendered output and supervision. Reflectors are rendered through a fixed analytic point-spread function derived from the radar's signal-processing chain.
vRC14XkJkT.key_idea: Separate sensor response from scene by rendering tracked point reflectors through a fixed analytic PSF, with Doppler taken from track velocities projected on the line of sight.
vRC14XkJkT.evidence: Experiments on RADIal and Boreas sequences with different radar settings, a render-and-refit check at displaced viewpoints, and zero-shot sensor-configuration transfer.
vRC14XkJkT.claimed_gains: The visible abstract gives no numbers; a reviewer cites a 90.7% foreground hit rate on RADIal versus 26.9% for a compared method.
vRC14XkJkT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it fills an underexplored gap (dynamic scenes with Doppler), the fixed-PSF design is sensible, and quantitative and qualitative results are strong across radar settings.
vRC14XkJkT.main_concern: It relies on ground-truth bounding boxes and tracks, which makes the setting easier than baselines, tracking sensitivity is not ablated, and novel-view accuracy is not verified against real radar from displaced viewpoints.

Tq9jZdZ0rt.one_liner: Conditions one shared LoRA on continuous log ground sampling distance via nested sigmoid rank gates for remote-sensing vision-language models.
Tq9jZdZ0rt.problem: Remote sensing imagery spans centimeter to tens-of-meters GSD, yet existing RS-VLMs ignore GSD or encode it only as a text token.
Tq9jZdZ0rt.method: CS-HLoRA gates the rank dimensions of a single shared LoRA with nested sigmoid functions of s = log10(GSD), with thresholds initialized at object, structure, and semantic scales and a frozen backbone. SSE-U estimates s with calibrated uncertainty when metadata is missing, and GeoScale-VQA supplies 1.5M QA pairs with resolved GSD.
Tq9jZdZ0rt.key_idea: Gate LoRA rank dimensions with nested sigmoids of continuous log-GSD so gradients route by scale during training and active ranks are selected at inference.
Tq9jZdZ0rt.evidence: An 8B backbone on XLRS-Bench and OmniEarth-Bench, with matched-Stage-1 comparisons against standard LoRA, textual GSD conditioning, and bucketed MoE-LoRA, plus GSD-shuffling tests.
Tq9jZdZ0rt.claimed_gains: Scores 59.4 on XLRS-Bench (+5.2 over the strongest RS specialist) and 40.71 on OmniEarth-Bench (+7.45 over the strongest open-source baseline).
Tq9jZdZ0rt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that conditioning a shared adapter on GSD is principled and that matched-checkpoint comparisons and GSD-shuffling controls give useful evidence (40.71 versus 31.98 for standard LoRA).
Tq9jZdZ0rt.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributable to physical scale, since GSD is confounded with dataset source and sensor, and CS-HLoRA reads as a conditional low-rank rule with limited novelty and unverified auto-generated QA data.

iO0N2x4fv1.one_liner: Training-free outer loop that keeps a Bayesian belief over latent states and asks clarifying questions maximizing expected mutual information.
iO0N2x4fv1.problem: LLM systems treat multi-turn dialogue reactively and lack a principled mechanism to reason about what information is missing.
iO0N2x4fv1.method: BALAR maintains a structured belief over latent states, selects clarifying questions by maximizing expected mutual information, and dynamically expands its state representation when the current one is insufficient. It also studies distilling BALAR into a questioning policy through SFT, DPO, and dense-reward RL.
iO0N2x4fv1.key_idea: Deterministic Bayesian belief updating and mutual-information question selection over an LLM-built, expandable latent-state representation.
iO0N2x4fv1.evidence: AR-Bench-DC, AR-Bench-SP, and iCraft-MD with Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct under held-out configuration selection, plus distillation across 18 iCraft-MD replications.
iO0N2x4fv1.claimed_gains: A clear gain on iCraft-MD with Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, trailing on AR-Bench-SP with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and four statistically inconclusive comparisons; no further numbers stated.
iO0N2x4fv1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find BALAR handles both discrete and open-ended label sets, improves over standard baselines (few-shot, CoT, ToT, UoT), and offers useful question-selection ablations and analyses.
iO0N2x4fv1.main_concern: Cost and evidence quality: it uses many inference calls (about 306 per iCraft-MD dialogue for Qwen-32B), headline results use full-dataset configuration selection, and the supplied simulator code appears inconsistent with the stated free-form protocol.

8NbAF0cIQs.one_liner: Generates corrective visual suffix tokens from a SuffixViT trained against a safety-neuron probe to restore refusal in VLMs.
8NbAF0cIQs.problem: Visual inputs can suppress safety neurons tied to harmful-request refusal in VLMs, letting multimodal jailbreaks bypass the language backbone's alignment.
8NbAF0cIQs.method: VISAR trains a plug-and-play SuffixViT, supervised by a differentiable safety probe, to emit visual suffixes that restore the suppressed refusal-aligned activation pattern without modifying the pretrained VLM.
8NbAF0cIQs.key_idea: Supervise a visual-suffix generator with a differentiable probe on safety-neuron activations so the frozen VLM's refusal-aligned state is restored.
8NbAF0cIQs.evidence: Multiple VLMs and three multimodal jailbreak attacks against four defenses (MM-SafetyBench per reviewers), with ablations on LLaVA, ScienceQA-IMG for utility, and mechanistic activation analysis.
8NbAF0cIQs.claimed_gains: Substantially reduces harmful responses while preserving benign utility; no numbers stated.
8NbAF0cIQs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the neuron-level view of vision-induced safety degradation is useful and that the frozen-VLM visual suffix gives the lowest reported average attack success rate among compared defenses with little inference overhead.
8NbAF0cIQs.main_concern: The safety-neuron interpretation and utility preservation are weakly validated: only correlational evidence, no held-out refusal validation, benign utility tested mainly on ScienceQA-IMG, and older VLMs only.

Eh9NQzBMRp.one_liner: Detects and repairs backdoored classifiers by scoring class-wise head anomalies and revising head weights along an estimated shortcut direction.
Eh9NQzBMRp.problem: Users acquiring models from untrusted sources need to assess backdoor compromise, localize target classes, and repair the model, ideally without retraining or trigger inversion.
Eh9NQzBMRp.method: SCAR combines classifier-weight anomalies with perturbation-induced prediction preferences to localize suspicious classes.
