For each class it estimates a shortcut-related feature direction from class-specific weights and feature-wise variability and selectively revises classifier-head parameters along it.
Eh9NQzBMRp.key_idea: Treat a backdoor as a trigger-to-target shortcut with weight and feature-direction signatures, then edit only the target class's head parameters along the estimated shortcut direction.
Eh9NQzBMRp.evidence: Four datasets, four architectures, ten attacks, and multiple baselines per reviewers, in a post-training setting without retraining or trigger inversion.
Eh9NQzBMRp.claimed_gains: Reported as effective across diverse datasets, attacks, and architectures; no numbers stated in the visible abstract.
Eh9NQzBMRp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the unified detection-and-repair framework practical (no retraining, trigger inversion, or labels) and the empirical evaluation broad.
Eh9NQzBMRp.main_concern: The shortcut-direction proxy is weakly justified and gains may come from suppressing target-class outputs, with clean-model and adaptive-attack experiments missing.

lTot2GNSTA.one_liner: Selects agent memories by sparse convex reconstruction of the query, using the residual to find still-missing evidence.
lTot2GNSTA.problem: Conventional memory retrieval scores and truncates memories independently, wasting context slots on redundant facts while leaving complementary evidence behind.
lTot2GNSTA.method: MemPursuit is a training-free read mechanism that composes nested evidence contexts by using the residual of a sparse convex query reconstruction as a proxy for what the selected set is missing, reusing the retrieval embeddings without any LLM or cross-encoder scoring.
lTot2GNSTA.key_idea: Greedy matching-pursuit-style selection: each memory is valued by how much it reduces the query's reconstruction residual given the evidence already selected.
lTot2GNSTA.evidence: Three benchmarks including LoCoMo, with multiple memory frameworks and budgets, plus coverage and latency analyses.
lTot2GNSTA.claimed_gains: On fixed-budget LoCoMo, end-to-end accuracy improves by 7.2 percentage points at Top-10 and 5.5 at Top-20, with a 32.9× speedup in median reranking latency over fully batched BGE-v2-m3.
lTot2GNSTA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method cheap, training-free, and easy to plug into existing memory systems, with consistent gains across frameworks and budgets and a sensible set-conditioned framing.
lTot2GNSTA.main_concern: The selector looks like a soft form of MMR, and key ablations (residual versus joint weight fitting, ridge, stopping threshold) and error bars are missing, with an LLM judge possibly inflating results.

XKRnNzdC9p.one_liner: Diagnoses four failure modes of test-time scaling and post-training in individual stance prediction using a Hacker News benchmark.
XKRnNzdC9p.problem: It is unclear whether test-time scaling and post-training gains from coding and math carry over to predicting a person's stance in a new discussion from their history.
XKRnNzdC9p.method: Builds STANCE-BENCH (2499 prediction tasks from 500 Hacker News users) and evaluates test-time scaling strategies, SFT, and RL, identifying incorrect consensus, selection failure, response overfitting, and early plateau. It then explores a simple approach combining direct scores for all candidate stances with explicit assessments of support from the individual's history, with a frozen LLM and fitted coefficients.
XKRnNzdC9p.key_idea: Combine direct scores over all candidate stances with explicit history-support assessments, with coefficients fitted on a frozen LLM, instead of sampling-based selection or training.
XKRnNzdC9p.evidence: 2499 tasks from 500 Hacker News users with a 781-task test set, Qwen3-8B, and a generation-versus-selection coverage analysis.
XKRnNzdC9p.claimed_gains: On the 781-task test set, the approach reaches 21.83 discussion-specific Macro F1 with Qwen3-8B versus 19.27 for direct scoring.
XKRnNzdC9p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the benchmark useful, linking many users to the same discussion, and the generation-versus-selection failure analysis informative and reusable.
XKRnNzdC9p.main_concern: Benchmark validity is under-documented: model-assisted labels lack reported human validation or agreement, data partitions are unspecified, and some failure explanations depend on specific implementation choices.

dCYSDNKYdE.one_liner: Stabilizes PPO for LLM post-training with actor-only overlong filtering, noise-normalized critic loss, and smaller critic mini-batches.
dCYSDNKYdE.problem: The learned critic is a major source of PPO instability for LLMs: filtering truncated rollouts shifts the objective to reward conditioned on completion, and heterogeneous return noise lets high-variance prompts dominate critic updates.
dCYSDNKYdE.method: EasyPPO filters overlong rollouts only for the actor so the critic trains on both completed and truncated returns, weights each prompt's critic loss by the inverse standard deviation of its sampled returns, and uses moderately smaller critic mini-batches to limit outlier influence under gradient clipping.
dCYSDNKYdE.key_idea: Keep truncated rollouts in critic training, normalize critic regression per prompt by return standard deviation, and shrink critic mini-batches to confine outliers.
dCYSDNKYdE.evidence: Continuous-reward coding on FrontierCS, binary-reward math reasoning on AIME24, and multi-turn search on Search-R1, compared with vanilla PPO, VAPO, and other baselines.
dCYSDNKYdE.claimed_gains: EasyPPO remains stable over the full training horizon and consistently outperforms vanilla PPO, VAPO, and other baselines; no numbers stated.
dCYSDNKYdE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the identified critic instabilities and the loss-normalization analysis insightful and the techniques valuable to practitioners doing LLM post-training with PPO.
dCYSDNKYdE.main_concern: Presentation and scope gaps: unclear writing and figures, limited novelty (small PPO modifications, with noise normalization already known), and no GRPO or Dr. GRPO comparison in the main table.

JmFYQ7GRSr.one_liner: Precomputes diffusion-drafter representations for every acceptance boundary during verification, then emits drafts instantly with an autoregressive head.
JmFYQ7GRSr.problem: Parallel speculative decoding must guess the accepted prefix and bonus token in advance, and a wrong guess reverts the whole batch to serial drafting.
JmFYQ7GRSr.method: While the target verifies, DPara's diffusion backbone precomputes draft representations for every acceptance boundary with the bonus left unspecified. A lightweight autoregressive head then combines the revealed verification outcome with the matching precomputed representation to emit the next draft.
JmFYQ7GRSr.key_idea: Precompute draft states for all possible acceptance boundaries in parallel with verification, then select by the revealed outcome, eliminating the probabilistic fallback.
JmFYQ7GRSr.evidence: Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B on seven math, coding, and chat benchmarks, with batching, stochastic sampling, and single-GPU colocation studies per reviewers.
JmFYQ7GRSr.claimed_gains: Average speedups of 3.21× and 3.52× over autoregressive decoding on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B, surpassing the strongest serial and parallel speculative decoding baselines.
JmFYQ7GRSr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that precomputing all acceptance boundaries removes the batch-fallback problem and that DPara beats baselines across seven benchmarks (2.89× to 3.21× over DSpark on Qwen3-8B).
JmFYQ7GRSr.main_concern: Overhead and fairness: precomputing d+1 branches makes single-GPU DPara slower than serial DSpark at batch sizes 8 and 16, main results use 2 GPUs versus 1, and the technical contribution is seen as limited.

XnPLTKxRPs.one_liner: Weights distillation loss by the expected downstream reward of the teacher's output, with trajectory-level and critic-based step-level variants.
XnPLTKxRPs.problem: Knowledge distillation does not use the measurable task performance of teacher samples to control how much each teacher sample influences the student.
XnPLTKxRPs.method: RG-KD weights the distillation loss by the expected downstream utility of the teacher's predictive distribution, extends to sequences through trajectory-level reward weighting, and uses a critic for step-level value estimation. It can be added to existing KD objectives.
XnPLTKxRPs.key_idea: Scale each teacher sample's distillation loss by a task-reward-derived weight (trajectory reward or critic value) so supervision favors high-reward teacher outputs.
XnPLTKxRPs.evidence: Five diverse tasks against unweighted, entropy-weighted, and adaptive or selective KD baselines, plus plug-in tests with GKD and DistiLLM and rebuttal controls per a reviewer.
XnPLTKxRPs.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms unweighted and entropy-weighted baselines and recent adaptive and selective methods across five tasks; a reviewer cites GSM8K improving from 78.70 to 80.36 in one plug-in case.
XnPLTKxRPs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea simple and easy to adopt as a scalar weight on existing divergences, with a wide range of tasks, encouraging improvements, and an interesting critic-based step-level extension.
XnPLTKxRPs.main_concern: The objective is unclear and weakly differentiated: Eq. 3 does not change the pointwise optimum of standard KD, its distinction from existing reward-weighted distillation is unclear, and the added covariance term and reward scaling are insufficiently justified.

LpRCJSlrDh.one_liner: Explains rewriting-based synthetic pretraining gains through a rewriting-pretraining gap formalized with algorithmic information theory.
LpRCJSlrDh.problem: Synthetic rewrites of human text improve downstream generalization even when the rewriting model lacks the capabilities gained, and why this happens is unexplained.
LpRCJSlrDh.method: They argue rewriting models learn simple transformations that generalize to unseen inputs; applying them changes pretraining prediction problems, increasing the computationally bounded information accessible to the learner and inducing new representations, which they formalize and test in controlled experiments.
LpRCJSlrDh.key_idea: Rewriting applies learned simple transformations that change pretraining prediction problems, raising the computationally bounded information accessible to the learner.
LpRCJSlrDh.evidence: An algorithmic-information-theory formalization, controlled experiments validating its predictions, and a challenging two-hop knowledge task where fictional rewrites improve compositional generalization.
LpRCJSlrDh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find understanding synthetic data from smaller models a worthwhile goal and see parts of the conceptual framing, such as removing in-context signal forcing internalization, as insightful.
LpRCJSlrDh.main_concern: The paper is hard to follow, relies on unjustified assumptions, and draws a broad conclusion from narrow fact- and relation-style tasks, with one reviewer saying the motivating premise misreads the cited rewriting papers.

dI5AAdk72i.one_liner: Minecraft dataset of synchronized POV and panoramic videos with actions, and a dual-tower world model coupled by ray-aligned cross-attention.
dI5AAdk72i.problem: A multiplayer world model must predict changes outside a player's field of view caused by other players, but no Minecraft dataset pairs synchronized POV and panoramic video with actions.
dI5AAdk72i.method: PAWA provides a distributed capture-and-render pipeline that scales beyond 64 simultaneous players and re-renders sessions under new observation configurations, and a dual-tower model that jointly predicts POV and panoramic video with cross-attention aligning tokens that observe the same direction in a shared world frame, plus quadratic-phase player codes.
dI5AAdk72i.key_idea: Panoramic video serves as world-stable context, and cross-attention aligns POV and panorama tokens that look in the same direction in a shared world frame.
dI5AAdk72i.evidence: Experiments on the new dataset using FVD and LPIPS against POV-only baselines, with ablations including disabled cross-attention (Table 9) and an action-binding evaluation, according to reviews.
dI5AAdk72i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the out-of-view interaction problem is well motivated, panoramas are a sensible intermediate representation, and the dataset and capture pipeline are useful contributions.
dI5AAdk72i.main_concern: Evaluation is weak on the central claim: no direct cross-view or cross-player consistency metrics, no comparison with simpler alternatives such as vanilla cross-attention or geometric warping, and the baseline comparison is arguably unfair since PAWA also receives initial panoramas.

p3geD5SoOp.one_liner: Learns world-model latents whose distances match commute times using a latent displacement predictor and a log-determinant regularizer.
p3geD5SoOp.problem: Self-supervised world models that encourage isotropic representations to avoid collapse degrade the eigenvalue-dependent scaling needed for latent distances to mirror commute times.
p3geD5SoOp.method: CTWM combines a latent displacement predictor with a log-determinant regularizer that prevents collapse, and provably recovers the correctly scaled graph Laplacian representation under deterministic dynamics at the predictor's fixed point.
p3geD5SoOp.key_idea: A log-determinant regularizer in place of isotropy-promoting regularizers keeps the Laplacian eigenvalue scaling, so latent distances mirror commute times.
p3geD5SoOp.evidence: A theorem on Laplacian recovery, a synthetic torus graph, and six pixel-based continuous goal-reaching benchmarks compared with LeWM.
p3geD5SoOp.claimed_gains: Matches or outperforms LeWM on several complex, continuous goal-reaching benchmarks while using only half the parameters.
p3geD5SoOp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the commute-time motivation is well grounded, the theory clearly shows how log-determinant regularization recovers the eigenvalue scaling, and CTWM matches or beats LeWM with half the parameters.
p3geD5SoOp.main_concern: The evidence does not isolate the regularizer: the torus test omits LeWM and uses VICReg while planning compares only against LeWM, and ablations of the residual predictor, LayerNorm, and weight-decay changes are missing.

cLndIHFADa.one_liner: Matches cells to adjacent reference sections, transfers measured protein signals, and fuses them with H&E features to recover missing mIF.
cLndIHFADa.problem: H&E-based or cross-omics inference of protein markers performs poorly for markers weakly associated with morphology or other omics features.
cLndIHFADa.method: NeighborMIF does cell-level matching to transfer experimentally measured protein signals from reference sections, reconstructs them in the spatial feature space of the target section, and integrates them with H&E features to recover missing mIF.
cLndIHFADa.key_idea: Use experimentally measured proteins from a neighboring section, aligned by cell-level matching, as extra evidence added on top of an H&E-only model.
cLndIHFADa.evidence: A consecutive-section dataset and ORION CRC under a cross-sample non-contiguous-reference setting, against external methods and a same-architecture H&E-only baseline across 15 proteins.
cLndIHFADa.claimed_gains: Average cell-level Pearson correlation of 82.83% (r x 100), 6.11 percentage points above the best external method; improves the same-architecture H&E-only baseline on all 15 proteins on ORION CRC.
cLndIHFADa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree measured reference signals are logically useful evidence beyond H&E morphology and that the fusion design is relevant, with a leakage-safe cross-sample reference bank.
cLndIHFADa.main_concern: The evaluation set is a small private dataset and the formulation is oversimplified (predicting proteins already measured in an adjacent section), with unclear ablation of the neighbor signal and baseline training controls.

j9iUb538cL.one_liner: Adds a discriminator-gated Sinkhorn optimal-transport term to the integral-KL energy of distribution matching distillation for few-step diffusion generators.
j9iUb538cL.problem: DMD guides samples by local density alone, so teacher scores can be unreliable in low-density regions and reverse-KL mode seeking can collapse the student onto a subset of teacher modes.
j9iUb538cL.method: Viewing DMD as Wasserstein gradient flow with an integral-KL energy, sDMD augments it with a Sinkhorn divergence term estimated from finite batches, and gates it per sample by discriminator output so it acts only on outliers where IKL may be unreliable.
j9iUb538cL.key_idea: Add Sinkhorn transport guidance to DMD's IKL gradient only for samples a discriminator flags as outliers, supplying mode coverage without perturbing in-domain samples.
j9iUb538cL.evidence: 2-4 step generation on FLUX.1-dev, Qwen-Image-20B, and Wan2.1-14B evaluated on GenEval, DPG, WISE, and VBench, plus theory connecting DMD to Wasserstein gradient flow.
j9iUb538cL.claimed_gains: Outperforms distillation baselines on GenEval, DPG, WISE, and VBench with 2-4 sampling steps and improves sample diversity over DMD2; no margins stated.
j9iUb538cL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear, the Wasserstein-gradient-flow view of DMD is a useful theoretical frame, and the experiments cover several large image and video models.
j9iUb538cL.main_concern: Gains may come from an implicit teacher-sample regression constraint rather than transport, the gate threshold is not ablated, and the cost of generating extra samples and the recovery from mode collapse are insufficiently characterized.

H2CxkGecWg.one_liner: Region-level entropy graphs with closed-form spatial and motion-compensated temporal edges for no-reference video quality assessment and localization.
H2CxkGecWg.problem: No-reference video quality assessment collapses spatio-temporal failures into one scalar, so it cannot say where or when quality fails.
H2CxkGecWg.method: Region nodes carry a five-cue entropy decomposition, spatial edges measure conditional entropy deviation from natural statistics, and motion-compensated temporal edges use the aligned past as reference; only three matrices are learned.
H2CxkGecWg.key_idea: Fix graph structure analytically with conditional-entropy edge weights, using the motion-aligned past of the video as its own reference, and learn only three matrices.
H2CxkGecWg.evidence: The region-labeled D-CQA corpus (with released splits, metrics, and code), zero-shot transfer to KoNViD-1k and LIVE-VQC, and a multimodal LLM region-reasoning test.
H2CxkGecWg.claimed_gains: Global SRCC 0.897 versus 0.831 for the strongest holistic baseline, localization AUC 0.823, and a 12.6-point lift in a multimodal LLM's region-level quality reasoning.
H2CxkGecWg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the interpretable, analytic localization design with a small learned component and the region-labeled D-CQA annotations valuable contributions.
H2CxkGecWg.main_concern: Localization results are inconsistent with the stated definition (ablations change a supposedly analytic map), and the proofs of Propositions 4 and 5 are not rigorous.

jMShEJfLSW.one_liner: Benchmark of 480 real patent examination cases covering Office Action generation and applicant rebuttal in multi-turn exchanges.
jMShEJfLSW.problem: Prior patent benchmarks treat examination as static classification or extraction and miss its interactive, iterative office-action and rebuttal process.
jMShEJfLSW.method: PatRe models the full examination lifecycle across 480 real cases, supports oracle and retrieval-simulated reference settings, and evaluates LLMs on examiner-side analysis and applicant-side rebuttal.
jMShEJfLSW.key_idea: Frame patent examination as a multi-turn justification-and-response process, pairing each Office Action with the applicant rebuttal under controlled prior-art reference conditions.
jMShEJfLSW.evidence: Experiments across proprietary and open-source LLMs in oracle and retrieval-simulated settings, with LLM-as-judge and a human study per reviews.
jMShEJfLSW.claimed_gains: Benchmark of 480 real-world cases; findings on proprietary versus open-source gaps and examiner versus applicant task asymmetry, with no numeric gains stated.
jMShEJfLSW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the full-lifecycle, multi-turn modeling of office actions and rebuttals a meaningful extension, with broad evaluation across LLM families and reference conditions.
jMShEJfLSW.main_concern: Missing trivial baselines and weak metrics (decision accuracy near the majority class, statute precision without recall), a small 480-case dataset, and unclear dataset release.

AwjS0mv7WU.one_liner: Federated LoRA that shares dominant subspaces of input-aware action matrices to regularize local training instead of averaging weights.
AwjS0mv7WU.problem: Similarity among trained LoRA projection matrices across clients may come mostly from common initialization and ignores local input regime, so it is an unreliable shared structure.
AwjS0mv7WU.method: FedSAIL builds an input-aware action matrix that weights the adapter update by second-moment statistics of local layer inputs, and estimates a shared action subspace from clients' leading right singular directions. It uses that subspace to regularize local training while keeping client-specific coefficients.
AwjS0mv7WU.key_idea: Share the leading right singular subspace of the input-weighted LoRA update across clients as a regularizer, rather than averaging adapter weights.
AwjS0mv7WU.evidence: Diagnostics showing parameter similarity vanishes under independent initialization while action-matrix directions stay aligned, plus benchmark comparisons against federated LoRA methods (reviews cite RoBERTa-large on GLUE with three clients).
AwjS0mv7WU.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports consistent predictive improvements over federated LoRA baselines and significantly lower communication cost, without numbers)
AwjS0mv7WU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnostic showing LoRA A-matrix similarity collapses under independent initialization is insightful and that the small shared message makes communication savings practical.
AwjS0mv7WU.main_concern: Empirical gains are small, sometimes within one standard deviation, on a narrow setup (three clients), and the gain from sharing is not isolated from the local rank-1 regularization.

rSLn8p1uK1.one_liner: Converts radiologists' routine 2D CT annotations into 3D phrase-mask training triplets via report matching and promptable segmentation.
rSLn8p1uK1.problem: 3D CT visual grounding lacks large paired phrase-region datasets because hand annotation by radiologists is expensive and findings occupy a tiny fraction of the volume.
rSLn8p1uK1.method: An automated pipeline links each PACS 2D annotation to a report finding through metadata matching, then converts it to a volumetric mask with a promptable 3D segmentation model, producing phrase-mask-volume triplets. A grounding model (LocusCT) is trained on them and evaluated on LocusBench, a radiologist-verified benchmark.
rSLn8p1uK1.key_idea: Reuse routine GSPS annotations on key images as implicit supervision, matched to report findings by metadata and lifted to 3D masks by promptable segmentation.
rSLn8p1uK1.evidence: Pipeline applied to one institution's PACS (59K abdominal CT exams), LocusBench evaluation against zero-shot baselines VoxTell, SegVol and BiomedParse-v2, and data-scaling curves.
rSLn8p1uK1.claimed_gains: Generated 105K phrase-mask-volume triplets from 59K abdominal CT exams of a single institution's PACS; model performance numbers are not stated in the provided abstract.
rSLn8p1uK1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the approach is a practical, scalable source of clinically grounded supervision and that the radiologist-verified LocusBench is useful.
rSLn8p1uK1.main_concern: LocusBench cases come from the same pipeline and institution as the training data, and baselines are zero-shot rather than trained on matched supervision, limiting generalization claims.

cFkX5PpXaJ.one_liner: Training-free budget allocator for OmniLLM token pruning: query-driven skill pools split audio/video budget, then complexity-based intra-modal reallocation.
cFkX5PpXaJ.problem: OmniLLM token compression fixes the retained budget and only selects tokens, leaving inter-modal and intra-modal budget allocation underexplored; query-to-audio/video similarity is unreliable and uniform intra-modal budgets miss key evidence.
cFkX5PpXaJ.method: OmniDelta builds audio and video skill pools to shift the retained-token budget between modalities according to query demand, then reallocates each modality's budget over audio segments and video frames using local complexity and temporal redundancy. The local budgets plug into existing pruning strategies while keeping the total retained-token ratio fixed.
cFkX5PpXaJ.key_idea: Matches the query to audio and video skill pools to set the inter-modal split, then redistributes within each modality by local complexity and temporal redundancy.
cFkX5PpXaJ.evidence: Four audio-video benchmarks with two Qwen2.5-Omni models across pruning ratios, with ablation studies and inference-efficiency analysis.
cFkX5PpXaJ.claimed_gains: Abstract states a new accuracy-efficiency Pareto frontier across pruning ratios; its example of GPU-memory reduction at 25% token retention on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B is cut off in the provided text.
cFkX5PpXaJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating budget allocation from token selection, the training-free plug-in design that keeps the total budget fixed, and the broad evaluation across benchmarks and model scales.
cFkX5PpXaJ.main_concern: Novelty over query-aware budget methods (OmniSelect, OmniFocus) is not substantiated without direct comparisons, and inter-modal allocation alone adds little (average 56.8 to 56.9 in Table 4).

kEQqdQufvz.one_liner: Universal approximation theory showing diagonal-plus-low-rank layers restore expressivity lost by purely low-rank networks, via width and depth constructions.
kEQqdQufvz.problem: Purely low-rank networks can interpolate finite datasets yet fail to approximate continuous functions that vary along directions ignored by the low-rank hidden mapping.
kEQqdQufvz.method: Adds a one-parameter diagonal component to the low-rank structure (DLoR) and shows a full-rank linear map can be rebuilt from DLoR components by additive width expansion or multiplicative depth extension (Structural Correspondence). Combined with local linearization of the activation, this gives universal approximation for general activations.
kEQqdQufvz.key_idea: A scalar diagonal term restores the directions a low-rank layer ignores; full-rank maps are rebuilt by summing low-rank branches (width) or composing DLoR factors (depth).
kEQqdQufvz.evidence: Theoretical proofs (universal approximation, parameter bounds, transfer theorems), including exact ReLU constructions; the abstract reports no experiments.
kEQqdQufvz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the statements precise and the checked proofs correct, with the width-depth-rank correspondence a clear and elegant theoretical insight.
kEQqdQufvz.main_concern: Limited theoretical novelty, since results follow from known tools (minimum-width results, 1-D interpolation, SVD reparametrization), and reconstructing dense maps can require many layers (up to N/r DLoR factors).

Q4HQjTG2hC.one_liner: Hybrid quantum-classical model whose trainable sampler generates valid tensor-network topologies, trained jointly with PDE dynamics.
Q4HQjTG2hC.problem: Tensor-network PDE solvers use structures fixed in advance, structure-search methods optimize compression of individual fields rather than PDE dynamics, and quantum samplers lack a mechanism that emits only valid network structures.
Q4HQjTG2hC.method: A trainable quantum sampler generates valid tensor-network topologies without rejection and feeds them into a differentiable tensor-network PDE solver. Aster+ adds rank adaptation to the discovered structure.
Q4HQjTG2hC.key_idea: A bit-to-tree decoder maps number-preserving quantum-circuit samples to valid binary trees without rejection, so topology is learned jointly with PDE dynamics.
Q4HQjTG2hC.evidence: Three evaluation settings: seven benchmark PDEs against spectral Runge-Kutta and twelve two-dimensional PDEs against neural PDE solvers; reviewers note the problems are small (2D 32^2, 3D 16^3).
Q4HQjTG2hC.claimed_gains: Aster+ matches spectral Runge-Kutta accuracy on six of seven benchmark PDEs using 2.9-10x fewer stored scalars on five; Aster-Solver achieves the lowest error at every evaluated resolution on eight of twelve two-dimensional PDEs against neural PDE solvers.
Q4HQjTG2hC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find jointly learning tensor-network topology and PDE dynamics well motivated, and the rejection-free tree decoder a clean contribution with a clear validity guarantee.
Q4HQjTG2hC.main_concern: The need for a quantum sampler is not demonstrated, since the decoder is not inherently quantum and the classical-sampler comparison does not isolate quantum advantage, with experiments limited to small problems.

DiTHJCF9XI.one_liner: Benchmark that forks Clean and Shifted continuations from one saved workspace to test coding agents under mid-execution changes.
DiTHJCF9XI.problem: Repository-level coding benchmarks assume tasks and environments stay fixed, although code, dependencies, runtime state, and requirements can change while an agent is still working.
DiTHJCF9XI.method: SWE-Shift runs a Clean continuation and a matched Shifted continuation (which receives a task-relevant update) from the same saved history and workspace. Success requires completing the current task, preserving still-valid work, and passing the applicable state and evidence checks.
DiTHJCF9XI.key_idea: Matched-prefix design: fork Clean and Shifted continuations from identical saved history and workspace, so any gap is attributable to the mid-execution update.
DiTHJCF9XI.evidence: 120 scenarios across 12 change families, each evaluated at nine scheduled intervention positions, with 17 coding-agent systems.
DiTHJCF9XI.claimed_gains: All 17 systems score lower Shifted than Clean; GPT-6 Astra drops from 67.35% to 24.79% with 20.34% paired success, and tool/session changes and stale evidence yield zero paired success across all systems.
DiTHJCF9XI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically important and that the matched-continuation design and the 12 change families give a useful control beyond static task success.
DiTHJCF9XI.main_concern: Strict success mixes behavioral correctness with procedural requirements, and task construction, Clean-failure causes, and intervention details are under-documented, so failures are hard to interpret.

uhNRUtcb9y.one_liner: EgoLAP pre-trains VLAs on human and robot data with shared language-action chain-of-thought and motion-level reasoning.
uhNRUtcb9y.problem: Raw egocentric human trajectories are a poor supervisory target for robot control because low-level actions are embodiment-specific.
uhNRUtcb9y.method: EgoLAP expresses motion intent as structured, temporally abstracted language actions and pairs them with motion-level reasoning grounded in scene geometry, physics, and object affordances. It jointly learns from human and robot trajectories through a shared language-based action chain-of-thought.
uhNRUtcb9y.key_idea: Use embodiment-agnostic motion intent, written as language actions plus motion-level reasoning, as the shared supervision target for human and robot trajectories.
uhNRUtcb9y.evidence: Extensive real-world and simulated experiments comparing action representations and reasoning formats; reviews cite simulation ablations of human-robot co-training and real-world YAM tasks.
uhNRUtcb9y.claimed_gains: Reaches 80.1% mean real-world task progress, a 2.3x gain over alternative action representations, and motion-level reasoning also outperforms a composite reasoning format.
uhNRUtcb9y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the language-action supervision is a practical shared interface for cross-embodiment learning and gives strong, consistent gains in simulation and real-world control.
uhNRUtcb9y.main_concern: Novelty is modest because language actions, movement explanations, and reasoning supervision without test-time generation were explored before, so the contribution is mostly the combination.

kAw1NI1vdI.one_liner: Tests medical VLM fixation attention heads in both directions and finds they are steerable but not readable as provenance.
kAw1NI1vdI.problem: Medical VLMs write fluent findings without showing which image region supports each sentence, and it is unknown whether attention heads can serve as provenance for their claims.
kAw1NI1vdI.method: The authors test fixation heads by reading their attention as evidence and by writing a region into it. Anatomy-conditioned generation writes one anatomical region into the heads per sentence without training, and MedGaze, a low-rank adapter on the heads' query rows, learns that write.
kAw1NI1vdI.key_idea: Steer fixation heads' attention toward one anatomical region per sentence so the sentence depends on it, instead of reading attention maps as evidence.
kAw1NI1vdI.evidence: Three model families and six corpora (25 VLMs from 2B to 73B parameters per reviews), with random-head controls, size-matched random boxes, and Holm-corrected tests.
kAw1NI1vdI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is large and carefully controlled, with 25 VLMs and random-head, random-box, and paired comparisons, and that separating steerability from readability is a useful framing.
kAw1NI1vdI.main_concern: MedGaze performs similarly to an answer-only adapter, so the benefit of attention supervision over ordinary fine-tuning is unclear, and provenance for individual clinical claims is not established.

C3E8VDeNG6.one_liner: Single-block recurrent ViT reuses one wide transformer block across depth, matching most of ViT-B accuracy with 8.6M parameters.
C3E8VDeNG6.problem: It is unclear how much of the independent parameterization of stacked ViT blocks is necessary and how much can be replaced by recurrent reuse.
C3E8VDeNG6.method: bViT repeatedly applies the same transformer block while preserving the iterative computation of a deep model. They then analyze attention, activation patterns, and step-conditioned spectral pruning across recurrent steps, and test transfer and parameter-efficient adaptation.
C3E8VDeNG6.key_idea: Tie all layers of a ViT to one sufficiently wide block applied recurrently, so the same heads, neurons, and weights can be tracked across steps.
C3E8VDeNG6.evidence: ImageNet-1K under the same training recipe and computational budget as ViT, width and recurrent-depth trade-offs, attention and spectral analyses, and downstream transfer.
C3E8VDeNG6.claimed_gains: On ImageNet-1K, bViT-B reaches 0.779 validation accuracy versus 0.789 for ViT-B under the same recipe and budget, using 8.6M rather than 86.6M parameters.
C3E8VDeNG6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a clean, well-controlled setting for studying extreme parameter sharing, with compute- and parameter-matched ablations and a gap that shrinks as width grows.
C3E8VDeNG6.main_concern: Novelty is limited relative to Universal Transformers and recursive ViTs such as SReT with no experimental comparison to them, and the ViT baselines are weak.

NAtWvXBsNG.one_liner: Clones a customer simulator's action policy from 452k shopping episodes with a structured score model and a metric-aware decision layer.
NAtWvXBsNG.problem: Prompted-LLM customer simulators are reported to be homogenized and over-agreeable, and per-step next-item metrics miss actions such as search, refine, convert, or stop.
NAtWvXBsNG.method: Factors a simulator step into action selection and semantic realization and learns the first by behavioral cloning over a ten-action space with a leakage-audited state. StructBC is a 3.4M-parameter structured score model, followed by a nine-parameter post-hoc decision layer.
NAtWvXBsNG.key_idea: Separate action selection from semantic realization, clone the action policy with structured scores, and tune a small post-hoc decision layer to the target metric.
NAtWvXBsNG.evidence: Open-loop evaluation on 452,296 real shopping episodes with customer-disjoint splits, closed-loop tests on a live storefront against 18,550 logged visits, and comparison with count-based, NARM, LoRA-LLM, and matched Transformer baselines across five seeds.
NAtWvXBsNG.claimed_gains: With a post-hoc decision layer the policy reaches 0.5065 macro-F1, and StructBC adds a consistent gain over a matched Transformer across two sequence families and five seeds.
NAtWvXBsNG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the experimental hygiene and transparency: customer-disjoint splits, multi-seed replication, a feature leakage audit, and honest reporting of limitations.
NAtWvXBsNG.main_concern: The structural gains are tiny (about +0.004 to +0.005 macro-F1) and vanish when the corpus-level product-popularity feature is removed, so the architectural contribution is not established.

oGutlRaMCf.one_liner: One recurrent ViT block whose FFN is a depth-programmed convex mix of shared experts, matching full-depth accuracy with fewer parameters.
oGutlRaMCf.problem: Applying a single Transformer block recurrently loses depth-specific transformations, so parameters stored by a vision encoder remain tied to the depth it executes.
oGutlRaMCf.method: reViT represents the FFN at each recurrent depth as a convex combination of a small shared expert bank, programmed by a continuous normalized-depth coordinate that defines a resampleable trajectory through FFN parameter space. For fixed-depth deployment it can be materialized as a conventional dense graph.
oGutlRaMCf.key_idea: Mix the FFN weights of a shared expert bank with coefficients generated from a continuous normalized-depth coordinate, giving each recurrent step its own FFN.
oGutlRaMCf.evidence: Supervised ImageNet-1k training and distillation from a DINOv2 teacher, with transfer to classification, segmentation, and depth prediction and a controlled comparison of MoE families.
oGutlRaMCf.claimed_gains: reViT-B/16 attains DeiT III accuracy with about 70% fewer stored parameters, and an 8-experts distilled model retains nearly all of its DINOv2 teacher's linear-probe accuracy.
oGutlRaMCf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the architecture is simple and effective, achieving large parameter reduction (e.g. 23.6M versus 86.6M for DeiT III) with competitive accuracy across model sizes and downstream tasks.
oGutlRaMCf.main_concern: Limited novelty: it is seen as an extension of ALBERT-style parameter sharing, recurrent transformers, and expert weight merging, with modest gains over existing parameter-saving methods such as SMEAR.

f5EFsSJVUz.one_liner: Contrasting expert and agent kernels produces hardware-specific diagnostics and guides retained only after transfer tests with fresh agents.
f5EFsSJVUz.problem: LLM kernel agents lack hardware-specific knowledge needed to identify and implement optimizations on unfamiliar accelerators.
f5EFsSJVUz.method: Artisan derives reusable diagnostic tools and implementation guides from expert-agent kernel contrasts. It retains artifacts only when fresh agents without expert access achieve verified improvements using them.
f5EFsSJVUz.key_idea: Convert measured expert-agent kernel differences into reusable support and filter it by verified transfer to fresh agents.
f5EFsSJVUz.evidence: Evaluation covers 40 unseen AWS Trainium 2 kernels, four agentic optimization pipelines, correctness verification, and ablations of tools and guides.
f5EFsSJVUz.claimed_gains: Artisan achieves 1.58× geometric-mean speedup over NKIPy versus 1.37× for the strongest same-expert baseline, and raises four pipelines from 0.46–1.27× with 24–40/40 coverage to 1.55–1.60× with 40/40.
f5EFsSJVUz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical unfamiliar-hardware problem and reusable expert-derived support validated through execution feedback.
f5EFsSJVUz.main_concern: Reviewers question comparison fairness because verified-kernel coverage differs and token and artifact-preparation costs are not fully matched.

T9jEpadeNL.one_liner: Contrastively constructed accommodation listings create unique booking targets with controlled geographic and preference-disclosure difficulty.
T9jEpadeNL.problem: Conversational search benchmarks often assume precise requests and lack verifiable targets for underspecified user goals.
T9jEpadeNL.method: LODGE constructs single-item accommodation-booking tasks with a unique best-fitting listing confirmed by human review. GeoFlex varies geographic specification, while Vagueness changes how explicitly the same goal is disclosed.
T9jEpadeNL.key_idea: Construct contrastive listing sets with a unique target, then vary geographic cues and goal disclosure while retaining an explicit success criterion.
T9jEpadeNL.evidence: The benchmark contains 360 tasks with a fixed 300-task evaluation split and evaluates seven language agents using controlled variants and booking outcomes.
T9jEpadeNL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value verifiable, judge-free targets for underspecified multi-turn booking tasks and diagnostic difficulty variants.
T9jEpadeNL.main_concern: Reviewers question whether narrowly scoped synthetic accommodation tasks and limited construction validation generalize to real travel search.

UKBAKfOjfn.one_liner: Policy entropy redistributes outcome-conditioned GRPO credit across action segments in long-horizon vision-language-action rollouts.
UKBAKfOjfn.problem: Trajectory-level advantages assign the same credit to useful and failed intermediate actions under sparse terminal rewards.
UKBAKfOjfn.method: ESCAPO uses policy entropy to refine GRPO advantages without a critic or dense supervision. It protects reliable low-entropy segments in failures and gives additional positive credit to uncertain actions in successful rollouts.
UKBAKfOjfn.key_idea: Condition entropy-based segment credit on rollout success, preserving confident behavior in failures and reinforcing uncertainty validated by success.
UKBAKfOjfn.evidence: Human-annotated rollout analysis and LIBERO-10 and LIBERO-Plus-10 experiments examine entropy-quality associations, SFT and shared warm-up initializations, and failure-branch ablations.
UKBAKfOjfn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a practical approach to finer credit assignment that improves long-horizon learning without external action-quality supervision.
UKBAKfOjfn.main_concern: Reviewers find the specific contribution of entropy-guided segmentation insufficiently isolated from close prior methods and simpler temporal weighting.

O5oK3ZtpfC.one_liner: A bounded spatial-polarity gate modulates token interactions in spiking transformers trained only on clean event data.
O5oK3ZtpfC.problem: Noise robustness after event tokenization is not fully addressed by denoising, corruption-aware training, or feature design.
O5oK3ZtpfC.method: SECA maps token-aligned spatial and polarity structure into bounded modulation of native token interactions. It adds two learnable scalars per block while preserving spiking dynamics and uses clean-only training.
O5oK3ZtpfC.key_idea: Use sensing-derived spatial and polarity relationships to construct a bounded gate over spiking token interactions.
O5oK3ZtpfC.evidence: Experiments span three Spiking Transformer families and event datasets, with polarity-flip, background-activity, and hot-pixel corruptions plus prior-violation and gate-removal ablations.
O5oK3ZtpfC.claimed_gains: Under the strongest polarity flip on DVS128-Gesture, SECA reduces the performance drop from 28.82 to 9.38 points.
O5oK3ZtpfC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a simple, lightweight design with substantial polarity-noise robustness gains and detailed structural-prior ablations.
O5oK3ZtpfC.main_concern: Reviewers question the claimed interaction mechanism because removing the gate at inference preserves or slightly improves robustness.

5KBYAraeHy.one_liner: Weight-derived retention horizons select recurrent-state units for ragged checkpoints in hybrid linear-attention prefix caches.
5KBYAraeHy.problem: Persistent recurrent-state checkpoints increase memory pressure, evictions, and repeated prefill in hybrid-attention serving.
5KBYAraeHy.method: DASC derives retention horizons from decay parameters and packs selected long-horizon heads or channels into ragged checkpoints, optionally balancing storage across tensor-parallel ranks. Reuse zero-fills omitted units or refreshes them from a bounded suffix.
5KBYAraeHy.key_idea: Select persistent state units by weight-derived decay horizons and reconstruct omitted units by zero filling or bounded-suffix replay.
5KBYAraeHy.evidence: Kimi-Linear, Qwen3-Next, and Kimi-K3 evaluations cover GDN and KDA, retrieval and reasoning quality, count-matched random selection, and SGLang serving workloads.
5KBYAraeHy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a practical checkpoint-memory problem and an implementable architecture-aware compression design with multi-model evaluation.
5KBYAraeHy.main_concern: Reviewers find comparisons against random selection insufficient to establish the quality-memory-latency advantage over stronger selection or checkpoint-management alternatives.

dAMG7n2cPR.one_liner: Recorded tokens, routes, dependencies, and tool delays replay identical agent workloads while preserving normal autoregressive computation.
dAMG7n2cPR.problem: Changing agent trajectories confound serving-system benchmarks, and length-only replay omits token-dependent cache and expert-routing behavior.
dAMG7n2cPR.method: AgentReplay records model tokens, expert selections, request dependencies, and tool durations. It forces recorded output tokens during normal autoregressive execution with optional route and delay controls while leaving system scheduling decisions free.
dAMG7n2cPR.key_idea: Force recorded token trajectories during live model computation so serving configurations process the same logical agent workload.
dAMG7n2cPR.evidence: Experiments compare token-wise replay with greedy decoding and length-wise replay on coding tasks, including repeated executions and a cross-model long-horizon trace.
dAMG7n2cPR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that trajectory variation is a meaningful benchmarking problem and that token-wise replay provides useful workload control.
dAMG7n2cPR.main_concern: Reviewers unanimously identify unquantified replay overhead as a threat to trustworthy relative performance measurements.

9hmyNsona9.one_liner: Neighborhood ranking and geometric similarity combine with an analytic null expectation to measure representation alignment across scales.
9hmyNsona9.problem: Existing similarity measures trade off local detail, global coverage, geometric information, and robust calibration.
9hmyNsona9.method: Mutual Neighbor Similarity compares corresponding embedding neighborhoods using both ordinal and geometric information. An analytically derived null expectation calibrates the measure against point-cloud geometry across neighborhood scales.
9hmyNsona9.key_idea: Combine neighborhood order with geometric similarities and an analytically computable null expectation for multiscale alignment measurement.
9hmyNsona9.evidence: The paper derives invariances and a robust calibrated form, then evaluates synthetic perturbations and functional representation alignment.
9hmyNsona9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple combination of ranking and geometry and the analytically computable calibration for multiscale comparison.
9hmyNsona9.main_concern: Reviewers find the empirical evidence insufficient to show that the richer geometric sensitivity is more meaningful than established similarity measures.

W5bh0hkmKi.one_liner: Persistent road, scene, and instance memories anchor driving generation, followed by reward-guided online flow-matching optimization.
W5bh0hkmKi.problem: Autoregressive driving world models suffer structural drift, identity drift, and quality decay when conditioning lacks persistent state.
W5bh0hkmKi.method: WAM-Sim maintains pose-aligned road tokens, read-only geolocated scene tokens, and write-once instance tokens. Online flow-matching RL optimizes generated rollouts using hierarchy-aligned visual rewards and a vision-language physical judge.
W5bh0hkmKi.key_idea: Persist road structure, scene appearance, and instance identity in separate memories while optimizing generated rollouts with hierarchy-aligned rewards.
W5bh0hkmKi.evidence: Evaluation includes nuScenes generation and downstream perception metrics, minute-scale driving rollouts, and memory ablations, with reviewers noting scene-memory tests rely on self-collected data.
W5bh0hkmKi.claimed_gains: On nuScenes, WAM-Sim reports FID=7.07, FVD=42.01, 19.67 mAP, and 68.08 road mIoU.
W5bh0hkmKi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value decomposing long-horizon drift into persistent structure, appearance, and identity requirements.
W5bh0hkmKi.main_concern: Reviewers find test-time appearance-reference sources and temporal availability insufficiently specified, obscuring information access and comparison fairness.

6MrulGSXs5.one_liner: Verifiable trajectory curation, compaction-aware policy training, and leakage filtering support reproducible deep-search agent development.
6MrulGSXs5.problem: Opaque training data, context-compaction mismatch, and retrieval of benchmark answers hinder reliable development and evaluation of deep-search agents.
6MrulGSXs5.method: Glasseek combines a verifiable trajectory pipeline with CM-GSPO, which uses one policy for search and summarization while optimizing execution sub-trajectories across compaction boundaries. It also audits web leakage and provides a modular anti-leakage evaluation plugin.
6MrulGSXs5.key_idea: Train execution segments across context-compaction boundaries with a shared search-summary policy and audit retrieved evaluation content for benchmark leakage.
6MrulGSXs5.evidence: The paper evaluates deep-search checkpoints, audits retrieved benchmark answers and solution traces, and analyzes selective restarts and first-attempt performance on BrowseComp.
6MrulGSXs5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the transparency effort and the concrete analysis of open-web benchmark leakage and evaluation protocols.
6MrulGSXs5.main_concern: Reviewers find comparisons with prior context-compaction training methods insufficient to establish CM-GSPO's distinct contribution.

eGQbFlkOuQ.one_liner: Denoising-path correction energy and overlapping-chunk agreement adapt action execution horizons without changing predicted actions.
eGQbFlkOuQ.problem: Fixed execution horizons trade frequent, expensive replanning against delayed responses to environmental changes.
eGQbFlkOuQ.method: KPE-AC measures deviations from constant-velocity transport during action denoising to guide horizon selection. Cross-Chunk Consistency compares actions predicted for overlapping future timesteps and further adjusts how many actions are executed.
eGQbFlkOuQ.key_idea: Use correction energy within a generated action chunk and agreement across overlapping chunks to select the next replanning time.
eGQbFlkOuQ.evidence: Evaluations include multiple flow-based VLA backbones, LIBERO, RoboCasa, real robots, and a Gaussian-case theoretical analysis of the energy signal.
eGQbFlkOuQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical horizon-selection problem and reuse of existing denoising information without additional sampling or training.
eGQbFlkOuQ.main_concern: Reviewers find the advantage over well-tuned fixed horizons small and unsupported by adequate statistical evidence.

orYEypEAQP.one_liner: Alternating GRPO test-time updates under a smooth best-of-budget objective co-adapt a branch-assigning Coordinator and private Scientist LLMs.
orYEypEAQP.problem: Multi-agent LLM scientific discovery couples team-level research branch assignment with individual agent adaptation, since branch choices determine the experimental experiences from which agents learn.
orYEypEAQP.method: MELD adapts a Coordinator policy that proposes portfolios of search branches and directives over a shared derivation tree alongside private Scientist policies whose hypotheses and plans run on a shared frozen Executor. Both levels receive alternating GRPO-style test-time parameter updates aligned under a shared smooth best-of-budget objective.
orYEypEAQP.key_idea: Co-adapt a portfolio-proposing Coordinator policy and private Scientist policies at test time via alternating GRPO parameter updates under a shared smooth best-of-budget objective.
orYEypEAQP.evidence: Supported by theoretical alignment, private-adaptation, and finite-budget regret analyses, and evaluated with a 4B backbone across 22 MLGym and MLE-bench tasks using a shared frozen Executor.
orYEypEAQP.claimed_gains: On 22 MLGym and MLE-bench tasks using a 4B backbone for coordination and research, MELD is best on 20 tasks and achieves the highest aggregate normalized scores on MLGym.
orYEypEAQP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear formulation of joint Coordinator and Scientist test-time adaptation, transparent theoretical documentation, and budget-matched benchmark evaluation.
orYEypEAQP.main_concern: Reviewers highlight discrepancies between the analyzed theoretical assumptions and the implemented sampling code, alongside ablations restricted to one update cycle that do not isolate recursive updates or private adapters.

0mV8ZM0zfY.one_liner: Converting monocular geometry estimates into candidate polarization angular coordinates conditions a lightweight four-step pixel-space RGB-to-polarization diffusion model.
0mV8ZM0zfY.problem: Synthesizing polarization from RGB images faces a diffuse-specular ambiguity where identical surface orientations produce polarization angles 90 degrees apart that appearance alone cannot distinguish.
0mV8ZM0zfY.method: GeoPolar extracts scene geometry from the input RGB image with a monocular foundation model and converts it into the angular coordinates of polarization rather than raw surface normals. Conditioned on these two candidate geometric angles, a lightweight four-step pixel-space diffusion model predicts native-resolution polarization.
0mV8ZM0zfY.key_idea: Convert monocular RGB geometry predictions into polarization angular coordinates so a four-step pixel-space diffusion model resolves the two-branch diffuse-specular reflection ambiguity.
0mV8ZM0zfY.evidence: Evaluated at native resolution against latent-diffusion baselines on benchmark polarization data, a six-scene unseen-camera set, and geometry-representation and normal-perturbation ablations.
0mV8ZM0zfY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that encoding monocular geometry in polarization angular coordinates rather than raw normals is physically well motivated and clearly drives accuracy and model-size gains in ablations.
0mV8ZM0zfY.main_concern: Reviewers point out sensitivity to inaccurate monocular normals on reflective surfaces—creating a circular dependency with shape-from-polarization—and the lack of downstream geometric task validation.

PXkMJQ5v6Y.one_liner: Paired executions estimate memory transfer gains, while structural coverage governs memory selection and pair-level deferral.
PXkMJQ5v6Y.problem: Textual relevance and prior success do not establish that an agent memory will help a particular request.
PXkMJQ5v6Y.method: The method measures request–memory transfer through executions with and without memory and generalizes by tool-call structure. Coverage calibration separates average-value guarantees from marginal pair-level certificates and defers unsupported pair decisions.
PXkMJQ5v6Y.key_idea: Gate memory reuse using interventional transfer estimates and coverage of comparable tool-call structures, with deferral when pair-level evidence is insufficient.
PXkMJQ5v6Y.evidence: Confirmatory controlled benchmarks support average-value selection, while independent pair-level validation yields no certificates and organic AppWorld and BFCL pilots fail to reproduce reliable harm.
PXkMJQ5v6Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value defining memory utility through its incremental execution effect and distinguishing average usefulness from pair-level certification.
PXkMJQ5v6Y.main_concern: Reliable harmful transfer appears only in authored adversarial-memory settings, leaving practical value for naturally collected agent memories unestablished.

5gmCxxY5C4.one_liner: Seven fixed activation directions track representation drift to detect emergent misalignment during fine-tuning.
5gmCxxY5C4.problem: Repeated behavioral evaluation makes checkpoint-by-checkpoint detection of emergent misalignment expensive.
5gmCxxY5C4.method: The monitor projects activations onto seven alignment-related trait directions and tracks checkpoint drift during LoRA fine-tuning. Learned monitors use the resulting profile to distinguish dangerous changes, with stress tests examining training shifts.
5gmCxxY5C4.key_idea: Measure checkpoint drift in a fixed seven-direction activation coordinate system and classify misalignment from the resulting trait profile.
5gmCxxY5C4.evidence: Experiments cover four 7–9B models, 468 held-out checkpoints, benign-dangerous controls, and stress tests with two 14B models and full fine-tuning.
5gmCxxY5C4.claimed_gains: A dominant axis explains 78.6% of drift variance, and monitors attain 1.8% FNR, 2.0% FPR, and 0.989 AUROC.
5gmCxxY5C4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider internal-state monitoring useful and appreciate the extensive experiments and reported limits.
5gmCxxY5C4.main_concern: Dangerous held-out cases largely share the calibration data's harmful-advice category, so generalization to other misalignment types remains uncertain.

Jbcpv8zCGx.one_liner: Random action perturbations and dual-variable exchange drive decentralized equilibrium learning under decision-dependent data distributions.
Jbcpv8zCGx.problem: Players with coupled constraints may observe only payoffs while their own actions change the data-generating distribution.
Jbcpv8zCGx.method: SPADE combines payoff-based random-perturbation estimates with distributed updates that communicate dual variables. Its sampling variants target performative-stable or Nash equilibria, while SPADE-MP uses paired two-point feedback.
Jbcpv8zCGx.key_idea: Estimate updates from perturbed-action payoffs and coordinate coupled constraints through dual-variable consensus, with equilibrium targets determined by the data-sampling protocol.
Jbcpv8zCGx.evidence: The paper gives convergence and regret analyses under specified feedback assumptions and numerical experiments on networked Cournot competition.
Jbcpv8zCGx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reduced peer communication and the explicit distinction between feedback models for different equilibrium targets.
Jbcpv8zCGx.main_concern: Practical guarantees depend on demanding intended-action or paired-feedback access, and per-iteration communication savings do not establish savings at matched accuracy.

YciRLGP2D9.one_liner: Improvement-aware confidence bounds decide when to continue cheap proxy evaluation or purchase trusted bandit feedback.
YciRLGP2D9.problem: Static-proxy bandit models miss the resource trade-off when inexpensive evaluators improve through continued use.
YciRLGP2D9.method: TACC models a stationary high-fidelity target alongside a changing low-fidelity discrepancy bounded by a known average-mismatch certificate. Improvement-aware confidence bounds determine whether to continue proxy evaluation beyond a switching threshold or escalate.
YciRLGP2D9.key_idea: Use a certified bound on evolving proxy-target mismatch to extend low-fidelity sampling when further proxy improvement can avoid expensive confirmation.
YciRLGP2D9.evidence: Instance-dependent regret and proxy-improvement lower bounds accompany experiments on synthetic bandits and NAS-Bench-201.
YciRLGP2D9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard improving-proxy feedback as a relevant extension of multi-fidelity bandit learning.
YciRLGP2D9.main_concern: The guarantees require a known uniformly valid mismatch certificate whose estimation and maintenance in real deployments remain unclear.

uIO57iRdYr.one_liner: A fixed crystal generator and interatomic potential isolate the effects of training, post-training, and inference-time physics.
uIO57iRdYr.problem: Molecular crystal generators produce geometric and packing violations, but physics-integration routes lack controlled comparisons.
uIO57iRdYr.method: CrystAF uses an all-atom crystal flow-map generator with the UMA potential to compare physics at different stages. Post-training filters broken samples and adjusts cell volume, while explicit inference corrections address residual clashes and stereochemistry.
uIO57iRdYr.key_idea: Hold the generator and physical signal fixed while varying when physical supervision or correction enters crystal generation.
uIO57iRdYr.evidence: Controlled quality-cost comparisons and ablations examine CrystAF, with post-training transfer to Clari-M and MolCrystalFlow.
uIO57iRdYr.claimed_gains: UMA relaxation repairs local clashes but makes generation 6--26$\times$ slower.
uIO57iRdYr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the controlled empirical comparisons and computational-cost accounting useful.
uIO57iRdYr.main_concern: The mechanistic contribution is limited because feasibility filtering explains validity gains and the distinct physical information supplied by UMA remains unclear.

eUiXxsFZt8.one_liner: Answer-preserving image perturbations invert vision-language confidence and degrade confidence-gated selection.
eUiXxsFZt8.problem: Confidence gates can fail if adversaries change confidence without changing a model's generated answer.
eUiXxsFZt8.method: The study optimizes bounded image perturbations to corrupt confidence while constraining answer tokens and verifying byte-identical regenerated answers. It evaluates oracle and label-free attackers, unchanged explanations, score-only API attacks, and defenses.
eUiXxsFZt8.key_idea: Optimize image perturbations against confidence readouts while enforcing exactly unchanged generated answers.
eUiXxsFZt8.evidence: Experiments span four VLMs, three benchmarks, seven confidence readouts, multiple attack assumptions, and defenses including trained probes and independent verifiers.
eUiXxsFZt8.claimed_gains: At an $L_\infty$ budget of $8/255$, the oracle attacker drives discrimination below chance in 83 of the 84 combinations, while the label-free attacker does so for six of the seven readouts on every model and benchmark.
eUiXxsFZt8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the carefully controlled attack evaluation, strict answer-preservation checks, and broad experimental coverage.
eUiXxsFZt8.main_concern: The practical representativeness of white-box access and specialized confidence estimators for deployed VLM systems remains unclear.

yfaHTacEno.one_liner: Functional-path loss decomposition examines why constrained fine-tuning updates still forget and how optimizer placement changes retention.
yfaHTacEno.problem: Parameter or gradient constraints do not establish how the intervening training trajectory preserves old-task outputs.
yfaHTacEno.method: The analysis decomposes old-loss changes into controlled direction, gradient staleness, probe mismatch, and finite-step effects. Matched QLoRA interventions vary constraint granularity, placement around Adam, and replay schedules while measuring endpoint and sampled-path retention.
yfaHTacEno.key_idea: Decompose old-task loss along realized updates to distinguish local constraint satisfaction from accumulated functional forgetting.
yfaHTacEno.evidence: Theory, counterexamples, controlled QLoRA studies on 7B models, checkpointed generation, and short sequential-task comparisons test the functional-path account.
yfaHTacEno.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the analytical organization and controlled experiments, particularly the retention differences from constraint placement around Adam.
yfaHTacEno.main_concern: The decomposition has limited demonstrated predictive value and does not clearly explain the main multi-step generation results.

kWfyqJ8dkd.one_liner: Crossed gold and predicted specifications with exact and language-model constructors diagnose recommendation-agent failures.
kWfyqJ8dkd.problem: End-to-end recommendation success conflates request grounding, compliant set construction, and recovery from earlier mistakes.
kWfyqJ8dkd.method: MosaicRec separates specification grounding from set construction using solver-certified feasible tasks from Goodreads and Amazon. Crossed evaluations and counterexample search assess specification safety and compare generated recommendations with exact execution of cached specifications.
kWfyqJ8dkd.key_idea: Cross gold or predicted specifications with exact or language-model set constructors, and search for counterexamples to specification safety.
kWfyqJ8dkd.evidence: Held-out Goodreads tasks and an independently constructed Amazon split include personalized constraints joining user histories to catalog metadata.
kWfyqJ8dkd.reviewer_consensus: Review strengths emphasize stage-specific diagnosis and semantic checks of intermediate specifications, with another reviewer praising readability.
kWfyqJ8dkd.main_concern: Template-generated, explicitly specified requests may not represent real user ambiguity, and their correspondence to gold specifications needs stronger validation.

YXsfYtQB1h.one_liner: Cloned-state counterfactual rollouts train world dynamics on all branches while restricting action imitation to successful segments.
YXsfYtQB1h.problem: World action models need diverse experience for dynamics learning but successful behavior for action supervision.
YXsfYtQB1h.method: PlayWAM clones simulator states and collects controlled nominal, perturbed, failing, and recovering branches. It trains dynamics on every branch, imitates successful segments, and learns a lightweight value head to select parallel future–action candidates.
YXsfYtQB1h.key_idea: Separate dynamics supervision from action imitation across same-state counterfactual branches, then rank candidate futures with a learned value head.
YXsfYtQB1h.evidence: Evaluation covers PlayBench, RoboTwin-Play, LIBERO, and eight real-world tasks, including controls across model families and physical robots.
YXsfYtQB1h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the separation of physical evidence from successful behavior and the empirical simulation-to-real evaluation.
YXsfYtQB1h.main_concern: The main text insufficiently explains branch generation, expert action scripts, and value supervision, making the approach's feasibility and scalability difficult to assess.

uXkO3yaysv.one_liner: Fixed-rank subspace protection and neuron recycling address distinct plasticity failures in recurring task-free learning streams.
uXkO3yaysv.problem: Protection against forgetting can reduce plasticity, while neuron activity alone does not ensure continued learning.
uXkO3yaysv.method: The study combines fixed-rank subspace protection with neuron recycling on recurring supervised and reinforcement-learning streams. Analyses and controls examine saturation, mean-input-direction protection, dormant-neuron reactivation, and protected-layer choice.
uXkO3yaysv.key_idea: Cap protected subspace rank to prevent saturation and recycle dormant neurons whose reactivation pathways remain suppressed by projection.
uXkO3yaysv.evidence: CN-ImageNet and CN-Procgen experiments, factorial comparisons, and mean-direction removal controls examine retention, plasticity, and dormancy.
uXkO3yaysv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the joint analysis of forgetting and plasticity useful and recognize distinct saturation and dormancy mechanisms.
uXkO3yaysv.main_concern: The combined method delivers modest or mixed gains and low recall, leaving its retention–plasticity advantage over simpler alternatives uncertain.

YzLVomEJWq.one_liner: Minimax aggregation combines confidence intervals under partially ordered bias bounds for validation-free hyperparameter tuning.
YzLVomEJWq.problem: Existing estimator aggregation methods struggle with multidimensional hyperparameters when bias bounds have only a partial ordering.
YzLVomEJWq.method: OACIS chooses an aggregate that minimizes the worst-case oracle-approximation ratio using estimator intervals and the partial order of latent bias bounds. The paper characterizes the minimax problem and gives a linear-time algorithm.
YzLVomEJWq.key_idea: Minimize the worst-case oracle ratio over estimators consistent with observed confidence intervals and a partial ordering of unknown bias bounds.
YzLVomEJWq.evidence: Theory covers boundedness, uniqueness, stability, and statistical error, with evaluations on mobile-health simulation, spatial adaptation, and web-policy estimation.
YzLVomEJWq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the exact minimax characterization and stability analysis for aggregation without direct validation.
YzLVomEJWq.main_concern: The practical justification and tightness of ordered bias bounds, especially in the web-policy example, remain unclear.

yNQKyLxXke.one_liner: Feasibility-gated candidate selection and dispersion-weighted diversity feedback guide generative video super-resolution.
yNQKyLxXke.problem: Global preference rewards struggle to preserve video structure while allowing plausible variation in ambiguous local details.
yNQKyLxXke.method: FGPO screens candidates with low-resolution-conditioned detail plausibility and temporal consistency before Pareto selection. Low-resolution-aligned dispersion masks weight an inter-candidate feature-diversity bonus, producing scalar or pairwise optimization feedback.
yNQKyLxXke.key_idea: Gate candidate eligibility by fidelity and temporal feasibility, then weight diversity feedback toward high-dispersion regions consistent with low-resolution structure.
yNQKyLxXke.evidence: Reviewers report evaluations on four datasets, including YouHQ-40, with ablations, human evaluation, and different optimization algorithms.
yNQKyLxXke.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the fidelity-versus-detail trade-off as well motivated and report useful empirical improvements.
yNQKyLxXke.main_concern: The reward specification contains inconsistencies, including claims of continuity despite a hard feasible/infeasible partition and conflicting descriptions of infeasible-candidate handling.

RRIaUCGMrF.one_liner: A fixed post-commitment delay freezes diffusion-language-model tokens and reuses their cached keys and values.
RRIaUCGMrF.problem: Output-distribution convergence tests can miss stale KV effects on other tokens after a position has committed.
RRIaUCGMrF.method: The paper shuffles convergence-derived freeze times across tokens at equal compute to test whether token-specific timing matters. It replaces those signals with a uniform post-commitment delay and analyzes expected remaining KV motion.
RRIaUCGMrF.key_idea: Freeze every committed token after the same number of denoising steps and reuse its cached keys and values.
RRIaUCGMrF.evidence: Experiments cover five open diffusion language models with saturation analysis, shuffled freeze schedules, alternative signals, and a token-independent scheduling result.
RRIaUCGMrF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the diagnosis of the mismatch between monitored output convergence and propagated KV staleness.
RRIaUCGMrF.main_concern: The paper needs clearer positioning relative to existing delayed caching and convergence analyses that target different sources of freezing error.

DDSxCSaehJ.one_liner: Persistent coordination tokens receive centralized representation supervision while each decentralized actor updates memory from local observations.
DDSxCSaehJ.problem: Decentralized agents must coordinate from local histories without access to joint observations at execution.
DDSxCSaehJ.method: DSM equips each actor with persistent coordination tokens updated through a retention layer alongside local inputs. During training, a centralized teacher supervises token representations and guides the policy through action distributions.
DDSxCSaehJ.key_idea: Update persistent actor tokens from local history and distill centralized joint-observation representations into those tokens during training.
DDSxCSaehJ.evidence: Evaluation covers 44 tasks in six benchmarks, with reviews noting ten seeds, per-task reporting, and shuffled distillation-target controls.
DDSxCSaehJ.claimed_gains: The abstract reports the highest CTDE aggregate performance on all six benchmarks, matching or exceeding the best CTCE baseline on five, with about 68% fewer deployed parameters than the reference GRU actor.
DDSxCSaehJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit broad empirical evaluation and the extension of centralized guidance to decentralized recurrent memory.
DDSxCSaehJ.main_concern: The evidence does not isolate the architectural and distillation contributions or establish that tokens retain useful coordination information.

QChRzNBzza.one_liner: Coupled state-space transitions and adaptive expert routing model temporal EEG evolution together with cross-channel interactions.
QChRzNBzza.problem: Heterogeneous EEG recordings impede transfer, while existing backbones struggle to capture coupled spatial and temporal brain dynamics.
QChRzNBzza.method: BrainMamba represents multi-channel EEG as latent states evolving through structured state-space transitions shaped by cross-channel coupling. Expert routing adaptively specializes these dynamics for heterogeneous neural patterns.
QChRzNBzza.key_idea: Evolve latent EEG states through cross-channel-coupled state-space transitions and specialize their evolution with adaptive expert routing.
QChRzNBzza.evidence: Reviews describe pretraining and transfer on 10 EEG datasets, leave-one-dataset-out experiments, and independently collected sleep EEG validation.
QChRzNBzza.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit multi-dataset evaluation and the treatment of heterogeneous EEG recordings.
QChRzNBzza.main_concern: A reviewer questions whether pretraining on unlabeled target datasets confounds the claimed cross-dataset generalization.

dBnjPyGMhk.one_liner: Normalized, clipped loss-gradient sensitivities weight reconstruction errors during one-shot LLM pruning.
dBnjPyGMhk.problem: Uniform reconstruction weights let numerous low-sensitivity token occurrences dilute priority for occurrences that matter more to global loss.
dBnjPyGMhk.method: SWR defines occurrence sensitivity as the squared norm of the loss gradient at a module's output. It normalizes and clips these sensitivities into reconstruction weights inserted into existing pruning solvers.
dBnjPyGMhk.key_idea: Weight module reconstruction by normalized, clipped squared output-gradient norms for each calibration-token occurrence.
dBnjPyGMhk.evidence: Experiments cover five pruning methods and 11 models at 70% unstructured sparsity, WikiText-2, seven zero-shot tasks, and fixed-mask sensitivity interventions.
dBnjPyGMhk.claimed_gains: The abstract reports a median relative WikiText-2 perplexity reduction of 3.0% and a median mean-accuracy improvement of 0.38 percentage points across seven zero-shot tasks.
dBnjPyGMhk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the motivation and extensive evaluation across models, pruning methods, and ablations.
dBnjPyGMhk.main_concern: Reviewers find the pruning baselines outdated and request integration with stronger recent methods.

sJ5JnQwRos.one_liner: A multi-agent research pipeline combines hypothesis debate, execution repair, result verification, and reusable lessons across research runs.
sJ5JnQwRos.problem: Autonomous research systems struggle to revise failed research designs, preserve experience, and verify numerical claims against execution records.
sJ5JnQwRos.method: AutoResearchClaw runs a 23-stage pipeline from research questions to experiments and manuscripts, with structured debate and configurable human intervention. It uses Pivot/Refine decisions, a measurement registry, and lessons retained across runs.
sJ5JnQwRos.key_idea: Verify reported results against an execution registry and convert failures and research decisions into reusable lessons for subsequent runs.
sJ5JnQwRos.evidence: ARC-Bench evaluates 55 topics across machine learning, high-energy physics, metabolic modeling, statistics, and quantum computing, including baseline comparisons on 25 machine-learning topics.
sJ5JnQwRos.claimed_gains: ARC scores 0.596 versus 0.511 for AIDE and 0.419 for AI Scientist v2, with Overall performance rising from 0.564 to 0.827 after three persistent iterations.
sJ5JnQwRos.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical research pipeline and its support for traceable, verifiable experimental results.
sJ5JnQwRos.main_concern: The evaluation does not adequately establish general research ability or reliable improvement beyond the benchmark's limited tasks.

fisfZ9r56Q.one_liner: HILT pairs localized student continuation contexts with hazard evidence for a privileged teacher, then transfers guidance through on-policy self-distillation.
fisfZ9r56Q.problem: Trajectory-level safety feedback identifies unsafe episodes without specifying where correction should begin or which consequences should guide supervision.
fisfZ9r56Q.method: HILT couples a student's starting context with verifier evidence supplied to a privileged teacher to supervise safer continuations. On-policy self-distillation transfers guidance through student-sampled text, yielding a policy that needs no safety verifier at inference.
fisfZ9r56Q.key_idea: Localized continuation prefixes and evidence of harmful consequences jointly condition teacher guidance for student-sampled self-distillation.
fisfZ9r56Q.evidence: Experiments cover five models from three families, whole-trajectory self-distillation comparisons, and localization validation on 350 annotated trajectories with five-fold cross-validation.
fisfZ9r56Q.claimed_gains: Against whole-trajectory self-distillation, HILT reports absolute over-refusal reductions of 6.09%–23.60%, while aggregate reasoning accuracy remains within 1% of each base model in absolute terms.
fisfZ9r56Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the safety-utility motivation and the depth of experiments on focused correction of hazardous behavior.
fisfZ9r56Q.main_concern: Reviewers find hazard localization's specific contribution unresolved because the main ablation simultaneously changes prefixes, privileged evidence, and teacher instructions.

6usIPvzDy9.one_liner: RaOT jointly matches attention heads and within-head rotations, then aligns residual streams with LayerNorm-compatible rotations before merging.
6usIPvzDy9.problem: Permutation and transport-plan alignment cannot express all continuous Transformer symmetries needed for model merging.
6usIPvzDy9.method: RaOT estimates attention-head correspondences and rotations in one exact solve from a few unlabeled images, then applies a mean-preserving residual-stream rotation. An optional safe variant compares transformations with the identity and can decline alignment.
6usIPvzDy9.key_idea: Architecture-compatible rotations align attention subspaces and residual streams beyond the unit permutations expressible by transport plans.
6usIPvzDy9.evidence: Proofs characterize rotation constraints, while independently trained ImageNet ViT pairs support interpolation-barrier, component-ablation, and frozen-feature linear-probe comparisons.
