Ya4bvnVH9M.key_idea: Estimates intermediate-state terminal potential via Koopman transport to focus exact oracle queries on Pareto-decision-uncertain Hamming edits.
Ya4bvnVH9M.evidence: Decision-linear query-complexity bound and empirical comparisons on peptide and DNA sequence design benchmarks.
Ya4bvnVH9M.claimed_gains: Achieves competitive or superior terminal Pareto quality with up to 99x fewer unique oracle queries than compared discrete multi-objective generative baselines.
Ya4bvnVH9M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight strong query efficiency (up to ~99x fewer oracle queries) on peptide and DNA design tasks, backed by mathematical query-complexity analysis.
Ya4bvnVH9M.main_concern: A simpler finite-time linear observer matches or outperforms the Koopman observer on several metrics, and baseline comparisons are not fully budget-matched or wet-lab validated.

mcW0WyMKWW.one_liner: Attaches learnable Latent Reward Registers to a frozen DiT to provide dense differentiable preference rewards for training and sampling.
mcW0WyMKWW.problem: Sparse terminal preference rewards in diffusion alignment create severe credit-assignment difficulty and require costly policy-gradient rollouts.
mcW0WyMKWW.method: Learnable position-free register tokens read intermediate noisy DiT latents without altering the generator's velocity field, enabling per-step Reward-Gradient On-Policy Distillation (RG-OPD) and training-free Reward-Guided Sampling (RGS).
mcW0WyMKWW.key_idea: Prepends auxiliary register tokens to a frozen DiT to extract dense, differentiable preference gradients across all denoising timesteps.
mcW0WyMKWW.evidence: Evaluated across two backbones at high noise (t = 0.8) and compared against online diffusion RL baselines such as Flow-GRPO.
mcW0WyMKWW.claimed_gains: RG-OPD outperforms online RL baselines while reducing GPU hours by up to 33x.
mcW0WyMKWW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the frozen-DiT register stream simple and effective for extracting stable high-noise (t = 0.8) latent rewards usable in both training and inference.
mcW0WyMKWW.main_concern: Evaluation is circular (using HPS/ImageReward as both training proxy and main metric without human studies), the 33x speedup omits register training cost, and DiNa-LRM is missing from RGS comparisons.

RT76AAfPOv.one_liner: Improves multimodal knowledge editing generality by aligning latent adversarial perturbations onto a low-rank subspace.
RT76AAfPOv.problem: Intrinsic multimodal knowledge editing achieves high reliability and locality on exact edit samples but fails to generalize across semantically equivalent visual and linguistic variations.
RT76AAfPOv.method: ASAM combines Latent Adversarial Robustification (LAR), which generates challenging perturbations in the joint latent space from a single edit sample, with Rank-Constrained Subspace Learning (RCSL), which enforces low-rank alignment at the edit layer via a singular-value objective.
RT76AAfPOv.key_idea: Generates joint-latent adversarial variants from a single edit sample and aligns their edit-layer representations onto a low-rank subspace while detaching the original state.
RT76AAfPOv.evidence: Evaluated as a plug-and-play objective across four editors (WISE, MEND, T-Patcher, UniKE), multiple MLLM backbones, and E-VQA and E-IC benchmarks.
RT76AAfPOv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that ASAM is a clear, coherent, plug-and-play regularization approach that improves multimodal editing generalization without extra paired samples.
RT76AAfPOv.main_concern: Reviewers note locality drops (M-Loc.) alongside generality gains, question whether latent perturbations preserve semantics versus random noise, and cite missing comparisons to ODEdit.

Eyht9PsI5k.one_liner: Establishes minimax optimal excess risk for user-level private heavy-tailed SCO under moment bounds using O(1/epsilon) users.
Eyht9PsI5k.problem: User-level differentially private stochastic convex optimization previously assumed uniformly bounded gradients rather than heavy-tailed gradient distributions.
Eyht9PsI5k.method: Under (epsilon, delta)-user-level DP, they replace uniform Lipschitz bounds with second- and k-th moment bounds on random sample Lipschitz parameters. They develop multi-stage private mean-estimation and fused adaptive DP-SCO algorithms using FriendlyCore, outlier filtering, and dynamic clipping to achieve minimax optimal excess risk up to logarithmic factors.
Eyht9PsI5k.key_idea: Replaces uniform Lipschitz assumptions with 2nd- and k-th moment bounds in user-level DP-SCO via outlier-filtered adaptive clipping and FriendlyCore aggregation.
Eyht9PsI5k.evidence: Supported solely by theoretical upper and lower bounds in 27 pages of proofs, with zero empirical experiments.
Eyht9PsI5k.claimed_gains: Achieves minimax optimal excess population risk up to logarithmic factors using only O-tilde(1/epsilon) users (improving over prior n > d/epsilon requirements).
Eyht9PsI5k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper rigorously closes theoretical gaps for user-level DP-SCO and mean estimation under heavy-tailed moment assumptions.
Eyht9PsI5k.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the complete absence of experiments for complex multi-stage algorithms requiring unknown moment parameters, alongside dense, hard-to-follow presentation.

4Qmr2doVWe.one_liner: Synthesizes diverse tail-class graph nodes via LLM auxiliary subclasses and prototype-boundary filtering, then imputes debiased edges.
4Qmr2doVWe.problem: Long-tailed text-attributed graph learning suffers from overconcentrated synthetic tail nodes and noisy edges during graph augmentation.
4Qmr2doVWe.method: BEAST measures latent inter-class prototype distances to identify competing classes and prompts LLMs to generate diverse auxiliary subclasses for tail classes, filtered by boundary margins and an LLM critic. A trained edge predictor then imputes debiased connections for synthetic nodes under parent-class hierarchical supervision.
4Qmr2doVWe.key_idea: Generates LLM auxiliary subclasses separated from competing class prototypes and connects synthetic tail nodes using a debiased edge predictor.
4Qmr2doVWe.evidence: Evaluated on text-attributed graph benchmarks including Cora, Citeseer, Photo, Computer, and Children across Acc, F1, GMean, and bAcc.
4Qmr2doVWe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree combining boundary-aware tail-class semantic synthesis with topology imputation is well-motivated and coherent.
4Qmr2doVWe.main_concern: Reviewers find imbalance-metric margins often within standard deviation, flag an inconsistent GMean/bAcc table entry, note missing head-vs-tail breakdowns, and question compute cost and edge-predictor domain shift.

n1OLNd3zAC.one_liner: Halts compound LLM programs early via a runtime verification core that certifies remaining calls cannot alter the output.
n1OLNd3zAC.problem: Compound LLM workflows execute redundant model calls even after the final declared output is already mathematically determined.
n1OLNd3zAC.method: CertiJoin pairs program adapters—declaring output rules and call outcome domains—with a shared runtime checking core that tracks dependencies and state-bound certificates across nested joins. It proves exact output preservation without probability calibration and shows optimality across four join types and local pruning.
n1OLNd3zAC.key_idea: Verifies at runtime via dependency-aware certificates that pending LLM calls cannot change the declared join output, cancelling them immediately.
n1OLNd3zAC.evidence: Supported by optimality/preservation proofs and experiments on online nested code validation, 2,000-request majority voting, live serving, and Qwen3-8B chain-of-thought reasoning.
n1OLNd3zAC.claimed_gains: Cuts mean latency by 37.6% and tokens by 32.6% in nested code validation, finishes 84.5% of majority-voting requests early (27.6% live latency cut), and reduces Qwen3-8B CoT latency by up to 26.7% with exact output preservation.
n1OLNd3zAC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the deterministic certification framework is technically sound, cleanly scoped, and delivers real cancellation savings.
n1OLNd3zAC.main_concern: Reviewers view algorithmic novelty as incremental over standard short-circuit evaluation and question scalability given the 16-leaf/100k-assignment enumeration cap and failure-dominated code-validation savings.

Mz1BjZ8hK7.one_liner: Studies LLM deception by separating self-reported factual belief from stated commitment across benchmarks and prompting conditions.
Mz1BjZ8hK7.problem: The relationship between an LLM's internal belief in factual truth and its expressed confidence when generating deceptive responses is poorly understood.
Mz1BjZ8hK7.method: The authors measure both verbalized numerical and logit-based confidence across deception benchmarks and model families, distinguishing reported belief (truth likelihood) from commitment (willingness to assert and defend a claim) under prompting, fine-tuning, and backdoor interventions.
Mz1BjZ8hK7.key_idea: Decomposes LLM confidence during deception into reported factual belief and assertive commitment, showing that commitment scales up while belief remains low.
Mz1BjZ8hK7.evidence: Evaluated across multiple deception benchmarks, model families, prompting conditions, preference fine-tuning, human evaluations, and backdoor experiments.
Mz1BjZ8hK7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the conceptual distinction between belief and commitment insightful and appreciate the broad, transparent experimental investigation.
Mz1BjZ8hK7.main_concern: Reviewers question construct validity because belief and commitment are self-reported, and note that belief-based detection struggles to separate deliberate deception from ordinary factual errors or backdoored false beliefs.

mR68gGETr1.one_liner: Proves sharp KL-budget thresholds governing how many parallel sampling rounds masked diffusion models need on correlated bit pairs.
mR68gGETr1.problem: It is unclear how accurate a masked diffusion model's conditional predictions must be to preserve shallow parallel generation.
mR68gGETr1.method: Analyzing n independent correlated bit pairs under coherent conditional heads and exchangeable mismatch laws, the authors prove matching upper and lower KL-budget bounds for K-round parallel sampling, showing a geometric schedule suffices within budget while larger budgets force TV error to one.
mR68gGETr1.key_idea: Establishes a sharp Theta_{K,epsilon}(n^{-1/[2(K-1)]}) KL-budget threshold separating successful K-round parallel masked diffusion sampling from total-variation failure.
mR68gGETr1.evidence: Supported by minimax upper and lower bound proofs, heterogeneous extensions, and certified finite-dimensional experiments.
mR68gGETr1.claimed_gains: Proves a sharp KL budget of Theta_{K,epsilon}(n^{-1/[2(K-1)]}) for fixed K >= 2 rounds, and shows vanishing joint KL and single-token errors can still require Omega(log n / log log n) expected rounds.
mR68gGETr1.reviewer_consensus: Most reviewers view the minimax characterization as mathematically clean, rigorous, and surprising.
mR68gGETr1.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the dense, obscure presentation and undefined notation, and question practical applicability beyond the idealized correlated-bit-pair model.

NnhZDJv3hE.one_liner: Factorizes world models into agent and reusable background dynamics modules connected by an information-bottlenecked latent interface.
NnhZDJv3hE.problem: Monolithic latent world models couple agent and environment dynamics, preventing reuse of learned environment dynamics across different agents.
NnhZDJv3hE.method: BRICKS-WM splits a DreamerV3-style world model into an actuated Agent module and an external Background module bridged by a compact latent interface with an information bottleneck. For transfer, a frozen Background module is recomposed with a newly trained Agent module via an adapted interface.
NnhZDJv3hE.key_idea: Factorizes world-model transitions into an Agent module and a Background module linked by a bottlenecked latent interface so the Background module can be frozen and reused.
NnhZDJv3hE.evidence: Evaluated on continuous control tasks (DeepMind Control, CarRacing) across 14 source-target transfer pairs against DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2, plus perception-only controls.
NnhZDJv3hE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the modular Agent/Background decomposition and information-bottleneck interface intuitive and well-motivated.
NnhZDJv3hE.main_concern: Reviewers note weak transfer gains (outperforming scratch DreamerV3 on only 2 of 14 pairs), missing warm-started/fine-tuned DreamerV3 baselines, and lack of statistical significance tests.

xrxtRrN5bs.one_liner: Modulates GFlowNet molecular construction actions via preference-dependent feature gates and optional learned temperatures.
xrxtRrN5bs.problem: Multi-objective molecular GFlowNets struggle to both survive strict multi-property screens and reliably shift sampled molecules when user preferences change.
xrxtRrN5bs.method: PrefGateGFN applies preference-dependent feature gates to modulate action scores, pairs them with optional learned sampling temperatures, and uses dynamic reward normalization during training.
xrxtRrN5bs.key_idea: Uses preference-dependent feature gates to reorder molecular construction actions alongside optional learned temperatures and dynamic reward normalization.
xrxtRrN5bs.evidence: Exact-grid distribution checks, a three-objective fragment task, and a 14-objective screen across five protein targets comparing against MOGFN and HN-GFN.
xrxtRrN5bs.claimed_gains: On the 14-objective screen across five targets, PrefGateGFN averages 133 distinct qualifying molecules per 1,000 draws, outperforming MOGFN-PC by factors of 1.93 in qualifying molecules and 2.10 in qualifying scaffolds; normalization raises mean hypervolume from 0.668 to 0.885.
xrxtRrN5bs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise testing preference shifts on frozen policies and thorough exact-distribution and screen evaluations.
xrxtRrN5bs.main_concern: Coverage gains in ablations are driven largely by dynamic reward normalization rather than gating, and baselines were not trained with the same normalization.

TVsogD4IYT.one_liner: Characterizes output-preserving parameter-space path barriers (ghost directions) and branch intersection lattices in shallow ReLU networks.
TVsogD4IYT.problem: It is unclear when two parameter settings of a shallow ReLU network with identical outputs on finite data can be connected by an output-preserving path.
TVsogD4IYT.method: Using an output-space algebraic-geometry view, each activation cell is represented by its output-image closure (linear branch) and compared against its shared wall-image closure to define ghost directions. Refining cells by output-weight signs yields a finite graph for exact fiber components, alongside an analysis of maximal-branch intersection lattices.
TVsogD4IYT.key_idea: Identifies ghost directions outside shared wall-image closures as obstructions to output-preserving paths and builds a sign-refined finite graph to compute exact parameter-fiber components.
TVsogD4IYT.evidence: Theoretical proofs, small-network examples (including six planar inputs), and an empirical NTK comparison showing jumps across ghost walls.
TVsogD4IYT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the algebraic-geometry formulation and identification of ghost-direction path barriers are mathematically rigorous and original.
TVsogD4IYT.main_concern: Reviewers note the two sections (ghost directions and intersection lattices) feel disconnected and the scope is limited to tiny shallow networks without real training validation.

ovGu851Kc4.one_liner: Jointly RL-trains skill selection, Triton kernel generation, and execution-verified skill summarization within a single shared LLM backbone.
ovGu851Kc4.problem: Agentic GPU kernel optimization struggles to discover, select, and reuse optimization techniques that adapt as the policy's capabilities evolve.
ovGu851Kc4.method: CORAL shares one LLM backbone across three agents—Skill Selection (BM25 + LLM reranking), Policy (multi-turn Triton kernel generation), and Skill Summary—connected to a dynamic skill library. Skills are admitted only after execution verifies first-turn speedups, and all three agents are initialized with diversity-filtered SFT and trained jointly via multi-turn REINFORCE.
ovGu851Kc4.key_idea: Couples skill selection, multi-turn kernel generation, and execution-verified skill summarization in one LLM jointly optimized with multi-turn REINFORCE.
ovGu851Kc4.evidence: Evaluated on KernelBench Levels 1-3 against a reproduced Dr. Kernel-14B baseline, with ablations on inference skills, joint training, learned selection, and diversity filtering.
ovGu851Kc4.claimed_gains: CORAL-14B achieves 37.2%, 70.6%, and 32.2% on KernelBench Levels 1, 2, and 3 under Fast_1 using the last output of three-turn rollouts.
ovGu851Kc4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the end-to-end co-evolution of skill discovery, selection, and execution-verified utilization is practical and well-suited to kernel optimization.
ovGu851Kc4.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental novelty over SkillRL/Skill1, gains that largely vanish at 14 turns, single-run variance, and reliance on a reproduced baseline.

pwpZIELri3.one_liner: Predicts coding-agent terminal rewards from trajectory prefixes using task- and stage-specific rubrics synthesized from historical experience.
pwpZIELri3.problem: Long-horizon coding agents only receive verifiable rewards at rollout completion, wasting inference tokens and creating sparse RL signals.
pwpZIELri3.method: Contextual Early Reward (CER) retrieves related historical task experiences to synthesize adaptive task- and stage-specific rubrics, then scores sibling trajectory prefixes side-by-side to predict terminal rewards for test-time search and RL training.
pwpZIELri3.key_idea: Synthesizes adaptive rubrics from historical task experiences to score sibling coding-agent trajectory prefixes before rollout completion.
pwpZIELri3.evidence: Evaluated on SWE-bench Verified for test-time scaling (Nemotron 3 Ultra, Qwen 3.6 27B) and RL training.
pwpZIELri3.claimed_gains: Improves RM@8 by 4.2 pp on Nemotron 3 Ultra (matching best baseline with 15.2% tokens) and 2.0 pp on Qwen 3.6 27B; exceeds full-rollout TMax by 1.9 pp in RL using 52.7% fewer online policy-and-judge tokens.
pwpZIELri3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical value of early prefix feedback and the strong ablation showing side-by-side sibling scoring matters.
pwpZIELri3.main_concern: Reviewers note that TTS compares beam search against static baselines, offline experience-bank/rubric costs are excluded from token savings, and direct prefix ranking accuracy is not reported.

nLBvyM9Xo0.one_liner: Introduces a benchmark aligning sequences, images, and multi-resolution graphs to isolate structural abstraction in traffic forecasting.
nLBvyM9Xo0.problem: Changing input representations and forecasting architectures simultaneously prevents isolating how much structural abstraction traffic forecasting requires.
nLBvyM9Xo0.method: GB-Traffic aligns historical signals, image encodings, and coarse-to-fine temporal-region graphs (T-GRIG) to identical targets across six datasets, using a shared ridge predictor and fixed regional readout to isolate input composition, resolution, and edge placement.
nLBvyM9Xo0.key_idea: Holds the forecasting predictor and targets fixed across aligned sequence, image, and multi-resolution graph representations to treat structural resolution as an explicit variable.
nLBvyM9Xo0.evidence: Evaluated across six traffic datasets (including four-dataset matched diagnostics and PeMS04 threshold sweeps) with count-matched random edges and regular partitions.
nLBvyM9Xo0.claimed_gains: On the PeMS04 threshold sweep, medium resolution uses 54.2% fewer regions than fine with 1.57% lower MAE.
nLBvyM9Xo0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the goal of decoupling structural abstraction from forecasting backbones under matched targets.
nLBvyM9Xo0.main_concern: Reviewers note that conclusions are tied to the single T-GRIG/region-to-sensor pipeline, lack of road-network topology in per-sensor graphs, and fixed 12-step horizons.

L6sUUuJ9SY.one_liner: Proves that pre-layer-norm and linear-attention blocks are almost always surjective, implying inverse mappings exist for arbitrary outputs.
L6sUUuJ9SY.problem: It is unclear whether modern neural architectures are surjective, which would imply any target output—including harmful content—has a corresponding input.
L6sUUuJ9SY.method: The authors analyze surjectivity of architectural building blocks, proving that networks with pre-layer normalization, skip connections, and linear-attention modules are almost always surjective, and extend this as corollaries to GPT-style transformers and deterministic-ODE diffusion models.
L6sUUuJ9SY.key_idea: Establishes almost-always surjectivity for pre-layer-norm residual blocks and linear-attention layers via polynomial and topological arguments.
L6sUUuJ9SY.evidence: Purely theoretical proofs (including Theorem 3.4 on Retention and negative results on softmax attention).
L6sUUuJ9SY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mathematical proofs are clean, readable, and establish interesting surjectivity results for modern neural network blocks.
L6sUUuJ9SY.main_concern: Reviewers argue the safety and generative-modeling implications in the abstract do not hold for real models because the proofs assume equal input-output dimensions and ignore final LayerNorm/RMSNorm, LM heads, and VAE decoders.

2l2Uh5Wi13.one_liner: Aggregates multiple neural SAT solvers by grouping variables with consistent assignment and relational votes into Heider blocks for local search.
2l2Uh5Wi13.problem: Naive per-variable voting across multiple neural SAT solvers discards inter-variable relational structure needed to construct consistent satisfying assignments.
2l2Uh5Wi13.method: cdNSE formalizes solver agreement on both variable assignments and pairwise variable relationships, using these equivalence relations to partition variables into bounded-size Heider blocks. These blocks then define structured block moves to guide stochastic local search.
2l2Uh5Wi13.key_idea: Partitioning variables into Heider blocks based on pairwise relational agreement across neural SAT solvers to guide local-search block moves.
2l2Uh5Wi13.evidence: Benchmarked on 123 instances from six SATLIB datasets against eleven fusion-based and ten learning-based methods.
2l2Uh5Wi13.claimed_gains: Improves the solve rate by a relative improvement of 14.1% over the baseline (abstract truncated).
2l2Uh5Wi13.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that ensembling neural SAT solvers using two-level variable and relational consistency is an interesting and underexplored problem formulation.
2l2Uh5Wi13.main_concern: Reviewers point out the absence of standalone neural SAT solver baselines to show the ensemble beats individual solvers, unconvincing justification for relational agreement when solvers can agree wrongly, and unclear pseudocode.

k2TTm0bDYP.one_liner: Bounds inherited and newly injected watermark information under text rewrites using erased, transmitted, and fresh information budgets.
k2TTm0bDYP.problem: When watermarked text is rewritten by another model, it is unclear how much of the upstream watermark survives and how much new watermark signal can be injected.
k2TTm0bDYP.method: The authors decompose a rewrite into erased, transmitted, and fresh information budgets, proving a key-flow theorem where inherited keys are capped by the transmitted budget and task fidelity sets a retention floor. They derive exact floors for statistic preservation via conditional resampling and exact injection optima for binary symmetric rewriting.
k2TTm0bDYP.key_idea: Decomposing text rewrites into erased, transmitted, and fresh information budgets to bound inherited watermark retention and fresh key injection.
k2TTm0bDYP.evidence: Theoretical proofs with tight finite-alphabet examples and controlled LLM experiments using Qwen3-4B on 64 reports.
k2TTm0bDYP.claimed_gains: Qwen3-4B rewrites all four target facts correctly in 64/64 reports while inherited-key detection falls from 14/64 upstream to 1/64.
k2TTm0bDYP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the three-budget decomposition and formal bounds provide a clean, technically rigorous framework for analyzing watermark survival under rewriting.
k2TTm0bDYP.main_concern: Reviewers note that the task-relation bounds rely on idealized assumptions that do not connect directly to real-world natural-language semantic rewriting tasks like paraphrasing or summarization.

0lsa7teWtR.one_liner: Shows numerical scale of embeddings causes RQ-VAE codebook collapse and proposes reconstruction-loss calibration to restore diverse Semantic IDs.
0lsa7teWtR.problem: Embeddings that yield identical pairwise recommendation rankings can produce completely different learned Semantic IDs, collapsing to a single code at native numerical scales.
0lsa7teWtR.method: The authors show that rescaling pretrained SASRec embeddings preserves rankings while preventing RQ-VAE codebook collapse because reconstruction loss and its latent gradient scale quadratically relative to quantization terms. They propose a reconstruction-loss calibration that achieves non-collapsed codebooks without altering the original item embeddings.
0lsa7teWtR.key_idea: Calibrating RQ-VAE reconstruction loss to counter quadratic gradient scaling relative to quantization terms without rescaling input embeddings.
0lsa7teWtR.evidence: Experiments on three Amazon datasets using SASRec embeddings and a TIGER-style T5 encoder-decoder generative recommender across nine paired runs.
0lsa7teWtR.claimed_gains: Calibration improves Hit@10 and NDCG@10 in all nine paired runs across three Amazon datasets, matching the accuracy of direct embedding rescaling.
0lsa7teWtR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that demonstrating how numerical scale drives RQ-VAE codebook collapse under fixed rankings is an insightful and well-isolated empirical finding.
0lsa7teWtR.main_concern: Reviewers note that validation is limited to RQ-VAE tokenizers and a single T5-based generator family, leaving generality to other tokenizers and decoder-only recommenders unestablished.

Jw2rCRp0m4.one_liner: Evaluates safety LLM-judges on in-context sensitivity and steerability across changing safety policies that conflict with internal priors.
Jw2rCRp0m4.problem: LLM-as-a-judge safety evaluators are mostly tested on static human-agreement benchmarks, leaving their ability to adapt to new in-context facts or custom safety policies unknown.
Jw2rCRp0m4.method: The authors evaluate 13 generalist LLMs and dedicated safety judges under novel in-context information and modified safety definitions—including multilingual prompts and response evaluation—to measure context sensitivity and policy steerability.
Jw2rCRp0m4.key_idea: Probes safety judges with novel in-context facts and altered safety policy definitions that contradict internal priors to separate static agreement from context sensitivity and steerability.
Jw2rCRp0m4.evidence: Empirical study across 13 generalist and safety-specific LLM judges on novel-information and policy-variation datasets.
Jw2rCRp0m4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that testing context sensitivity and policy steerability addresses an important practical gap missed by static safety benchmarks.
Jw2rCRp0m4.main_concern: Reviewers criticize ambiguous examples in NovelPrompts, flip-rate metrics that do not confirm correct directional adaptation, and a narrow set of policy variants that may not support broad non-steerability claims.

s5YLl1VTc7.one_liner: Adapts per-step hidden-state update scales online in looped transformers by tracking persistent progress versus centered fluctuations.
s5YLl1VTc7.problem: Looped recurrent reasoning models apply fixed unit update scales at every iteration, wasting loops during steady progress and overshooting during fluctuating updates.
s5YLl1VTc7.method: The authors decompose terminal-loss sensitivity into persistent-progress and centered-fluctuation terms and introduce TAPS, an online scheduler that adapts recurrent step sizes from trajectory statistics without retraining and can also be incorporated into training.
s5YLl1VTc7.key_idea: Decomposes recurrent trajectory dynamics into persistent-progress and centered-fluctuation components to adapt hidden-state update step sizes online.
s5YLl1VTc7.evidence: Theoretical conditions for expected loss reduction plus experiments on structured reasoning tasks (including Sudoku, Maze, and GSM8K) across multiple recurrent architectures.
s5YLl1VTc7.claimed_gains: Incorporating the progress-fluctuation principle into training yields additional accuracy gains with up to 1.56x wall-clock speedup at matched baseline accuracy.
s5YLl1VTc7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like framing update magnitude as a lightweight, training-free control dimension for looped transformers backed by theoretical analysis.
s5YLl1VTc7.main_concern: Reviewers note that accuracy gains are generally small (often under 1 point), fixed-scale baselines are undertuned, and update persistence does not guarantee progress toward the correct solution.

2xog9w4SJv.one_liner: Calibrates interactive world-model camera poses using a multimodal tool-using agent that combines semantic scene editing with physics rollouts.
2xog9w4SJv.problem: Interactive world models ignore physical interactions between the camera carrier and the scene, generating implausible motions such as passing through solid walls.
2xog9w4SJv.method: CarPhy supplies a tool-using agent with multimodal scene and carrier context plus tools for semantic analysis, world editing, and physics-based motion rollout so it adaptively refines scene properties and simulates physically plausible camera trajectories.
2xog9w4SJv.key_idea: Pairs a multimodal agent that infers semantic physical properties and edits reconstructed scenes with physics-engine rollouts to correct interactive world-model camera poses.
2xog9w4SJv.evidence: Evaluated on a newly constructed terrain-and-obstacle test set measuring physical event recognition and pitch-response timing across multiple VLM and LLM backbones.
2xog9w4SJv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating semantic scene interpretation from physics-engine simulation is a well-motivated approach to enforcing carrier physics in interactive world models.
2xog9w4SJv.main_concern: Reviewers point out that experiments fail to isolate the agent's adaptive reasoning from the underlying reconstruction and default physics rollout, making the agentic contribution unclear.

DCknnmIEeh.one_liner: Transfers world-model optimization operators using shared-probe fingerprints and frozen-verifier paired experiments refined from verified contradictions.
DCknnmIEeh.problem: Optimization operators that improve one world model can degrade similar models, while existing automated search methods rely on static observational descriptors and discard failed transfers.
DCknnmIEeh.method: VERDI constructs shared-probe Optimization Fingerprints to retrieve candidate operators, settles each transfer via paired experiments under a frozen verifier that retains null and harmful outcomes, and admits new probes from verified contradictions gated by held-out replay.
DCknnmIEeh.key_idea: Uses shared-probe response fingerprints, frozen-verifier paired settlement, and held-out-gated probe admission from verified contradictions between nearby models to transfer optimization operators.
DCknnmIEeh.evidence: Evaluated across nine world-model backbones, 27 leave-one-backbone-out campaigns, and 216 transfer decisions.
DCknnmIEeh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise separating transfer prediction from frozen-verifier target confirmation and explicitly retaining null and harmful transfer outcomes.
DCknnmIEeh.main_concern: All reviewers flag serious scope inconsistencies between main tables claiming 9 backbones / 27 campaigns / 216 decisions and appendix tables attributing the identical numbers to a 3-backbone / 9-campaign / 72-decision subset.

0DLXUWQGqN.one_liner: Plug-in state controller that detects unproductive deep-research trajectories and steers a frozen host LLM via small logit modifications.
0DLXUWQGqN.problem: Deep Research agents stop prematurely, continue needlessly, or fail to redirect unproductive trajectories, while retraining or heuristic rules are costly or misaligned with utility.
0DLXUWQGqN.method: RIVO estimates the research state from lightweight signals to decide when trajectory redirection is needed, then modifies the frozen Host LLM's token logits to steer generation toward higher-utility directions. The paper also introduces the BrowseCore dataset and proves local utility improvement under value-alignment and bounded curvature.
0DLXUWQGqN.key_idea: Uses a lightweight state-conditioned trigger to apply small token-logit offsets to a frozen Host LLM for adaptive deep-research trajectory rerouting.
0DLXUWQGqN.evidence: Theoretical local-utility guarantee plus experiments on BrowseCore and two additional benchmarks across two Host models with ablations.
0DLXUWQGqN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like decoupling trajectory control from a frozen Host generator and find the problem framing and BrowseCore resource practical.
0DLXUWQGqN.main_concern: Reviewers flag potential test-set leakage from tuning hyperparameters on the 359 BrowseCore evaluation questions, missing latency/compute overhead accounting, and omitted proxy-tuning/controlled-decoding citations.

k29Vjtk65g.one_liner: Calibrates third- and fourth-order functional brain hyperedges with individual gray-matter evidence and aggregates them via sparse reference-state attention.
k29Vjtk65g.problem: Pairwise brain connectivity misses multi-region dependence, while higher-order functional hypergraphs lack subject-specific structural grounding.
k29Vjtk65g.method: HiBrain computes third- and fourth-order cumulant increments relative to lower-order models and calibrates candidate hyperedges using individual gray-matter morphology. It combines joint-evidence sparse attention (with a zero-valued reference state), adjacent-order propagation, and conditional innovation admission for disorder classification.
k29Vjtk65g.key_idea: Combines residualized third/fourth-order functional cumulants calibrated by gray-matter features with reference-state sparse hypergraph attention and conditional admission.
k29Vjtk65g.evidence: Evaluated against 12 methods on ABIDE-II (ASD), REST-MDD (MDD), SRPBS-SCZ (SCZ), and external ABIDE-I transfer.
k29Vjtk65g.claimed_gains: Exceeds the strongest baseline in mean accuracy by 4.54, 6.94, and 6.47 percentage points on ABIDE-II, REST-MDD, and SRPBS-SCZ, by 3.04, 3.04, and 2.99 points over the strongest attention alternative, and by 4.01 points externally on ABIDE-I.
k29Vjtk65g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate conditioning higher-order cumulants on lower-order relations, the zero-reference sparse attention design, and multi-cohort evaluation.
k29Vjtk65g.main_concern: Reviewers note incomplete ablations isolating gray-matter fusion from fourth-order hyperedges, non-independent temporal block sizing across held-out cohorts, and weak justification for gray-matter morphology as connectivity support.

jfWwZNE7i3.one_liner: Training-free Video-LLM token compressor separating reference-frame semantic anchors from motion-and-residual-guided prediction-frame updates using video codecs.
jfWwZNE7i3.problem: Training-free Video-LLM token compression relying solely on token saliency struggles to balance persistent scene context against subtle temporal changes.
jfWwZNE7i3.method: CoGCo uses standard video codec structure to select reference-frame (I-frame) semantic anchors via attention- and diversity-aware scoring, while selecting prediction-frame (P-frame) tokens using camera-compensated motion vectors, residuals, and within-frame diversity (excluding top-attention tokens). Codec frame packets also guide token-budget allocation.
jfWwZNE7i3.key_idea: Exploits video codec I/P-frame structure, motion vectors, and residuals to separate persistent anchor selection from temporal-update token selection.
jfWwZNE7i3.evidence: Evaluated across four video benchmarks and four Video-LLM backbones at 15%, 20%, and 25% token retention settings.
jfWwZNE7i3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the codec-guided separation of persistent I-frame context and P-frame temporal updates intuitive, well-presented, and thoroughly evaluated.
jfWwZNE7i3.main_concern: Reviewers note that reported latency omits decoding/re-encoding and codec-sidecar overhead, dataset-specific hyperparameters hurt generality, and accuracy gains over baselines are modest relative to pipeline complexity.

a56FVSRMv4.one_liner: Adds a frozen ML-predicted Hessian curvature residual to flow matching for molecular conformer and transition-state generation.
a56FVSRMv4.problem: Coordinate-only molecular generative models ignore potential energy surface physics, and first-order forces vanish at stationary points like conformers and transition states.
a56FVSRMv4.method: CurvFM augments flow matching with a curvature loss evaluated using a frozen machine-learned Hessian predictor at both the generated endpoint and reference structure, imposing second-order PES supervision at every training step without expensive quantum-chemical Hessians.
a56FVSRMv4.key_idea: Constrains flow-matching molecular endpoints by matching frozen ML-predicted PES Hessians between generated and reference geometries at each training step.
a56FVSRMv4.evidence: Evaluated on molecular transition-state and conformer generation benchmarks measuring physical fidelity and global structural accuracy.
a56FVSRMv4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that supervising second-order PES curvature with a cheap frozen ML Hessian surrogate is a clean, practical integration for flow matching.
a56FVSRMv4.main_concern: Reviewers question whether matching a frozen surrogate learns the true PES rather than surrogate biases, note missing comparisons with energy-guided or post-refinement baselines, and observe inconsistent physical-metric gains over DiTMC.

ySHySiRaIZ.one_liner: Certifies automated open-ended video evaluators by requiring human-baseline agreement at both intermediate factor judgments and final scores.
ySHySiRaIZ.problem: Automated evaluators for open-ended video understanding can match human final-score correlations while hiding canceling errors in intermediate factual judgments.
ySHySiRaIZ.method: The authors propose a certification paradigm using a shared scoring procedure, expert references, and leave-one-annotator-out human baselines on a calibration panel, requiring automated judges to match or exceed human agreement at every intermediate and final checkpoint. They instantiate it on detailed video captioning with factor-level precision, recall, and F1.
ySHySiRaIZ.key_idea: Requires automated evaluators to match leave-one-out human agreement at every intermediate factor judgment and final score under a shared scoring procedure.
ySHySiRaIZ.evidence: Instantiated on detailed video captioning (64 captions from 61 videos on CaReBench, per reviews), testing individual VLMs and agentic-plus-single-call ensembles.
ySHySiRaIZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that checking intermediate judgments alongside final scores reveals canceling errors missed by aggregate correlation metrics.
ySHySiRaIZ.main_concern: Reviewers note the tiny certification sample (64 captions from 61 videos), single-task validation (captioning only), missing agentic cost/runtime analysis, and modest novelty over FActScore-style claim evaluation.

oXKG319IOO.one_liner: Curates simulation demonstrations for sim-to-real robot co-training by jointly optimizing influence-based trajectory utility and set coverage.
oXKG319IOO.problem: Existing data curation methods for robot policy co-training optimize either individual trajectory utility or dataset diversity separately rather than jointly.
oXKG319IOO.method: TUCO uses closed-loop influence functions to quantify both individual simulation trajectory utility and complementary set-level coverage toward target performance. A performance-aligned subset optimizer then selects a non-redundant subset of simulation demonstrations for sim-to-real co-training.
oXKG319IOO.key_idea: Uses closed-loop influence estimates inside a subset optimizer to jointly maximize individual trajectory utility and complementary set-level coverage.
oXKG319IOO.evidence: Evaluated on RoboMimic and OmniReset in sim-to-sim and real-world robot co-training tasks (including CupCake and Peg, per reviews).
oXKG319IOO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that set-level coverage is a useful addition to simulation curation and that sim-to-real co-training results (such as CupCake) show strong gains over random or full-pool selection.
oXKG319IOO.main_concern: Reviewers criticize unclear presentation and missing upfront definitions of core terms, modest gains over the CUPID baseline, and reliance on a single fixed set of 10 real rollouts.

jvSDtCTRmv.one_liner: Casts multi-query metagradient data attribution as sketched low-rank influence-matrix estimation with separate reconstruction (MAGE) and attribution (SPELL) algorithms.
jvSDtCTRmv.problem: Exact metagradient data attribution methods like MAGIC require a separate full training replay per test prediction, making multi-query attribution prohibitively expensive.
jvSDtCTRmv.method: The authors exploit the linearity of reverse-mode differentiation through training to measure linear combinations of query influences under a fixed replay budget. Because optimal measurements differ for matrix recovery versus attribution, they introduce two sketching algorithms, MAGE and SPELL, built on existing metagradient machinery.
jvSDtCTRmv.key_idea: Shares metagradient replays across queries via sketched linear measurements, separating influence-matrix reconstruction (MAGE) from direct attribution (SPELL).
jvSDtCTRmv.evidence: Theoretical derivation and empirical studies across training scales and budgets (including CIFAR-10, TinyStories, and GPT-2, per reviews).
jvSDtCTRmv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing budgeted multi-query metadifferentiation as sketched influence-matrix estimation and separating reconstruction from attribution is clean and theoretically grounded.
jvSDtCTRmv.main_concern: Reviewers note missing end-to-end wall-clock/FLOP accounting for the extra forward-mode passes and a large attribution-quality drop relative to MAGIC (e.g., LDS 0.335 vs 0.909 on CIFAR-10).

X1fJkTrOAi.one_liner: Adapts Optimal Computing Budget Allocation from simulation optimization to sequentially allocate RL training budgets across candidate reward functions.
X1fJkTrOAi.problem: Evaluating multiple candidate reward functions in RL requires training a separate policy per candidate, creating a severe computational bottleneck.
X1fJkTrOAi.method: Fast Reward Evaluation reframes reward selection as a sequential ranking-and-selection problem under a fixed compute budget. It adapts Optimal Computing Budget Allocation (OCBA) to non-stationary RL training to dynamically allocate policy-training steps across candidate rewards based on performance and uncertainty.
X1fJkTrOAi.key_idea: Adapts Optimal Computing Budget Allocation (OCBA) to dynamically allocate finite RL training compute across candidate reward functions based on performance and uncertainty.
X1fJkTrOAi.evidence: Evaluated on sparse-reward RL benchmarks, automatic reward generation tasks, and LLM reasoning (GSM8K, per reviews).
X1fJkTrOAi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reducing candidate-reward evaluation cost is an important problem and that adapting OCBA from operations research is a sensible formulation.
X1fJkTrOAi.main_concern: Reviewers question the realism of the GSM8K reward candidates, note missing guidance on candidate-set properties (e.g., near-ties or all-poor sets), and find surrogate-variance estimation details underspecified.

DTwbqUfdR9.one_liner: Filters detrimental RL post-training trajectories online using mini-batch gradient agreement without requiring a validation set.
DTwbqUfdR9.problem: Conventional influence-based data valuation requires fixed training and validation sets, making it inapplicable to dynamically generated trajectories in online RL post-training.
DTwbqUfdR9.method: Dynamic Trajectory Valuation (DTV) estimates trajectory utility at the mini-batch level solely from gradient information and filters out detrimental trajectories before updating the policy. It integrates directly into GRPO, DPO, and PPO pipelines with a single filtering-rate hyperparameter.
DTwbqUfdR9.key_idea: Estimates online trajectory utility via mini-batch gradient alignment without validation sets and filters out detrimental trajectories during policy updates.
DTwbqUfdR9.evidence: Evaluated on LLM post-training with online GRPO and offline DPO (including mismatched feedback) plus PPO experiments beyond language models.
DTwbqUfdR9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the validation-free gradient filtering rule is simple, easy to integrate across GRPO, DPO, and PPO, and supported by controlled DPO experiments.
DTwbqUfdR9.main_concern: Reviewers question the untested assumption that batch-mean gradient agreement reflects true utility (risking removal of rare correct signals), note missing rollout-selection baselines (PODS, DAPO), and find general RL evidence narrow.

0g60hSLIgX.one_liner: Studies how fixed post-training updates transfer via merging or distillation onto checkpoints of a second training lineage.
0g60hSLIgX.problem: It remains unclear how a post-training update learned along one training lineage composes with a recipient model at different stages along another lineage.
0g60hSLIgX.method: Using Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 8B, the authors transfer a fixed donor update (from RL or distillation) via weight merging or distillation onto successive checkpoints of a second lineage differing only in random seed. They decompose outcomes into teacher-only versus recipient-only solved problems to analyze capability gain and loss.
0g60hSLIgX.key_idea: Transfers a fixed donor post-training update across a moving recipient lineage and decomposes accuracy changes into teacher-only gains versus recipient-only regressions.
0g60hSLIgX.evidence: Controlled lineage-transfer experiments across Qwen3 models (0.6B–8B) with dose scaling, sign-flip, self-distillation, and teacher-strength controls.
0g60hSLIgX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the experimental controls are thorough and that the teacher-only versus recipient-only problem decomposition clearly illustrates transfer trade-offs.
0g60hSLIgX.main_concern: Reviewers view the core finding as expected and confounded with relative teacher strength, note reliance on a single lineage pair per scale, and see limited practical guidance for post-training pipelines.

1LwSTQTmlu.one_liner: Introduces ConsumerGym with evolving latent user states and RUS-GPO for multi-turn conversational commerce RL.
1LwSTQTmlu.problem: Conversational commerce agents must track user needs that emerge and shift across turns, requiring realistic state-evolving environments and fine-grained credit assignment.
1LwSTQTmlu.method: ConsumerGym separates latent user requirements, revealed oracle states, and agent-maintained states with catalog-grounded tools, decomposed rewards, and replayable snapshots. The authors also propose RUS-GPO, combining failure-aware trajectory resampling, user-state graph and boundary-critic estimation, counterfactual comparisons, and within-turn credit assignment.
1LwSTQTmlu.key_idea: Decouples latent, revealed, and agent user states in an interactive commerce gym and assigns turn-level RL credit via counterfactual replay and failure-aware resampling.
1LwSTQTmlu.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3.5-4B, 9B, and 27B across two internal protocols and three external benchmarks using both PPO and GRPO variants.
1LwSTQTmlu.claimed_gains: Relative to the strongest non-RUS baseline at each scale, the PPO variant improves fixed-context Avg. P@1 by 4.8–5.4 points and ConsumerGym success by 3.3–6.1 percentage points.
1LwSTQTmlu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree ConsumerGym is a strong, realistic environment contribution whose state-tracking design improves training even under plain PPO and transfers to external benchmarks.
1LwSTQTmlu.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the dynamic credit allocator R(E) is underspecified, RUS-GPO comparisons are not compute-matched due to extra counterfactual replay interactions, and environment/benchmark code and provenance lack detail.

M68qFsbXs4.one_liner: Combines an autoregressive component-tree Transformer with a dynamic-programming compiler to enforce exact global molecular count constraints.
M68qFsbXs4.problem: Property-conditioned molecular generators steer outputs toward target compositions and ring counts but cannot guarantee exact satisfaction of multiple global count constraints.
M68qFsbXs4.method: TopoCompile represents molecules as trees of intact ring systems and individual atoms so supported global counts are additive over components. At inference, an autoregressive Transformer scores actions while a dynamic-programming compiler masks actions lacking any target-satisfying completion, supporting arbitrary targets without retraining.
M68qFsbXs4.key_idea: Masks infeasible autoregressive component-tree actions at inference time using a dynamic-programming completion oracle over additive integer count states.
M68qFsbXs4.evidence: Evaluated across four molecular generation benchmarks on Common and Rare four-count target groups plus unconditional generation and ablations.
M68qFsbXs4.claimed_gains: Achieves 100% Exact-valid yield across all four benchmarks for Common and Rare four-count target groups, whereas the strongest baseline per dataset reaches 44.9% or less on Rare targets.
M68qFsbXs4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the compact dynamic-programming completion oracle provides a clean, retraining-free exactness guarantee with strong exact-valid yields.
M68qFsbXs4.main_concern: Reviewers note limited testing on unseen count combinations, missing quantitative comparisons against other hard-constrained generators, unclear baseline conditioning setups (e.g., STGG+), and fixed-vocabulary diversity limits.

lpVNNKTctO.one_liner: Expands human motion VQ-VAE tokenizers by jointly scaling training data with synthetic motion sequences and discrete codebooks.
lpVNNKTctO.problem: Motion capture datasets are dominated by common repetitive actions, restricting VQ-VAE motion vocabularies and hurting generalization to rare or compositional motions.
lpVNNKTctO.method: The authors build a synthetic human motion generation pipeline producing diverse, physically plausible sequences beyond existing MoCap distributions and pair it with a redesigned VQ-VAE tokenizer that scales the discrete codebook. The resulting tokenizer plugs directly into existing text-to-motion frameworks like MotionGPT without text annotations on synthetic data.
lpVNNKTctO.key_idea: Jointly scales a VQ-VAE motion codebook and its training distribution using unlabeled synthetic physically plausible motion sequences.
lpVNNKTctO.evidence: Evaluated on text-to-motion and motion continuation tasks across frameworks such as MotionGPT and T2M-GPT, including HumanML3D and out-of-distribution prompt tests (per abstract and reviews).
lpVNNKTctO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree reframing motion generation around tokenizer vocabulary coverage is a practical perspective and that the tokenizer drops into existing models without architectural changes.
lpVNNKTctO.main_concern: Reviewers note that standard text-motion alignment metrics (R-Precision, MM-Dist) degrade on HumanML3D, question circular evaluator arguments, and critique SLERP-based synthesis and missing video/LLM-motion baselines.

pHdeURRX0J.one_liner: Routes MLLM queries matching target forget identities via text and face verification to a lightweight refusal adapter.
pHdeURRX0J.problem: Parameter-updating multimodal unlearning degrades unrelated model utility, while standalone refusal training fails to consistently recognize target individuals across text and image modalities.
pHdeURRX0J.method: MIRRA decouples identity recognition from refusal generation by combining textual identity matching with single-reference face verification using forget and retain prototypes. Any match activates a lightweight refusal adapter while non-matching queries run directly on the frozen base MLLM.
pHdeURRX0J.key_idea: Uses dual text-matching and prototype-based face verification gates to selectively route target-identity queries to a lightweight LoRA refusal adapter.
pHdeURRX0J.evidence: Evaluated across three MLLMs on MLLMU-Bench and CLEAR with modality-gate and adapter ablations.
pHdeURRX0J.claimed_gains: On MLLMU-Bench, reduces forget-set classification accuracy to 0.42–1.25% while retain-set accuracy drops by at most 1.23 percentage points.
pHdeURRX0J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the modular separation of multimodal identity routing from refusal generation effectively suppresses target responses while preserving retain-set utility.
pHdeURRX0J.main_concern: Reviewers argue MIRRA acts as an inference-time guardrail rather than true weight-level unlearning, receives extra supervision (names and reference faces) unavailable to baselines, and lacks adversarial evasion tests.

07XHuKCnNy.one_liner: Analyzes looped Transformer step overshooting via pathwise curvature and recovers reference utility by scaling down recurrent updates.
07XHuKCnNy.problem: Additional recurrent loops in Looped Transformers can degrade answer support, and it is unclear whether failures stem from bad update directions or overly large step sizes.
07XHuKCnNy.method: The authors interpolate along each proposed recurrent update direction and measure teacher-forced reference utility to separate direction failures from finite-step overshooting. Using local quadratic approximations and integrated curvature variation bounds, they predict full-step utility changes and optimal step scales.
07XHuKCnNy.key_idea: Separates update direction from step size in looped Transformers via pathwise curvature analysis and recovers overshot updates by scaling down step length.
07XHuKCnNy.evidence: Theoretical curvature error bounds and empirical evaluations across two model families and three tasks (nine settings total), including full GSM8K test-set interventions.
07XHuKCnNy.claimed_gains: A fixed quarter step recovers 72.2–83.2% of selected finite-step failures across four settings, and quadratic scale selection improves recovery on the full GSM8K test set in both model families.
07XHuKCnNy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating update direction from step scale via pathwise curvature is an intuitive, well-connected analytical perspective on looped Transformers.
07XHuKCnNy.main_concern: Reviewers note that recovery is measured only under single-step teacher-forced reference utility (requiring ground-truth answers for adaptive scaling) without showing actual autoregressive generation accuracy gains.

n9fk6z9v6N.one_liner: Jointly evolves a shared skill, specialized expert skills, and a task router for LLM agents using five-stage credit-assigned updates.
n9fk6z9v6N.problem: Optimizing a single reusable skill across diverse agent tasks causes cross-task interference where edits helping one task group degrade another.
n9fk6z9v6N.method: EvoMoSkill maintains a shared skill, specialized expert skills, and a router, updating them via five-stage Credit-Assigned Gradient Descent (CreAGD): failure attribution, textual/routing edits, scope-conditioned paired evaluation, history-calibrated validation acceptance, and optimizer memory accumulation.
n9fk6z9v6N.key_idea: Jointly edits skill text, expert creation, and router scope from execution feedback using scope-conditioned paired evaluation and history-calibrated acceptance checks.
n9fk6z9v6N.evidence: Evaluated with five frozen student LLMs across five benchmarks covering interactive environments, QA, spreadsheets, and reusable skills, plus acceptance-check ablations.
n9fk6z9v6N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cross-task interference problem is practical, editing router scope alongside skill text is sensible, and empirical coverage across five models and five benchmarks is broad.
n9fk6z9v6N.main_concern: Reviewers note missing equal-budget comparisons against simpler strong-teacher or dynamic skill-library baselines, bundled design changes without isolating mixture routing, and no direct measurement of conflicting updates.

wDDYKtpcfI.one_liner: Combines a geometric mixture of self-teacher and frozen initial policy with forward Renyi divergence for on-policy self-distillation.
wDDYKtpcfI.problem: In on-policy self-distillation, the moving self-teacher co-evolves with the student, and how target-student probability mismatches translate into updates is poorly controlled.
wDDYKtpcfI.method: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation (SR-OPSD) forms a normalized geometric target interpolating the self-teacher and a frozen initial policy, then minimizes the forward Renyi divergence from this target to the student. The authors derive a conditional variational characterization and exact token-logit gradients for fixed contexts.
wDDYKtpcfI.key_idea: Anchors the moving self-teacher via geometric interpolation with a frozen initial policy and optimizes the student under forward Renyi divergence.
wDDYKtpcfI.evidence: Variational and gradient analysis plus experiments across scientific reasoning, tool use, mathematical reasoning, and code generation over multiple model families and scales.
wDDYKtpcfI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mathematical formulation and gradient derivations are clean, and ablations show that reference anchoring interacts strongly with the choice of divergence.
wDDYKtpcfI.main_concern: Reviewers note that joint hyperparameter ablations are limited to a single task (SciKnowEval Physics), direct comparisons with closely related anchored OPSD methods (e.g., beta-OPSD) are missing, and theory does not explain dynamic stabilization.

rh2e0vPItl.one_liner: Proves asymptotic convergence of Q-learning and smooth Bellman variants using a weighted degree-2p polynomial Lyapunov certificate.
rh2e0vPItl.problem: Classical ODE convergence proofs for Q-learning rely directly on non-differentiable infinity-norm contractions, complicating analysis of preconditioned dynamics and smooth Bellman variants.
rh2e0vPItl.method: The paper transfers infinity-norm contraction to a smooth weighted degree-2p polynomial Lyapunov function induced by a finite 2p-norm, proving global exponential ODE stability and almost-sure convergence under i.i.d. sampling for max, log-sum-exp, and mellowmax operators, plus an invariant error set for non-contractive Boltzmann Q-learning.
rh2e0vPItl.key_idea: Transfers infinity-norm Bellman contraction to a weighted degree-2p polynomial Lyapunov function whose inverse-diagonal weights cancel preconditioning for unified smooth ODE stability proofs.
rh2e0vPItl.evidence: Theoretical ODE stability and stochastic-approximation convergence proofs for tabular Q-learning, LSE, mellowmax, and Boltzmann variants, with simple appendix experiments.
rh2e0vPItl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the explicit inverse-diagonal weighted polynomial Lyapunov certificate clean, elegant, and unifying for tabular Q-learning and its smooth variants.
rh2e0vPItl.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty and significance relative to prior smooth-Lyapunov stochastic approximation analyses (e.g., Chen et al.) since the proof yields no new convergence regimes such as function approximation.
